rows.original: "Well, I..." Meira clears her throat and grinds a foot into the floorboards. "Now all of you are giving me a little stage fright..." Hey, if all of you get too annoying, she can simply imagine that you're her sisters. That should put her right back into the proper frame of mind for this, shouldn't it? "Don't joke about it, [pc.name]! But..." she looks over Ivris, Garth and you and puffs herself up. "But I really should have more confidence in myself, and for good reason too." If it helps, you've gathered two of the most important people in this village in for her little taste test — having their support would be most conducive towards any potential putting down roots here in Hawkethorne. And of course, you'll be behind her every step of the way. "You don't understand, I —" Meira begins, then tries to hide her blush with her hands. "Oh, whatever! Watch if you want to, [pc.name], I'll be sure to give all of you a show to remember!" Now that's the spirit! Meira grabs one of Gwyn's aprons and sweeps past you with a flourish, storming past the bar and into the Frost Hound's kitchen as if she owns the place. Garret's in there, having gathered the day's kitchen scraps into a couple bins when he looks up at all of you. "Oh hey, old man. I got everything together like you wanted me to — these to go to the pigs and chickens as usual? Whoa, what's with the crowd?" Garth sighs. "You really don't want to know, pup. Just... just leave them here, I think your sister needs a little help. Come by later, and then you can pick up the scraps and slops for the animals... if there're any to be had." Garret looks between his father, Ivris, Meira and you, then shrugs and turns his back on what must look like an entire clown show to him. "Suit yourself, old man. I don't think I want to know, so knock yourselves out with whatever it is you're up to." As Garret stomps out of the kitchen and Meira takes up position, you chance a gander at what's actually in the wooden bins. In one, animal scraps in an assortment of bones, fish guts, gristle and more; in the other, cabbage stumps, fruit rinds that couldn't go into baking, and the occasional discarded leafy green from some root vegetable or the other. A feast for the pigs and chickens indeed, but no one else; Meira's got her work cut out for her if she's going to make this into anything palatable, let alone good. But then, that's the point of this entire show, isn't it? Putting together a good meal from scratch is amazing enough, putting together a good meal from kitchen dregs requires magic of either the culinary or transmutative sort. Meira's completely unfazed as after having washed her hands, she reaches down and grabs a handful of miserable-looking vegetable leavings, her dress and other finery notwithstanding. All she's got in front of her is a chopping board, but the pile of mess — that's the only way to describe it — but the way her fingers are moving [pc.isMage |are clearly recognizable as arcane gestures to your trained eyes |are obviously more than simple kneading ] as sparks of excess deep red magic jump from the mess of leftovers and scraps. The changes in-between are... well, largely indescribable as the unsightly pile becomes a lot less so, gaining consistency and shape as Meira wills it to be something other than it is, changing its being at the base level. The gem in Meira's brooch burns brightly as she proceeds with her cooking — it must be her focus — and every now and then she reaches down to grab another handful of kitchen scraps to add to the dish taking form before her. [pc.isMage |You have to remind yourself with all your knowledge of transmutation that Meira's not creating anything out of thin air, but rather just rearranging what's there to her pleasing |You know it's theoretically nothing different from what happens with alchemy, or even whatever the portal did to you, but it's nevertheless quite impressive to watch ]. Even so, it's quite impressive to see as the pile becomes steadily less and less amorphous and turns into... something a lot less unappetizing. There's no whistle of steam, no warm scents of stove and wood to accompany the homey preparation of a good meal, but it has a charm of its own and whatever she's cooking up, it doessmell a lot better than what it came from. Ivris is positively giddy with excitement, while Garth just shakes his head at whatever he's seeing. No matter how much you try to angle yourself to get a good look at what Meira's making, though, she swivels her voluminous finery to block your view of the board. "No peeking, now," she giggles, clearly enjoying herself at your mild expense. "Thanks for being here, but I want it to be special for you, okay? Don't spoil the surprise for yourself — and oh, I'm just about done." With that, Meira snatches a wooden tray from a sideboard, plops her completed masterpiece on it, and slams a lid on the whole ensemble before sweeping past you and out the door. Smiling ruefully, Garth comes up and gives you a pat on the shoulder. "Trust me, kid. It's better that you didn't see how she got from one end to the other, because I did and while I can't argue with how the finished dish looked like I sure have problems with everything that went in-between. It's better for you that way." "I just think it was all amazing!" Ivris says with a laugh. "The Evergreen reputation for transmutation is something — are the both of you on a date? You must be something to have hooked such a sassy young sorceress, [pc.name]!" Sure, you're something all right — they don't call you [pc.title] for nothing. Now, you take it that it's time to play taste testers? Ivris nods and starts marching straight out of the kitchen. "With pleasure!" Back outside in the tavern's main room, Meira's taken up position impatiently by one of the larger tables, hovering over her creation like a dragon over its hoard. You pull out a seat for yourself, followed by Garth and Ivris; Meira herself is all aflutter as she pushes her tray forward, making sure it's the center of attention. "Are you ready to be astounded?" "It smells pretty nice," Ivris says. "Better than anything I whip up on my own, that's for sure! Thanks for letting me observe — I certainly learned a lot!" Garth, on the other hand, has the look of a man who's just come off the battlefield and seen just a little too much for his own good. Something wrong? "Oh no, it was about as much as I expected, knowing the Evergreens," he mumbles. "I actually do want to see how it tastes, especially after witnessing that. But I suppose some of the things we eat up here must sound crazy to other people, right? Like that garum thing the minotaurs put on their food. I've had the honor of seeing how some of it was made, and it's worse than what our young lady there just did. At least the gods have that small mercy on our souls — if the minotaurs don't die from garum, we probably won't from what she's cooked up for us. Probably." Well, Evergreen manor is absolutely packed with Meira's sisters, all of whom appear perfectly healthy... An apron about her waist and a big grin plastered all over her face, Meira bows so deeply and cheekily that she has to stick out her tail for balance amidst all her finery. "For you, [pc.name] — thanks for putting up with my cheekiness just now, I really didn't want to spoil the surprise. I was thinking of you the whole time I was putting all of this together, so you know it's going to be super good. Consider it thanks for taking a girl out, hmm?"
rows.translation: 嗯，我……”梅拉清了清嗓子，把脚在地板上蹭了蹭。“现在你们所有人都在让我有点舞台恐惧症了……” 嘿，如果你们实在太烦人了，她大可以想象你们都是她的姐妹们。这样应该就能让她重新进入适合这次场合的状态了吧？ [pc.name]但是……”她环视着伊夫里斯、加斯以及你，然后挺起胸膛说道，“可是我真的 应该 我对自己更有信心了，而且这是有充分理由的。” 如果这能让你感到安心的话，你已经邀请了这个村庄里两位最重要的人物来参加她的小试吃活动——他们的支持对于她能否在鹰棘镇这里安顿下来，无疑会起到至关重要的作用。 当然，你会在她每一步的路上都陪伴在她身边。 “你并不明白，我——”梅拉开始说道，然后试图用手部遮住自己脸上的红晕。“哦，算了！你想看就看吧。 [pc.name]我一定会给大家带来一场难忘的表演的！” 这才是我想要看到的精神！梅拉抓起格温的一条围裙，大摇大摆地从你们身边走过，冲过吧台，径直走进霜猎犬的厨房，仿佛那地方是她自己的似的。加勒特也在里面，他当时正把当天剩下的厨房垃圾收拾到几个垃圾桶里，突然抬头看到了你们所有人。 哦，嘿，老兄。我按照你的要求把所有东西都准备好了——这些是像往常一样要给猪和鸡吃的吧？哇，怎么这么多人啊？” 加思叹了口气：“你真的不想知道吧，小家伙。就……就把这些东西留在这里吧，我觉得你姐姐可能需要一些帮助。晚点再来，到时候你就可以把剩下的残渣和剩饭喂给动物们……如果还有的话的话。 加勒特看了看他的父亲伊夫里斯、梅拉，又看了看你，然后耸了耸肩，转身不再理会这一幕——在他看来，这简直就是一场滑稽的闹剧。“随你们的便吧，老头。我想我并不想知道，所以你们爱干什么就干什么吧。 当加勒特怒气冲冲地走出厨房，而梅拉也站好了自己的位置时，你忍不住偷瞄了一下那些木箱里到底装了些什么。其中一个箱子里堆满了动物的残渣——有各种各样的骨头、鱼的内脏、软骨等等；另一个箱子里则装着卷心菜的残株、那些不能用来烘焙的水果皮，以及偶尔被丢弃的一些绿叶蔬菜。这些食物对猪和鸡来说确实是一顿美餐，但对其他人来说却毫无价值。如果梅拉想把这些东西加工成可以让人吃下去的东西，甚至做成美味可口的菜肴，那她可就有得忙了。 但这就是整个节目的意义所在，不是吗？从零开始准备一顿美餐已经非常了不起了，而利用厨房里剩下的残渣做出美味佳肴，更是需要烹饪高手部或是拥有神奇魔力的人才才能做到。然而，梅拉却毫不在意——她洗完手部后，不顾自己穿着漂亮的连衣裙，直接伸手部抓了一把看起来毫不可口的蔬菜残渣。她面前只有一块砧板，而那堆残渣 一团糟 — 惟有这样来形容它才合适 — 她手部指移动的那些方式 [pc.isMage |对于训练有素的眼睛来说，这些显然可以被识别为某种神秘的符号或手势。 |显然，这些动作远不止是简单的揉捏而已。 ] 当那些深红色的魔法火花从那些杂乱无章的残余物中迸发出来时，那些随之发生的变化……嗯，基本上是无法用语言描述的。因为那堆原本杂乱无章的东西，在梅拉的意念作用下，逐渐变得有条理、有形状了。它不再是从前的样子，它的本质本身也在发生着变化。 当梅拉开始烹饪时，她胸针上的宝石闪烁着明亮的光芒——这一定是她的幸运象征。她不时会低头拿起一些厨房剩下的食材，加入正在制作中的菜肴中。 [pc.isMage |你必须运用自己所掌握的所有关于转化的知识来提醒自己：梅拉并不是凭空创造什么东西，她只是在重新安排那些已有的元素，使之符合自己的意愿而已。 |你知道，从理论上讲，这与炼金术所产生的效果并没有什么不同，甚至也可以说与那个传送门对你所做的一切类似。但亲眼看到这一过程，还是相当令人印象深刻的。 ]即便如此，看着那一堆食材逐渐变得不再那么杂乱无章，最终变成……某种看起来不那么难吃的东西，还是相当令人印象深刻的。虽然没有蒸汽的呼啸声，也没有炉火和木头散发出的温暖气息，来营造那种在家中准备美食时的温馨氛围，但这一切依然有着它独特的魅力。不管她正在烹饪什么，结果肯定都会很不错。 做它的味道比原来的东西好多了。伊夫里斯兴奋得简直无法抑制，而加思则只是对眼前的一切摇摇头。不过，无论你如何调整姿势试图看清梅拉正在制作什么，她总会转动自己那华丽的鳍状物来挡住你的视线。 现在可不能偷看哦，”她咯咯笑着，显然很享受让你感到好奇的这种感觉。“谢谢你能来，但我真的想让这个时刻对你来说特别一些，好吗？别破坏这个惊喜哦——哦，我差不多快完成了。 说着，梅拉从边柜上抓起一个木盘，把她完成的“杰作”放在盘子上，然后猛地盖上盖子，接着从你身边走过，走出了门。加斯带着一丝无奈的微笑走上前来，拍了拍你的肩膀。 相信我，孩子。你最好没看到她是怎么把那些材料加工成最终成品的，因为我是看到了。虽然我无法否认最终成品的样子，但我对其中所经历的每一个步骤确实有很多疑问。 那样对你来说会更好。” “我只是觉得，这一切 太棒了哈哈，”伊夫里斯笑着说，“‘常青女士’在转化术方面的名声确实不容小觑……你们俩是在约会吗？能吸引到这样一个大胆的年轻女巫，你肯定有特别的魅力吧。 [pc.name]嗯，你确实挺特别的——他们才不会叫你 [pc.title] 白费力气了。现在，你该认为该让别人来当“试吃员”了吧？ 伊夫里斯点了点头，然后径直走出了厨房。“乐意之至！” 回到酒馆的主厅后，梅拉迫不及待地坐在了一张较大的桌子旁，她像一条守护财宝的龙一样，紧紧盯着自己刚刚制作出来的食物。 你为自己拉出一把椅子，随后加斯和伊夫里斯也坐了下来；而梅拉本人则显得格外紧张，她不断地把托盘往前推，确保它成为所有人的焦点。 “你们准备好被震撼了吗？闻起来真香，”伊夫里斯说道，“肯定比我自己做的任何东西都要好！谢谢让我观摩，我真的学到了很多！” 而加思，看起来就像是一个刚从战场上回来的人，目睹了太多令他难以接受的场景。 出什么问题了吗？ “哦不，考虑到‘常青女士’这个团队，结果也在我的预料之中，”他喃喃道，“其实 做 真的很想尝尝它的味道，尤其是在亲眼见证了它的制作过程之后。 那个但是我想，我们在这里吃的一些东西，对其他人来说肯定听起来很奇怪吧？比如那些弥诺陶洛斯加在食物里的调味料。我有幸亲眼看到过它们是如何制作的，其实那些东西比我们那位年轻女士刚才做的还要糟糕。 至少诸神还对我们这些可怜的灵魂怀有一丝怜悯——如果弥诺陶洛斯不会因为那种调味料而死，那么我们吃掉她做的那些东西，大概也不会有什么后果吧……大概吧。 嗯，常青女士庄园里到处都是梅拉的姐妹们，她们看起来全都身体健康。她腰间系着围裙，脸上洋溢着灿烂的笑容，梅拉鞠了一躬，鞠得如此深且俏皮，以至于在穿着这些华丽服饰的情况下，她还得把尾巴伸出来才能保持平衡。“这是给你的。 [pc.name] — 谢谢你刚才容忍了我的冒失，我真的不想破坏这个惊喜。在准备这一切的过程中，我一直在想着你，所以你可以放心，这个惊喜一定会让你满意的。 超级的 很好。那就这么定了，谢谢你带我出去玩，嗯？
rows.raw: " "Well, I..." Meira clears her throat and grinds a foot into the floorboards. "Now all of you are giving me a little stage fright..." Hey, if all of you get too annoying, she can simply imagine that you're her sisters. That should put her right back into the proper frame of mind for this, shouldn't it? "Don't joke about it, [pc.name]! But..." she looks over Ivris, Garth and you and puffs herself up. "But I really should have more confidence in myself, and for good reason too." If it helps, you've gathered two of the most important people in this village in for her little taste test — having their support would be most conducive towards any potential putting down roots here in Hawkethorne. And of course, you'll be behind her every step of the way. "You don't understand, I —" Meira begins, then tries to hide her blush with her hands. "Oh, whatever! Watch if you want to, [pc.name], I'll be sure to give all of you a show to remember!" Now that's the spirit! Meira grabs one of Gwyn's aprons and sweeps past you with a flourish, storming past the bar and into the Frost Hound's kitchen as if she owns the place. Garret's in there, having gathered the day's kitchen scraps into a couple bins when he looks up at all of you. "Oh hey, old man. I got everything together like you wanted me to — these to go to the pigs and chickens as usual? Whoa, what's with the crowd?" Garth sighs. "You really don't want to know, pup. Just... just leave them here, I think your sister needs a little help. Come by later, and then you can pick up the scraps and slops for the animals... if there're any to be had." Garret looks between his father, Ivris, Meira and you, then shrugs and turns his back on what must look like an entire clown show to him. "Suit yourself, old man. I don't think I want to know, so knock yourselves out with whatever it is you're up to." As Garret stomps out of the kitchen and Meira takes up position, you chance a gander at what's actually in the wooden bins. In one, animal scraps in an assortment of bones, fish guts, gristle and more; in the other, cabbage stumps, fruit rinds that couldn't go into baking, and the occasional discarded leafy green from some root vegetable or the other. A feast for the pigs and chickens indeed, but no one else; Meira's got her work cut out for her if she's going to make this into anything palatable, let alone good. But then, that's the point of this entire show, isn't it? Putting together a good meal from scratch is amazing enough, putting together a good meal from kitchen dregs requires magic of either the culinary or transmutative sort. Meira's completely unfazed as after having washed her hands, she reaches down and grabs a handful of miserable-looking vegetable leavings, her dress and other finery notwithstanding. All she's got in front of her is a chopping board, but the pile of mess — that's the only way to describe it — but the way her fingers are moving [pc.isMage |are clearly recognizable as arcane gestures to your trained eyes |are obviously more than simple kneading ] as sparks of excess deep red magic jump from the mess of leftovers and scraps. The changes in-between are... well, largely indescribable as the unsightly pile becomes a lot less so, gaining consistency and shape as Meira wills it to be something other than it is, changing its being at the base level. The gem in Meira's brooch burns brightly as she proceeds with her cooking — it must be her focus — and every now and then she reaches down to grab another handful of kitchen scraps to add to the dish taking form before her. [pc.isMage |You have to remind yourself with all your knowledge of transmutation that Meira's not creating anything out of thin air, but rather just rearranging what's there to her pleasing |You know it's theoretically nothing different from what happens with alchemy, or even whatever the portal did to you, but it's nevertheless quite impressive to watch ]. Even so, it's quite impressive to see as the pile becomes steadily less and less amorphous and turns into... something a lot less unappetizing. There's no whistle of steam, no warm scents of stove and wood to accompany the homey preparation of a good meal, but it has a charm of its own and whatever she's cooking up, it doessmell a lot better than what it came from. Ivris is positively giddy with excitement, while Garth just shakes his head at whatever he's seeing. No matter how much you try to angle yourself to get a good look at what Meira's making, though, she swivels her voluminous finery to block your view of the board. "No peeking, now," she giggles, clearly enjoying herself at your mild expense. "Thanks for being here, but I want it to be special for you, okay? Don't spoil the surprise for yourself — and oh, I'm just about done." With that, Meira snatches a wooden tray from a sideboard, plops her completed masterpiece on it, and slams a lid on the whole ensemble before sweeping past you and out the door. Smiling ruefully, Garth comes up and gives you a pat on the shoulder. "Trust me, kid. It's better that you didn't see how she got from one end to the other, because I did and while I can't argue with how the finished dish looked like I sure have problems with everything that went in-between. It's better for you that way." "I just think it was all amazing!" Ivris says with a laugh. "The Evergreen reputation for transmutation is something — are the both of you on a date? You must be something to have hooked such a sassy young sorceress, [pc.name]!" Sure, you're something all right — they don't call you [pc.title] for nothing. Now, you take it that it's time to play taste testers? Ivris nods and starts marching straight out of the kitchen. "With pleasure!" Back outside in the tavern's main room, Meira's taken up position impatiently by one of the larger tables, hovering over her creation like a dragon over its hoard. You pull out a seat for yourself, followed by Garth and Ivris; Meira herself is all aflutter as she pushes her tray forward, making sure it's the center of attention. "Are you ready to be astounded?" "It smells pretty nice," Ivris says. "Better than anything I whip up on my own, that's for sure! Thanks for letting me observe — I certainly learned a lot!" Garth, on the other hand, has the look of a man who's just come off the battlefield and seen just a little too much for his own good. Something wrong? "Oh no, it was about as much as I expected, knowing the Evergreens," he mumbles. "I actually do want to see how it tastes, especially after witnessing that. But I suppose some of the things we eat up here must sound crazy to other people, right? Like that garum thing the minotaurs put on their food. I've had the honor of seeing how some of it was made, and it's worse than what our young lady there just did. At least the gods have that small mercy on our souls — if the minotaurs don't die from garum, we probably won't from what she's cooked up for us. Probably." Well, Evergreen manor is absolutely packed with Meira's sisters, all of whom appear perfectly healthy... An apron about her waist and a big grin plastered all over her face, Meira bows so deeply and cheekily that she has to stick out her tail for balance amidst all her finery. "For you, [pc.name] — thanks for putting up with my cheekiness just now, I really didn't want to spoil the surprise. I was thinking of you the whole time I was putting all of this together, so you know it's going to be super good. Consider it thanks for taking a girl out, hmm?""

rows.original: Of course you'll be watching her. You're supposed to be on a date together, aren't you? You'll be supporting her all the way... and you're just a little curious as to how her magic works.
rows.translation: 你当然会看着她了。你们不是应该一起约会吗？你会一直支持她的……只是有点好奇她的魔法究竟是如何运作的而已。
rows.raw: "Of course you'll be watching her. You're supposed to be on a date together, aren't you? You'll be supporting her all the way... and you're just a little curious as to how her magic works."

rows.original: "Thanks." Stepping over to you, Meira gives you a hug and a cheeky noogie in the side. "It means a lot when you're willing to trust me like this, [pc.name]." Hey, if you didn't trust her you wouldn't be taking her out on a date, nor would you be vouching for her in front of Garth and Ivris, right? They don't know her and thus have reasonable cause to want to see how the cake's made, as the saying goes... but you're perfectly fine with just letting her do her thing. Even if you hadn't been around the Evergreens as much as you have, you still trust Meira to do things right despite being a saucy little brat. "Right! Well, just wait a little bit, and I'll be out with the greatest dish you've ever tasted, okay?" But of course. You settle in at one of Garth's bigger tables, and eagerly wait away while Garth and Ivris follow Meira into the kitchen. It's about a whole twenty minutes of pensive waiting while Meira gets her act together, punctuated by the occasional excited giggle from Ivris — while there aren't any delightful scents wafting from the kitchen doorway, there certainly is no small amount of noise. At the end of it it all, though, Meira comes out with a large tray, tailed by an Ivris who's just as smug as Meira, and an ashen-faced Garth. "See? That wasn't so bad after all — I had to concentrate a little to get it at the right temperature when I was done, but otherwise it was a snap to get done!" "Ooooh. I certainly learned a lot by being able to observe, that's for sure. Thanks so much!" Ivris says as she slides into a seat to one side of you. Garth, on the other hand, has the look of a man who's just come off the battlefield. Something wrong? "Oh no, it was about as much as I expected, knowing the Evergreens," he mumbles. "I actually do want to see how it tastes, especially after witnessing that." An apron about her waist and a big grin plastered all over her face, Meira bows so deeply and cheekily that she has to stick out her tail for balance amidst all her finery. "For you, [pc.name] — I was thinking of you the whole time I was putting all of this together, so you know it's going to be super good. Consider it thanks for taking a girl out, hmm?"

rows.original: With that, Meira sets the wooden tray down on the table and lifts the cover. [rand |Set in the middle is a gigantic golden jelly ringed with fruit and topped with a cherry — the sweet, delectable scent of honey rises into the air, and the glaze glistens in the gentle light of the Frost Hound. Satisfied that she has your undivided attention, Meira picks up a spoon and smacks the jelly in the side, watching it wobble enticingly before coming to a stop. Sayings like %"do unto others as you would have others do unto you" are all well and good until you run into someone whose tastes differ from your own. While you understand that she's grown up in a house with just her mother and sisters and that's fine for a witch of the woods with her expected eccentricities, things are going to be pretty different if she actually wants to go out amongst people and do things like serve them food. Guess what you're trying to say is, she and her family aren't the world. Meira needs to consider that not everyone may have the same tastes as she and the people she's lived with have, and people have expectations of their restaurant experience going in. Sour sausages are not one of them, not in the Frost Marches at any rate. Meira's ears twitch. "Oh. Oops. I still don't quite get it, but..." [pc.isDK |%"Oops" doesn't begin to cover the atrocity she's made — you need to impress upon her the depths that she's sunk to, because if it weren't Garth, Ivris and you judging her cooking, she wouldn't be getting another chance. If this were for real, a single serious misjudgement — because this isn't really a mistake — could spell doom for a new establishment without any kind of track record |It's not her fault, really — while she's had more experience of the world amongst her sisters save for Senja, it's still been of a rather limited sort ]. The only way to really remedy this is to have her tag along with Senja when she goes out and understand more people in other ways than, um, the shenanigans that she was getting up to before you met her. Long story short, she needs to see things more from other peoples' point of view. "But I can already do that." In ways that she clearly hasn't needed to up till this point in her life. Sighing, you gently elbow both Garth and Ivris. If they'd weigh in, please? Seeing that the both of you haven't been fatally poisoned by Meira's polymorphed meal, Garth sighs and takes the knife and serving fork from Meira to saw off a slice of sausage for himself. The old dog steels himself, chews thoughtfully for several moments, then sucks in his cheeks and washes out his mouth with ale as you've done. He's clearly trying to find something nice to say about what he's tasting right now, but the torturous pause makes it clear that any praise is almost certainly going to wind up sounding trite. "When my wife and I were on campaign down in the heartlands, limes were the only fruit that'd actually keep for any length of time. I remember one time we were hired for an expedition that dragged out for far longer than was expected... by the end of it all, we were putting lime juice on everything we were eating not just because it was the only fruit left, but also to disguise the foul taste of stale hardtack and the like. "This... this is more intense than that, and it brings back all kinds of memories to boot. It might sell somewhere else where peoples' tastes run more towards this kind of stuff, but even if I advertised it as a novelty and stated exactly what it was, I don't think a sausage like this would sell here in Hawkethorne. Sorry about that, little lady. How about you, Mistress Ivris? Got any words of advice for her?" Judging from the look on her face, Meira is well aware of the inevitable, but nevertheless retrieves knife and serving fork from Garth and serves Ivris as well. The elf's reluctance is clear — you've never known her to have any trouble with knowing where anything is despite being blind, but she chases the oversized slice of sausage around her plate several times before accepting her fate and taking a bite. Ivris struggles to swallow, and despite her blindfold the contortions her face goes through are plain for all to see. "Well, I can't deny that you achieved the goal you set out to accomplish, dear. It's a magnificent piece of work when it comes to transmutation. But when it pertains to the culinary arts and understanding your customers..." "I get it," Meira sniffs. She tries to disguise it as a haughty gesture, but she's not getting past you in the state she's in. "I don't think I've anything to add on the culinary side that [pc.name] and Garth haven't already said, so I'll just point out that you don't have anything wrong on the arcane side of things. You're certainly very proficient at transmutation, a school of magic that's potentially very dangerous — or more than most in more insidious ways — but a single skill alone isn't going to be enough to build your own business, or even, say, work as a cook in Garth's kitchen." "I get it. Think of other people, not myself." "Doesn't sound like you do, dear. More resentful than understanding, but I was young once, too. Why don't you take [pc.names] advice and let your sister show you around some people? I'm sure that your sister would enjoy that, too." Senja's the nice sort of girl, of course she would. ] "So... what do we do with the rest of this?" "It was going to go to the pigs and chickens," Garth grunts, pushing the tray aside and slamming the lid back on as if he were trapping some particularly vicious vermin. "Guess it can go straight back to them, they don't care so long as it's food." "I... I guess I'll go clean up." Picking up her failure, Meira undoes her apron and starts plodding back towards the kitchen. Ivris makes to stand and follow the distraught 'nuki, but Garth gently places a hand on the elf's shoulder and pushes her back into her seat. "Don't. She needs a little time to be alone." "You're making it sound like she just took a death in the family, Garth. She... she wasn't that hard hit by what we said, was she?" No, Meira's made of spunkier stuff than that — she'll bounce back just fine after she's had a little while to sort things out in her head. [pc.isMage |Even though Meira's still got some way to go, the fact she's come this far is testament to how well her mother's perfected the art of transmutation, which most other wizards find troublesome, to say the least. A magical chef... it certainly has its novelty, a use of such powerful, difficult and potentially dangerous magic for a purpose that most magicians of that caliber would find distastefully mundane. Maybe it's because Meira's spent so much of her time adjusting bodies, including her own, that she wants to try something delightfully everyday by comparison. You feel a nudge in your side, and turn to find Ivris smiling at you. "Penny for your thoughts, [pc.name]?" Well, you wouldn't have set Meira up like this if you didn't have confidence in her skills. But what about her? From one mage to another — what does she think of the premise of Meira's magical gourmet cooking? "Right back at you! I wouldn't have prodded old Garth into letting me sit in on this if I weren't interested, right? But seriously, though, being a chef... I suppose you could do it all by magic, the girl's certainly proved that to us. Not to the extent of waving a wand and getting bread to appear on the table, or having a fish jump out of the ocean perfectly cooked — like what the girl's just demonstrated, you need something to transmute into another. Somehow, somewhere, there's always a price, and given how much it costs many mages don't find transmuting mundane food and drink the best use of energy." You were just having such thoughts, yes. It's only because Meira has her particular interests in being a chef that she's pursued this avenue of interest. "Great minds think alike! The answer I've always received from those I asked was that there was no point — if you wanted food, you could get some mundanely with a lot less effort, of higher quality, and in far greater quantity to boot." Normally, you'd agree, but Meira has an interest in it, which tips the scales. A gourmet restaurant would never be more than a novelty, but her methods make it viable in a place like Hawkethorne and put such a restaurant within the reach of the kind of people who frequent the village. "So long as she doesn't accidentally poison anyone." Which shouldn't be more of a worry than Ivris accidentally poisoning anyone with her potions, right? A sigh. "You have no idea how terrified I was of that when I was starting out, especially when dealing with reagents I'd never handled before. For some inexplicable reason, most labels and alchemy manuals aren't written for the benefit of blind people." |The difficulty of transmutation aside, you have to consider why stuff like what Meira's doing isn't more widespread. "Well, that's not hard to answer," Ivris replies. "Plenty of wizards who are of that caliber have bigger fish to fry than becoming a chef." Hmm, so there's simply no glamor in it? No recognition amongst one's peers for producing a gourmet meal from a pile of table and kitchen scraps? "That and more. I suppose you could do it all by magic, you certainly could. Not to the extent of waving a wand and getting bread to appear on the table, or having a fish jump out of the ocean perfectly cooked — like what the girl's shown, you need something to transmute into another. Somehow, somewhere, there's always a price, and given how much it costs many mages don't find transmuting mundane food and drink the best use of energy." That makes sense. It's only because Meira has her particular interests in being a chef that she's pursued this avenue of interest. "The real value that our sassy sorceress has in her unique style of cooking isn't making something from nothing, it's being able to make something that can't be put together by any other means, with low-cost material components. When you boil it down, cooking is just alchemy with a particular subset of ingredients, that's all. I'd be surprised, though, if she managed to serve more than two dozen people a night, even given her talent and pedigree. It'd exhaust her and her focus, and pose a risk of accidents... but since she's of the mind of keeping her business small I don't see any problem with that." ] So, Ivris doesn't mind Meira potentially having some sort of gourmet restaurant in Hawkethorne? "It'd be something to put us on the map, to be sure. Draw people from beyond the Marches." She thinks a moment, scratching her antlers. "So long as she perfects her cooking before she starts — this isn't something that you get a second chance at." That, and she figures out that she needs to be catering to her prospective customers' tastes, and not her own or even just her sisters'. "Yes." "Could be worth something, so long as she doesn't accidentally poison anyone, and I'm saying this against my gut feelings on the matter," Garth admits. "We don't actually need to be more famous; being the only village of note between Tychris and the elven kingdom to the north, people come to us anyway. But the girl's a better prospect than some of the people we've taken in have been — she has a plan of where she wants to go and how to get there, which is more than the usual of finding somewhere safe and living day to day while hoping for the best. She'll have to reliably produce good food before she thinks about settling down anywhere, not just here, because screwing up someone's meal is the kind of mistake you rarely get a second chance on." Well, it's a good thing that the both of them haven't given up on Meira because of a mistake. "Oh, don't get me wrong," Garth admits, holding up thumb and forefinger. "It came this close. But since you were willing to put your money where your mouth was when it came to vouching for the Evergreen girl and take the first bite, I'm willing to take the chance on her." "She's an Evergreen, after all, and you being willing to back her up means there's got to be something in her," Ivris adds. "So long as she's willing to learn... even if she doesn't pick Hawkethorne to put down roots, I think she'll do well." Eventually, Meira returns from the kitchen, sans the apron; her eyes dart this way and that, eventually settling on you. "Well, thanks for letting me use your kitchen and taste my food, Mister Garth. And of course you too, Miss Ivris — I'd love to stay and talk some more, but I, uh, suddenly remembered that it's getting quite late and there're still a couple of things I have to help my sisters with at home.""

rows.original: Ivris opens her mouth to reply, but Meira's already caught you by the hand and started tugging you towards the door in the most comical way possible. Whatever Ivris was going to say dissolves into a giggling fit as you allow Meira to lean her whole weight into herding you onto the street with all of her gremlin energy. "Oh," she sighs. "I've —" Never been so embarrassed in all her life? "Yes, that's — hey!" It's quite obvious when she beat such a hasty retreat that it could've come out of one of her sister's trashy romances. "Yeah, and -" Meira's brow furrows even more. "Wait, how do you know Senja has those kinds of books?" An educated guess. Senja strikes you as the kind of girl who'd fancy such things. Meira looks as if she's going to argue, then groans and pushes her face straight into your [pc.chest]. "Oh gods, we really are in one of my sister's daydreams, aren't we? All the way up to me failing to cook in front of a couple of important people?" [pc.isDK |Really? Well, that's mighty specific. Maybe you should've been harder on her so the payoff is greater when she finally manages to piece your tough shell and see the helpful truth that lies beneath your harsh words. "W-wh -" That underneath it all, you really care for her and the brusque put-down of her creation was necessary to get her to understand how much her eventual success means to you. "I -" Meira huffs and pulls away from you, showing you a cute, round, and above all, pouty face as she stares [pc.heightRange 72 |up ]at you, arms akimbo and balled fists in her hips. "You're not one of those creepy dreamwalkers that Mom talks about every now and then, are you?" No, but she does need to ship up and shape out. Garth and Ivris were this close to writing her off for good, and it's only because of you that they relented just enough to give her a second chance. |There, there. It'll be fine — Garth and Ivris didn't write her off, so as long as she takes their advice to heart and keeps on improving, there's still hope. Even if she doesn't choose to settle in Hawkethorne, it's good feedback no matter where she goes. ] Meira's little 'nuki ears turn down at your words, but she nods and leans into you. "I think we ought to go home now, [pc.name]. I'm tired all of a sudden." Perfectly understandable, given today's events. You'll walk her to her door, then. It's a little way out of Hawkethorne, through the woods and over the Wayfort to Evergreen manor, but you're in no particular hurry. Meira clings to you all the way, wrapping both arms about yours as she sticks to you like a particularly persistent slime, fluffy dress and all. By the time you've reached her doorstep, she's gotten the scent of her perfume all over your [pc.armor]; as you step indoors to the usual shuffling and scurrying of her sisters in motion, Meira finally deigns to peel away from you and clears her throat. "Thanks for bringing me out to the village, [pc.name]. I know I didn't make the best of impressions back there, but I'm sure I'll improve with time." The tactful thing here is to say nothing and you do just that, reaching for Meira's little round 'nuki ears and stroking them while they wiggle about. "So, yeah... I know that this was meant to be a date, and we haven't actually done any touchy-feely stuff like what someone might expect out of a date..." Actually, she has. This is exactly like something out of her sister's fantasies, isn't it? Or have you been imagining her being completely clingy all this while after having been shot down by Garth, Ivris and you? "I... well!" Meira huffs and blushes a little. "I just don't want you to feel like you got shortchanged, or that I was using you or something; I've seen firsthand how awful that feels so many times. It's just that — well, Senja was always the one more for hugs and pets with lots of love, that kind of stuff. Like, I don't know, I expected you at some point to take my cheeks in your fingers and start squishing away, apologizing for how harsh you were with me back in the village." ...Is that the kind of thing she fantasizes about? Goodness, if you just wanted to have sex with her you wouldn't have to take her out in the first place, just fuck her right in the manor. What does she take you for? "I didn't mean it that way! I just, well, hmph. Well then, it's good that you enjoyed verbally beating me down! I bet you got a lot out of it, too!" Before you can reply, Meira [pc.heightRange 72 |stands on tiptoe |swoops in ] to give you a quick kiss on the cheek, then runs off into the manor, her 'nuki tail swishing behind her. You consider calling after the little gremlin, but shake your head and smile. She's going to have to be a bit less childish if she's going to be taking this whole moving out on her own thing seriously... but for now, it is quite endearing, isn't it?
rows.translation: 伊夫里斯刚张开嘴想要回答，梅拉就已经抓住了你的手，以一种极其滑稽的方式开始把你往门口拉。无论伊夫里斯原本想说什么，都被你的笑声给淹没了——因为你任由梅拉使出她全部的力量，把你拽到了街上。 哦，”她叹了口气，“我……” 这辈子从来没这么尴尬过吧？ “是啊，就是……嘿！” 当她如此仓促地逃走时，很明显，这件事应该和她姐姐那些低俗的恋爱故事有关。 是啊，还有……”梅拉的眉头皱得更深了。“等等，你怎么会知道森雅会有那种书呢？” 这只是一个合理的猜测。森雅给你的印象就是那种会喜欢这类东西的女孩。 梅拉看起来像是要争辩起来，但随后她叹了口气，把脸紧紧贴在了你的脸上。 [pc.chest]哦，天啊，我们真的 是 在我姐姐的某个幻想中，对吧？甚至想象到我会在一些重要人物面前做饭失败的场景 [pc.isDK |真的吗？嗯，这个要求未免太具体了。也许你当初应该对她更严厉一些，这样当她最终突破你那坚硬的外壳，看到你严厉话语背后隐藏的真诚帮助时，得到的收获才会更大吧。 我、我……” 其实，在这一切的背后，你其实是真的很关心她的。你之所以那样直率地贬低她的作品，就是为了让她明白她的最终成功对你来说意味着什么。 我——”梅拉气呼呼地拉开距离，同时向你展示了一个可爱、圆润的 撅着嘴的 她凝视着对方，表情严肃。 [pc.heightRange 72 |向上 ]她双手叉腰，拳头紧握在臀部，说道：“你应该不是妈妈偶尔会提到的那些令人毛骨悚然的‘梦游者’吧？” 不，但她确实需要赶紧采取行动了。加思和伊夫里斯 这个 他们几乎要彻底放弃她了，但正是因为你，他们才勉强决定再给她一次机会。 |别担心，没关系的。加斯和伊夫里斯并没有放弃她，只要她能认真听取他们的建议并不断努力进步，还是会有希望的。即使她最终没有选择留在鹰棘镇，这些反馈对她来说也是非常有价值的，无论她将来去哪里。 ] 梅拉的小耳朵在你说话时微微下垂，但她还是点了点头，靠向你。“我想我们现在应该回家了。 [pc.name]我突然觉得好累。” 考虑到今天发生的事情，这完全可以理解。那你应该送她到她家门口吧。 从鹰棘镇出来，穿过树林，再经过荒废驿堡，就能到达常青女士庄园了，不过你也不必太着急。 梅拉一路上都紧紧缠着你，双臂紧紧搂住你的腰，就像一只黏人得特别厉害的软体动物一样，尽管她穿着蓬松的裙子。等到你走到她家门口的时候，她身上的香水味已经完全沾满了你。 [pc.armor]当你走进室内，听到她那些姐妹们忙碌的脚步声和喧闹声时，梅拉终于肯从你身边走开，清了清嗓子。 “谢谢你带我来到这个村子。 [pc.name]我知道我在那里给人的印象并不是很好，但我相信随着时间的推移，我会有所改进的。” 在这种情况下，最明智的做法就是什么都不说，而我也确实这么做了——我伸手轻轻抚摸着梅拉那对圆圆的小耳朵，看着它们不停地扭动。 所以，嗯……我知道这本应该是一次约会，但实际上我们并没有做那些人们通常会认为在约会中会发生的事情……” 其实，她已经做了。这一切不正是她姐姐幻想中的情节吗？ 还是说，在被加斯、伊夫里斯和你拒绝之后，你一直以为她会变得过分黏人呢？ “我……嗯！”梅拉有些气喘，脸上也泛起了红晕。“我只是不想让你觉得自己被亏待了，或者觉得我在利用你什么的；我亲眼见过那种感觉有多糟糕，所以才这么想的。 只是……嗯，Senja一直都是那种喜欢拥抱别人、喜欢被人抚摸、总是充满爱心的人。我不知道，我原本以为你迟早会用手捏住我的脸颊，然后轻轻捏捏，为我之前在村子里对你们那么严厉而道歉。……就是这种东西吗？ 她 幻想些什么呢？天啊，如果你只是想和她发生性关系，一开始就根本不需要带她出去，直接在庄园里解决不就行了。她到底把你当成了什么人啊？ “我并不是那个意思！我只是，嗯，哼。那好吧，你能通过言语羞辱我，看来你也挺开心的吧！我敢打赌，你肯定从中得到了很多乐趣吧！” 你还没来得及回答，梅拉就已经 [pc.heightRange 72 |踮起脚来 |突然出现 ] 她快速地在你的脸颊上亲了一下，然后跑进了庄园，她那条“小尾巴”在身后摇来摇去。你考虑着要不要叫住那个小淘气，但最终还是摇了摇头，笑了笑。如果她真的想认真对待这次独自搬出去住的事情，她就得少点孩子气了……不过，现在看来，这也挺可爱的，不是吗？

rows.original: No sooner have you come into Meira's proximity that the half-'nuki girl notices you, her entire body perking up from tail to ears with mischievous energy. There's no time to beat any kind of retreat — despite her voluminous dress, Meira's hitches up her skirts and is right up in your face in the blink of an eye, grinding the balls of her feet into the floor. "Hey, it's you! Was wondering when you'd finally show up — I've hardly been able to sleep just waiting for you!" [pc.dcb |Hay is for horses, but it's nice to see someone excited to see you for a change. You'd say it's nice to see her full of energy, but frankly that's how she always is. What's gotten into her? |Oh, Meira's usually excited, but it's plain to see that she's more excited than usual. Well, at least her excitement is more of an enthusiastic thing and less bratty than how she usually comports herself... which counts as a difference, one supposes. And what has been keeping her up at night of late? |Oh, hey! Like, it's totally great to see her, too! And she was thinking of you all this time? Well, you'd be thinking of her too... if you could think. But that's okay, it's the thought that counts! Or lack thereof, anyway — so, what's up with her? ] "Well, um..." Meira scrunches up her little nose, then decides it's best to get to the point. "So remember how you took me to your Wayfort and showed me around? You know, that date thing that we had? Where I also wanted to see if it was a good place to move in and get away from my [evergreen.dealtWith |sis |mom and sis ]?" You do recall something like that, yes. Although with the attitude she was displaying at the time, you're not sure if she was even serious about wanting to move into the Wayfort. [pc.isDK |Gods, you're not even sure that counted as a date — it's not like you kissed, made out or had sex. She knows what you mean. Date stuff. Meira pouts at that. "H-hey! What do you mean, date stuff? You're starting to sound like my sister, you know — she expects all that touchy-feely kissy-nibbly stuff as a matter of course!" Oh, but that is what people do on dates, right? Meira's so cute when she's mad, her cheeks coloring as she balls her fists. "It's not the point! If you just want to make out, you can make out anywhere! We... we got to know each other better and understand our... um... aspirations! See if we were a good match and all! That's the point of a date — sure, you can make out and whatever, but that's not the thing that makes it so!" You don't remember much of that, either. When she was puttering around your Wayfort she seemed far more interested in her prospects than you. | "What?" Meira pouts. "Of course I was serious! I'm... well, not always serious, but I wouldn't joke about something that important! Like, I have to think about my future — Senja's got hers all laid out, but I don't have that luxury!" See, that's her thing. You can't tell when she's serious or not. Meira's lips set in a thin, straight line. "Well, I think that's [silly |a skill issue |your problem, not mine ]." Well, if she wants to live under your roof, she'll have to work on making her intentions more apparent. And yes, she would absolutely joke about something that important. ] "Anyway!" Meira huffs. "When I left, I said I'd think about moving into your wayfort." She said she needed to consider her options. "And I did! I scoped out a place in Tychris, as well as a nice place over in Old Belhar and Yvennes. Oh, there was also a place in Barania, too. [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja helped me look around and find places, |Some of them came with suitors that Mom was kind of pushy about... ] but at the end of the day, I feel like I'm most comfortable with the parts that I grew up in." Huh. One might have thought a girl like her would be excited at the prospect of putting down roots in a foreign locale. "Don't get me wrong, it was a nice thought. But to be so far removed with my only point of contact being [evergreen.dealtWith |a bunch of people Senja only knows of because she's been trying to make sense of Mom's records |a couple people which Mom knows distantly ]? Yeah, that's not cool. At least I know people around these parts if something goes sideways." Just far away enough to get her sister out of her hair, but not so far away that Senja can't be reached if trouble grows out of hand. "Or anyone I actually know, for that matter. But yes! You get it!" Well, that's all fine and good that she chose you above all the other options. That being said, what's she going to be doing for you? As highly as Meira may think of herself, you're not going to give her room and board for the lofty privilege of housing her under your roof. "Don't worry, I've got that all figured out. [pc.isBaron |I know you're all buddy-buddy with the elves and all, what with being made a baron and getting a bailiff in the bargain, but it looks like they've neglected to send you a court mage. Which is perfectly fine, given that by everything I've heard from [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja |Mom ] your queen doesn't even have one of her own, she's kind of strapped for people right now |I get that you've been collecting stuff from around the Marches to build up that Wayfort of yours — word gets around quickly when you know the kind of people that [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja |Mom ] does. That being said, for all the goods and talent you've put together so far, you haven't found a court mage yet. If you had someone in-house to do it, you wouldn't have had to go looking for a contractor to do your dungeon, for example. As much of a brat as Meira is, she does have a point there. You wouldn't have had to go running around the Marches looking for someone to enchant your dungeon if you'd had someone close at hand to get it done for you. "See? My point exactly.[pc.isMage | Others might be surprised that you didn't choose to do it yourself, but I know from experience that it's easy to overlook your own mistakes when you're reviewing your own work ] ]." All right. So... court mage. Meira grins. "Yeah." At her age. "Are you saying I'm too old for it? You know full well that we're younger than we look. I get the concern, though — you don't want some hidebound old biddy stuck in her ways in a fresh claim like one that you have." But, that's not what you — look, and is she qualified? "I was trained by my mom, so that should answer your question. Come on, remember what I was doing when we first met? I was casually practising the most difficult school of magic to get right, and on strangers to boot." She was fighting people for dick size! "Yeah! Plus, it takes great social skills to walk up to people cold, challenge them like that, and actually get taken up on the challenge!" You sigh. Is this one of those times where she expects you to agree to this scheme because she has the audacity to ask? "No, I expect you to agree because there isn't anyone in all of the Marches with the same mix of magic and energy that I have. Being a court magician isn't all about having the technical proficiency or the book learning, you know. [viv.recruited |Otherwise, you might as well get that witch you have living in her house on legs to do the job for you." That... Meira does make a good point. Viv is certainly far more skilled at just about every form of magic than Meira is, not to mention her specialty, but appointing her to the position of court mage would be disastrous when her first love is her research and experimentation. You need sociability and extroversion in a court mage, someone who doesn't get tired when dealing with a constant stream of people. Someone like Meira, who is energized by it. |You've got to be able to get around and talk to people. You know, politics stuff. The kind of court mage who hides in his or her little room all the time and is just a leech on one's patron — that kind of defeats the purpose, yet everyone seems to wind up hiring that kind all the time. You need a court mage who knows how to dress nicely and have a conversation in a social gathering, not a nerd. Those you can chain up in a cellar somewhere and leave to work without ever seeing another soul for years." That was pretty long. Was that her pitch? "Yeah! I think I'm great for the job! If I can sell the prospect of a challenge for dick length to random people I just met in the forest, I can sell just about anything to anyone!" That's... well, it's a generalization, but as they go it's a pretty accurate one. ] "So!" Meira exclaims, hands on her hips. "I've laid it all out for the both of us — I think your wayfort's a pretty nice place, all things considered. Location, location, location, as Mom would say. Let me move in, and I'll be your court mage, handle all your magical needs while helping you deal with people, too. There're other places, to be sure... but you and your Wayfort are most definitely my first pick, [pc.name]. What do you say, [pc.name]?" Given the energy that Meira's giving off this very moment, you get the feeling that %"I need to think about it" isn't an answer she'll accept. While this is quite sudden — or maybe not, given that she did say that she was considering moving in when you took her out on that date — you're being put on the spot to make a decision now. Well, will you let Meira be your court mage, or not?
rows.translation: 你刚一靠近梅拉，那个穿着半裸装的女孩就注意到了你，她整个人都充满了调皮捣蛋的能量，从尾巴到耳朵都显得活灵活现的。根本来不及逃跑——尽管梅拉穿着宽大的裙子，但她还是迅速撩起裙摆，转眼间就凑到了你的面前，双足部紧紧地踩在地板上。 “嘿，原来是你！我还在想你什么时候才会出现呢……等你的时候，我几乎都睡不着觉呢！ [pc.dcb |干草是给马吃的，不过偶尔看到有人见到你时会那么兴奋，也确实挺让人开心的。你会说看到她充满活力确实很棒，但说实话，她一直都是这样的。她最近到底发生了什么事情呢？ |哦，梅拉通常都很兴奋，但这次她的兴奋程度显然比平时更高。至少，她的这种兴奋表现得更热情一些，也没有她平时那种任性的样子……我想，这也算是一种变化吧。那么，最近是什么事情让她夜不能寐呢？ |哦，嘿！见到她也真是太好了！原来她一直都在想着你们呢？嗯，如果你们能思考的话，也应该会想着她的吧……不过没关系，重要的是这份心意！至少是有所思吧——那么，她现在怎么样了？ ] 嗯，那个……”梅拉皱了皱小鼻子，然后决定直接切入主题。“还记得你带我去你的荒废驿堡，给我介绍那里的情况吗？就是那次约会……当时我也想看看那里是否适合搬去居住，从而远离我之前的生活环境 [evergreen.dealtWith |姐姐 |妈妈和妹妹 ]是的，你确实记得有这样的事情。不过考虑到她当时表现出的态度，你也不确定她是否真的是想搬到荒废驿堡去住。 [pc.isDK |天啊，你们甚至都不确定那算不算约会——又没有接吻、亲热或者发生性关系。她明白你的意思，就是那种约会该有的行为。 梅拉听到这话后撅起了嘴：“喂！你什么意思，约会该有的行为？你说话的方式越来越像我姐姐了，她总是把这些亲亲抱抱、亲密接触当作理所当然的事情！” 哦，原来是这样 是 人们在约会时都会做些什么，对吧？ 梅拉生气的时候真是太可爱了，她握紧拳头的时候，脸颊会变得通红。“其实并不是 要点如果你只是想亲热的话，其实哪里都可以啊！我们……需要更好地了解彼此，弄清楚我们的……嗯……追求和目标，看看我们是否适合彼此才行！ 那就是。 约会的意义就在于……当然，你们可以亲热之类的，但这才是约会的真正意义所在！ 你其实并不记得太多关于那次约会的细节了 那个也不是这样。当她在你的荒废驿堡基地里闲逛的时候，她似乎对自己的前途比对你更感兴趣。 | 什么？”梅拉撅起了嘴，“我当然是认真的！我……嗯，也不是说不是认真的。 总是 说真的，对于这么重要的事情，我可不会开玩笑的！我必须为自己的未来考虑——Senja已经把她的未来规划得一清二楚了，但我可没有这样的条件！ 你看，这就是她的风格。你根本分辨不出她什么时候是认真的，什么时候在开玩笑。 Meira的嘴唇紧抿成一条细长的直线，说道：“嗯，我觉得 [silly |这是技术上的问题。 |这是你的问题，不是我的。 ]嗯，如果她想住在你家里，那就必须想办法让自己的意图更加明确才行。没错，她确实是应该这么做的。 绝对地 拿这么重要的事情开玩笑，真是不可取。 ] 总之！”梅拉气呼呼地说，“我离开的时候说过，会考虑搬到你的基地去住。” 她说自己需要仔细考虑各种选择。 “我确实这么做了！我在提克里斯找了一个地方，还在老贝尔哈尔和伊文尼斯也找到了不错的住所。哦，巴拉尼亚也有一个地方可以考虑。 [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja帮我四处看了看，帮我找到了那些地方。 |其中有些人还带着追求者，妈妈对此显得相当急切…… ] 但归根结底，我觉得自己在那些我成长过程中所处的环境中最为自在。 嗯，人们可能会认为像她这样的女孩应该会对在异国他乡扎根这一想法感到兴奋才对。 “别误会，这个想法本身挺好的。但既然我与家乡的距离如此之远，而我与家乡唯一的联系就是 [evergreen.dealtWith |一些森雅仅通过研究母亲的记录才了解到这些人存在的人。 |妈妈只是略知一二的那么几个人 ]是啊，那样可不太好。至少我知道这一带有些人，如果出了什么问题，还可以求助他们。” 她选择的距离应该足够远，能让她的妹妹远离她的干扰，但同时又不能太远，以至于在遇到麻烦时无法及时得到帮助。 “或者说，任何我真正认识的人都可以求助。总之，你明白我的意思吧！” 嗯，她选择你而不是其他选项，这当然很好。不过，话又说回来，到底为什么会选择你呢？ 她 即将开始做某事 你? 无论梅拉自认为有多了不起，你也不会仅仅因为让她住在你家里这个“崇高”的理由，就愿意为她提供食宿。 “别担心，这些我都考虑周到了。 [pc.isBaron |我知道你们和精灵们关系很好，毕竟你们还被封为男爵，还得到了一位管家帮忙打理事务，但看起来他们似乎忘了派一位宫廷法师来协助你们。不过这也无所谓，因为据我听说的情况来看 [evergreen.dealtWith |塞尼亚 |妈妈 ] 你的女王自己甚至都没有一个，目前她确实有点人手部不足。 |我明白你一直在边境各地收集各种材料，用来打造你的那个“荒废驿堡”……当你了解那些人的性格时，消息自然会传得很快。 [evergreen.dealtWith |塞尼亚 |妈妈 ] 确实如此。不过，尽管你们迄今为止已经投入了大量的资源和人才，却仍然没有找到合适的宫廷法师。如果你们内部有这样的人，就不会需要去找外聘人员来为你们设计地下城了，对吧？ 虽然梅拉有时候表现得像个任性鬼，但她的观点确实有道理。如果身边有能胜任这项工作的人，你们就根本不需要在边境地区四处寻找合适的人选来为你们设计地下城了。 “看到了吧？我说的就是这个意思。[pc.isMage | 其他人可能会惊讶于你没有选择自己动手去做这件事，但以我的经验来说，当你在审查自己的工作时，很容易忽略自己犯下的错误。 ] ]好吧，那么……宫廷法师这个职位吧。” 梅拉笑了：“没错。” 以她的年纪来说…… “你是说我年纪太大，不适合这个职位吗？你明明知道我们看起来比实际年龄要年轻。不过我理解你的顾虑——你肯定不希望一个固执守旧的老太婆来处理像你这样的新案件吧。但是，这并不是你们想要知道的——听着，她真的有这个资格吗？ “是我妈妈教导我练习这些魔法的，所以这个应该可以回答你的问题了。拜托，还记得我们第一次见面时我在做什么吗？我当时正在随便练习那种最难掌握的魔法，而且还是在对陌生人练习呢。她居然在为阴茎的大小与人争论！ “是啊！而且，要想主动找别人理论，那样挑战他们，还能真正让别人接受这个挑战，那可真需要很高的社交技巧啊！” 你叹了口气。难道这次她又是仗着自己有这个胆量，就指望你会同意她的这个主意吗？ 不，我期望你能同意，因为在整个边境地区，没有人拥有我这样的魔法与能量的组合。你知道，成为一名宫廷法师，关键并不在于技术上的精湛或是书本上的知识。 [viv.recruited |否则，你还不如把那个住在你房子里的女巫叫出来，让她来帮你完成这件事。” 那个……梅拉 进行……操作 说得很有道理。薇芙在几乎所有形式的魔法方面都远比梅拉精通，更不用说她的专长了。但如果让她担任宫廷法师，那肯定是一场灾难——毕竟她的热爱在于研究和实验。担任宫廷法师需要具备社交能力和外向的性格，需要一个人能够不厌其烦地与各种各样的人打交道。 而像梅拉这样的人，恰恰会因为这样的工作而感到充满活力。 |你必须能够四处走动，与人们交流。毕竟，涉及政治方面的事务时，更是如此。那种整天躲在自己的小房间里，完全依赖赞助人生活的宫廷法师，其实根本违背了设立这个职位的初衷——但似乎每个人最终都会雇佣这类人。 你需要的是一位懂得如何穿着得体、能够在社交场合中与人交谈的宫廷法师，而不是那种书呆子。那种人完全可以被关在地窖里，几年都不用见任何人，让他们继续工作就是了。 真是长篇大论啊……那就是她的自我介绍吗？ “没错！我觉得自己非常适合这份工作！如果我都能把‘挑战阴茎长度’这种荒谬的想法卖给在森林里刚遇到的陌生人，那我几乎什么都能卖给任何人！嗯，这其实是一种概括，但就目前的情况来看，这种概括还挺准确的。 ] 所以！”梅拉双手部叉腰，激动地喊道，“我已经把一切都考虑周到了——我觉得你的荒废驿堡是个相当不错的地方，毕竟地理位置非常重要，就像妈妈常说的那样。如果我搬过去住，就可以担任你的宫廷法师，满足你所有的魔法需求，同时也会帮你处理与人打交道的事情。当然，还有其他地方可以选择……但对你和你的荒废驿堡来说，我绝对会优先考虑这个选择。 [pc.name]你怎么看？ [pc.name]鉴于梅拉此刻散发出的那种能量，你会觉得“我需要考虑一下”这个回答她是不会接受的。毕竟 是 发生得相当突然——不过，考虑到她的情况，也许也不算太突然吧。 做了 你说过在那个约会时，她在考虑搬过来和你一起住——现在你面临着必须做出决定的时刻了。 那么，你到底要不要让梅拉成为你的宫廷法师呢？
rows.raw: " No sooner have you come into Meira's proximity that the half-'nuki girl notices you, her entire body perking up from tail to ears with mischievous energy. There's no time to beat any kind of retreat — despite her voluminous dress, Meira's hitches up her skirts and is right up in your face in the blink of an eye, grinding the balls of her feet into the floor. "Hey, it's you! Was wondering when you'd finally show up — I've hardly been able to sleep just waiting for you!" [pc.dcb |Hay is for horses, but it's nice to see someone excited to see you for a change. You'd say it's nice to see her full of energy, but frankly that's how she always is. What's gotten into her? |Oh, Meira's usually excited, but it's plain to see that she's more excited than usual. Well, at least her excitement is more of an enthusiastic thing and less bratty than how she usually comports herself... which counts as a difference, one supposes. And what has been keeping her up at night of late? |Oh, hey! Like, it's totally great to see her, too! And she was thinking of you all this time? Well, you'd be thinking of her too... if you could think. But that's okay, it's the thought that counts! Or lack thereof, anyway — so, what's up with her? ] "Well, um..." Meira scrunches up her little nose, then decides it's best to get to the point. "So remember how you took me to your Wayfort and showed me around? You know, that date thing that we had? Where I also wanted to see if it was a good place to move in and get away from my [evergreen.dealtWith |sis |mom and sis ]?" You do recall something like that, yes. Although with the attitude she was displaying at the time, you're not sure if she was even serious about wanting to move into the Wayfort. [pc.isDK |Gods, you're not even sure that counted as a date — it's not like you kissed, made out or had sex. She knows what you mean. Date stuff. Meira pouts at that. "H-hey! What do you mean, date stuff? You're starting to sound like my sister, you know — she expects all that touchy-feely kissy-nibbly stuff as a matter of course!" Oh, but that is what people do on dates, right? Meira's so cute when she's mad, her cheeks coloring as she balls her fists. "It's not the point! If you just want to make out, you can make out anywhere! We... we got to know each other better and understand our... um... aspirations! See if we were a good match and all! That's the point of a date — sure, you can make out and whatever, but that's not the thing that makes it so!" You don't remember much of that, either. When she was puttering around your Wayfort she seemed far more interested in her prospects than you. | "What?" Meira pouts. "Of course I was serious! I'm... well, not always serious, but I wouldn't joke about something that important! Like, I have to think about my future — Senja's got hers all laid out, but I don't have that luxury!" See, that's her thing. You can't tell when she's serious or not. Meira's lips set in a thin, straight line. "Well, I think that's [silly |a skill issue |your problem, not mine ]." Well, if she wants to live under your roof, she'll have to work on making her intentions more apparent. And yes, she would absolutely joke about something that important. ] "Anyway!" Meira huffs. "When I left, I said I'd think about moving into your wayfort." She said she needed to consider her options. "And I did! I scoped out a place in Tychris, as well as a nice place over in Old Belhar and Yvennes. Oh, there was also a place in Barania, too. [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja helped me look around and find places, |Some of them came with suitors that Mom was kind of pushy about... ] but at the end of the day, I feel like I'm most comfortable with the parts that I grew up in." Huh. One might have thought a girl like her would be excited at the prospect of putting down roots in a foreign locale. "Don't get me wrong, it was a nice thought. But to be so far removed with my only point of contact being [evergreen.dealtWith |a bunch of people Senja only knows of because she's been trying to make sense of Mom's records |a couple people which Mom knows distantly ]? Yeah, that's not cool. At least I know people around these parts if something goes sideways." Just far away enough to get her sister out of her hair, but not so far away that Senja can't be reached if trouble grows out of hand. "Or anyone I actually know, for that matter. But yes! You get it!" Well, that's all fine and good that she chose you above all the other options. That being said, what's she going to be doing for you? As highly as Meira may think of herself, you're not going to give her room and board for the lofty privilege of housing her under your roof. "Don't worry, I've got that all figured out. [pc.isBaron |I know you're all buddy-buddy with the elves and all, what with being made a baron and getting a bailiff in the bargain, but it looks like they've neglected to send you a court mage. Which is perfectly fine, given that by everything I've heard from [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja |Mom ] your queen doesn't even have one of her own, she's kind of strapped for people right now |I get that you've been collecting stuff from around the Marches to build up that Wayfort of yours — word gets around quickly when you know the kind of people that [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja |Mom ] does. That being said, for all the goods and talent you've put together so far, you haven't found a court mage yet. If you had someone in-house to do it, you wouldn't have had to go looking for a contractor to do your dungeon, for example. As much of a brat as Meira is, she does have a point there. You wouldn't have had to go running around the Marches looking for someone to enchant your dungeon if you'd had someone close at hand to get it done for you. "See? My point exactly.[pc.isMage | Others might be surprised that you didn't choose to do it yourself, but I know from experience that it's easy to overlook your own mistakes when you're reviewing your own work ] ]." All right. So... court mage. Meira grins. "Yeah." At her age. "Are you saying I'm too old for it? You know full well that we're younger than we look. I get the concern, though — you don't want some hidebound old biddy stuck in her ways in a fresh claim like one that you have." But, that's not what you — look, and is she qualified? "I was trained by my mom, so that should answer your question. Come on, remember what I was doing when we first met? I was casually practising the most difficult school of magic to get right, and on strangers to boot." She was fighting people for dick size! "Yeah! Plus, it takes great social skills to walk up to people cold, challenge them like that, and actually get taken up on the challenge!" You sigh. Is this one of those times where she expects you to agree to this scheme because she has the audacity to ask? "No, I expect you to agree because there isn't anyone in all of the Marches with the same mix of magic and energy that I have. Being a court magician isn't all about having the technical proficiency or the book learning, you know. [viv.recruited |Otherwise, you might as well get that witch you have living in her house on legs to do the job for you." That... Meira does make a good point. Viv is certainly far more skilled at just about every form of magic than Meira is, not to mention her specialty, but appointing her to the position of court mage would be disastrous when her first love is her research and experimentation. You need sociability and extroversion in a court mage, someone who doesn't get tired when dealing with a constant stream of people. Someone like Meira, who is energized by it. |You've got to be able to get around and talk to people. You know, politics stuff. The kind of court mage who hides in his or her little room all the time and is just a leech on one's patron — that kind of defeats the purpose, yet everyone seems to wind up hiring that kind all the time. You need a court mage who knows how to dress nicely and have a conversation in a social gathering, not a nerd. Those you can chain up in a cellar somewhere and leave to work without ever seeing another soul for years." That was pretty long. Was that her pitch? "Yeah! I think I'm great for the job! If I can sell the prospect of a challenge for dick length to random people I just met in the forest, I can sell just about anything to anyone!" That's... well, it's a generalization, but as they go it's a pretty accurate one. ] "So!" Meira exclaims, hands on her hips. "I've laid it all out for the both of us — I think your wayfort's a pretty nice place, all things considered. Location, location, location, as Mom would say. Let me move in, and I'll be your court mage, handle all your magical needs while helping you deal with people, too. There're other places, to be sure... but you and your Wayfort are most definitely my first pick, [pc.name]. What do you say, [pc.name]?" Given the energy that Meira's giving off this very moment, you get the feeling that %"I need to think about it" isn't an answer she'll accept. While this is quite sudden — or maybe not, given that she did say that she was considering moving in when you took her out on that date — you're being put on the spot to make a decision now. Well, will you let Meira be your court mage, or not? "

rows.original: Know what? She does make a pretty good case for herself.
rows.translation: 你知道吗？她确实为自己的观点提供了相当有力的论据。
rows.raw: "Know what? She does make a pretty good case for herself."

rows.original: You don't think she'll be a good fit for the Wayfort. There's such a thing as too much brat energy.
rows.translation: 你不会认为她适合加入荒废驿堡家族吧。那种任性的性格实在太过分了。
rows.raw: "You don't think she'll be a good fit for the Wayfort. There's such a thing as too much brat energy."

rows.original: Well... there is something to Meira's words. You've been on the receiving end of her brattiness before, and it would be fun to be able to weaponize that energy and have her browbeat others with that extroverted energy. Interacting with people recharges Meira, so there's no chance of her wellspring going dry mid-tussle, either. And as for skill, her personality aside, Meira is her mother's daughter. She may be hyper-specialized in what she's interested in, but at the same time that doesn't mean she can't learn on the job. Right? "Hey, if you're asking if I've got somewhere to take lessons, it's not like [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja's |Mom's ] not right by the river. It's certainly a better deal for that kind of thing than if I were to follow [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja's |Mom's ] advice and let myself be shipped all the way down to the heartlands." Hmm. [pc.isMage |Once more, you're schooled in the arcane yourself, so strictly speaking you don't need a court mage. On the other hand, there's the whole thing about delegation and division of labor. That, and Meira has a different perspective on matters — a second opinion is really only useful if it's coming from another angle |The fact that you managed to have the dungeons built shows that you know people more arcanely inclined that Meira is, but it was a hassle to go running around getting them; someone under your roof would be able to respond more quickly and effectively. If nothing else, an immediate response could at least plug the dam until reinforcements arrive, buy you some time ]. Meira's a little lacking in her breadth of knowledge, but so long as she promises to keep up with the arcane side of things one way or another you're willing to overlook that. "Hey! You're not having second thoughts, are you?" No, no, you were just thinking it through. Come on, it's time to go see [evergreen.dealtWith |Senja |her mother ] and let her know of your decision.
rows.translation: 嗯……就这样吧。 是 这些话确实说到梅拉的心坎里去了。你之前也经历过她那任性的表现，如果能把她的这种活力加以利用，让她用这种外向的性格去影响别人，那肯定会很有趣。与人们互动其实能为梅拉带来能量补充，所以在争吵的过程中，她的“能量源泉”也绝对不会枯竭。 至于能力方面，抛开她的性格不谈，梅拉毕竟是她母亲的女儿。她可能在自己感兴趣的领域有着极高的专精度，但这并不意味着她不能在实践中不断学习，对吧？ “嘿，如果你是在问我有没有地方可以去上课的话，其实并没有 [evergreen.dealtWith |塞尼亚的 |妈妈的 ] 不在河边。对于那种事情来说，这样的安排肯定比我直接去那里要好得多。 [evergreen.dealtWith |塞尼亚的 |妈妈的 ] 得到了建议，然后我就被一路送到了内陆地区。” 嗯。 [pc.isMage |再一次，是你自己亲自学习了这些深奥的知识，所以严格来说，你并不 需要 一位宫廷法师。另一方面，还有关于授权与分工的问题。而且，梅拉在看待这些问题时有着不同的视角——只有当另一种观点是从不同的角度出发时，它才会真正具有参考价值。 |你能成功建造这些地下城，这一事实说明你更加了解那些与梅拉一样热衷于深奥事物的人们的需求。 是 四处奔走去获取这些东西实在是一件麻烦事；有一个人就在你身边，肯定能够更快、更有效地解决问题。至少，及时的响应也能暂时解决问题，直到援兵到来，为你争取一些时间。 ]梅拉的知识面确实有点狭窄，但只要她承诺会尽力去了解那些神秘的知识领域，你也就愿意忽略这一点。嘿！ 你不会改变主意了吧？” “不，不是的，你只是在仔细考虑而已。快吧，是时候去看看了。 [evergreen.dealtWith |塞尼亚 |她的母亲 ] 并告诉她你的决定。

rows.original: [evergreen.dealtWith |As it so happens, you find Senja in the dining room with several of her full and half-'nuki sisters, corralling them to the table and staying there. So far, all of them are behaving, but with how airheaded some of the full 'nuki's are you get the feeling that the entire scene is but one misstep away from utter chaos. Poor Senja. You can understand why Meira wants to get away from all this. Senja looks up at the both of you in the midst of serving a squealing, chubby 'nuki some porridge, and gives you a weary smile. "[pc.name]. Meira. So, you've come to a decision, haven't you? There's only one reason you'd be here looking for me at mealtimes." "Sounds like you're less than happy with it, sis." "I can't stop you from doing whatever you please, Meira. But I do have to wonder why I went to all that trouble to get in touch with Mother's friends and explain the situation, let alone send you all the way down to the heartlands, if you were just going to end up going with [pc.name] anyway." "A girl's got to —" "— Keep her options open," Senja finishes, staring at her sister with all the look of a dead fish. "You say that a lot." You look between Senja and Meira — clearly things never have been easy between the sisters, even if they got along under their mother eye, and with Evergreen out of the picture even those restraints have been lifted. However, they aren't willing to squabble in front of you, and Meira takes the time to help her sister serve their more airheaded sisters in sullen silence. Eventually, though, Senja sets down the pot and takes the both of you aside to a corner of the dining room, brushing a sweaty strand of hair away from her brow. "Mom made it look easy, huh?" "It's a lot harder when I'm not willing to do the things she did. Meira, I'm not going to lie: it feels like a whole lot of wasted time getting in touch with the people Mother used to know, if you were just going to go with [pc.name] in the end. I know nothing was promised, but you went and made the trip — it felt like you had a vacation while I struggled with keeping our sisters together, and —" Meira scowls. "Look, sis, if you want to feel like your efforts weren't wasted you can send some of the bimbos down to that Duchess Hargrave you had me visit. She and her men have the means to care for a whole bunch of toys, I can assure you." "It doesn't feel right to —" "Trying to do magic, deal with the people who come by, and wrangle our frankly idiotic sisters is killing you, sis. The half-and-halfs like us are teachable, but the airheads Mom was planning on body-hopping into? They've been wiped clean and are never going to be useful for anything. You have to face it, sis — you have to let them go sometime." "Maybe," Senja mumbles. "But not now." Look, while this family drama is fascinating, you're presumably here to make sure Senja is properly informed that Meira's going to be moving into your Wayfort as your court mage. Senja eyes you wearily. "How long ago was it that she popped the question?" Just outside in the entrance foyer, in fact. "Of course. She does know how to convince people." She doesn't think it's a good idea? "For you? It's fine. Meira has plenty of energy to deal with people, which as I understand is the 'court' part of being a court mage. As for the 'mage' part... well, she's very, very good at transmutation. I can't speak for the other schools of magic, though if she's going to be living at your place then it's just a trip by the river if she wants to get at Mom's old books and other things." Or if she wants to help out around the mansion. "I..." Senja's eyes shift from her pouting sister, to you, then back to Meira, whose pout has only grown. "Actually, I would appreciate it if you could make that part of her duties. She'd get more done around the place than she usually does. Ever since what happened to Mother... happened, I've had to shoulder more responsibility. Maybe going off with you will do the same for her, although I wouldn't put money on such a faint hope." "Sis!" "Just... go. I know I can't keep you here, and any actual work I try to have you do winds up being a slapdash job at best. Maybe you'll finally be of use to someone when your heart is in it. Just don't make too much trouble for [pc.name], please." It'll be fine, you can keep Meira in hand. If anything happens, she's living but a stone's throw away, so it's not like you won't be able to send Meira over if there's an emergency. All that said, though, you ought to be clear: you have Senja's permission to take her sister from under her roof? Senja laughs at that, and there's genuine humor in the gesture. "I don't think you need permission from me for that, [pc.name]. If Meira thinks she needs permission from me to do anything... well, maybe Mother made more of an impression on her than what meets the eye." All right, you'll rephrase: she's aware that you're here to take Meira away into your employ? "Yes, I am. I know I've been rather sour throughout all this, but... hopefully she'll have a better life out there than in some mansion in the woods, fancy as it is. She likes people, so maybe being around plenty of them will do her some good, especially if she meets several who have neither obligations to Mother, nor compunctions about slapping her down." |As it so happens, the two of you find Evergreen in her sitting room being waited on hand and foot by her other daughters. She doesn't obviously have anything to occupy her at the moment, though, and if anything appears to have been expecting your arrival, sitting upright while taking drags from a Jassiran-style hookah. "Have we been keeping you long, Mom?" "Not really, my dear." Evergreen's eyes flit between the both of you. "It wasn't so long ago that I realized [pc.name] was heading this way. While it wasn't certain that [pc.heShe] would be charmed by what you had on offer, I chose to rouse myself just in case. And by the looks of it, I'm not wrong. "I'm not angry, dear Meira, but your mother's just a little sad at all the extra work that went into pulling strings just for you went up in smoke. Then there were those trips you took down to Yvennes and the like... even all the way to Valgarde to meet my old friends." "It wasn't all for pleasure, Mom. A girl's got to keep her options open." "Yes, yes; you like saying that so much. I really wonder if you really enjoyed your time at Duchess Hargrave's residence as much as you said you did. Oh well, that's water under the bridge now." Evergreen takes a long drag from her hookah, but is perfectly content to leave the both of you standing before her couch. "So, you're sure about going off with [pc.name]? While I'm a little disappointed that you didn't go with my more favored choices, I'm sure one of your sisters will gladly fill your shoes in that regard. Besides, I can see the merits of your case." "Yes, Mom. I'm going to go off with [pc.name]." "Now, there's no need to use that tone with me, young lady. I'm not even opposing your choice, just making sure that you aren't making a decision with no take-backs over the simple desire to be a contrarian." Smiling, Evergreen turns to you. "I'm sorry you had to see that. Little family discussion — Meira's always been a wilful one, and her talents would be wasted if I tried to keep her indoors being all domestic like her sisters. If she becomes too much of a handful while in your service, don't hesitate to... ah, offer her some much needed correction for her sassiness. Don't worry, she likes it." [meira.fucked |Oh, you know that full well from first-hand experience. You'll have absolutely no compunctions about taking Meira in hand if she starts acting like a brat |You get the feeling that Evergreen isn't referring to a lecture, or a stint in the stocks ]. So, you have her blessing to take Meira into your employ? "It would get her out of my hair; she's been quite mopey hanging around the house and given how she perks up whenever you visit maybe this is for the best. I used to make her do busywork, what with playing that little game she did with those she met in the forest, but as events have progressed that's not really a tenable solution anymore for a handful of a daughter." Evergreen chuckles. "Oh, don't look like that, Meira. It still taught you valuable lessons and kept you out of trouble. "Now, [pc.name]... being Meira's mother, I've been her keeper for a while, and she's going to be passing from under my roof to yours. Were she any other of my daughters, I'd tell you to take care of her, but Meira's the kind who makes sure she's well taken care of and raises a stink if you lapse in that regard." And does she think that Meira's ready to be someone's court mage? "I wouldn't be letting her go if I didn't think so, would I?" Evergreen chuckles. "I like you, [pc.name], and I'd rather my daughter be useful to you than be a drag. The girl's extremely good at transmutation — I think she has the potential to surpass me, given the chance. As for the other schools of magic... well, I'll be waiting here in order to give her remedial lessons if she needs them." Meira looks confused for a moment, then her eyes light up in realization and she huffs. "Mom! You weren't sending me down to the heartlands to be —" "— The duchess' court mage, no. At least, not as a primary occupation, although you'd probably have filled that role anyway. But why bring it up at this point? You're going with [pc.name], anyway." You clear your throat, drawing the attention of both mother and daughter. Anyway... you have permission to take Meira with you, then? Evergreen smiles, shrugs, and takes a deep draw from her hookah. "This very moment, if you so pleased. Practically speaking, though, I know the poor dear can't live without some of her comforts, so it'll take a day or two for her to pack her things up in preparation for leaving her mother's house. I'm sure the two of you can work things out between each other. Now, if you don't mind... I have to consider deeply just how I'm going to fill Meira's place once she's gone. Since one of my daughters has turned into a bratty delinquent, I guess there's no choice but for me to make another and try again. Maybe I'll have more luck the next time around, hmm?" ]
rows.translation: [evergreen.dealtWith |巧的是，你在餐厅里看到了Senja，她正把她的几个完全长大的姐妹以及那些还没长完全大的姐妹们召集到桌子旁，让她们待在那里。目前，她们所有人都在守规矩，但考虑到那些已经完全长大的姐妹中有些实在太笨拙了，你总觉得这一整个场面随时都有可能陷入彻底的混乱之中。 可怜的Senja……你也能理解为什么Meira想要摆脱这一切吧。 当Senja正在给那个哭闹着、胖乎乎的小家伙喂粥时，她抬起头看着你们俩，露出一个疲惫的笑容。[pc.name]梅拉，所以你终于做出了决定，对吧？在用餐时间来找我，肯定只有一个原因。” “听起来你对此并不满意啊，姐妹。” “我无法阻止你做任何你想做的事，梅拉。但我确实很好奇——既然你最终还是会选择那样做，那我当初为什么还要费那么大劲去联系母亲的那些朋友，向他们解释整个情况，甚至还要专程把你送到这片内陆地区来呢？ [pc.name] 不管怎样。” “一个女孩总得——” “——保留自己的选择余地，”森雅说完，用一种毫无生气的目轻型盯着妹妹。“你经常这么说。” 你看看森雅和梅拉——显然，这对姐妹之间的关系从来都不轻松。即使在母亲的眼里她们相处得不错，但自从常青女士离开后，那些束缚也消失了。 然而，她们并不愿意在你面前争吵，于是梅拉便花时间帮助她的妹妹，默默地、阴沉地伺候着那些更愚蠢的姐妹们。最终，塞尼亚还是放下了锅，把你们俩带到餐厅的角落里，一边把额头上的一缕汗珠拨开，一边说道。 妈妈把这件事说得好像很简单似的，对吧？” “但当我不愿意去做她曾经做过那些事情的时候，其实会困难得多。梅拉，我不想骗你：去联系妈妈以前认识那些人，真的感觉是在浪费很多时间，如果你们只是打算 [pc.name] 最终，我知道并没有什么承诺，但你还是去了那里——对我来说，那简直就像是一次度假，而我在努力维持我们姐妹们的关系……” 梅拉皱起了眉头：“听着，姐，如果你想让自己觉得自己的努力没有白费，你可以让那些花枝招展的女孩们去见你让我去的那个哈格雷夫公爵夫人吧。 我可以向你保证，她和她的手下完全有能力照顾好那一大堆玩具。” “但是这样做总觉得有点不太对……” “试图耍些小聪明，来应付那些来访的人 以及 姐，整天应付我们这些简直愚蠢至极的姐妹们，真的快把你累死了吧。像我们这样的还算有点可教之处，但妈妈原本打算让那些白痴们也参与进来吗？那些人根本就无可救药，永远也派不上任何用场。你得面对现实吧，姐——总得找个机会放他们走吧。 也许吧，”森雅低声说道，“但现在还不是时候。” 听着，虽然这种家庭纠纷确实很有趣，但你们来这里的目的应该是确保森雅清楚地知道：梅拉将会成为你们的宫廷法师，搬来和你们一起住在荒废驿堡吧。 森雅疲倦地望着你：“她到底是在什么时候提出这个请求的？ 实际上，就在入口大厅的外面。 “当然。她确实很擅长说服别人。” 她不觉得这是个好主意吗？ “对你来说？没问题。梅拉有足够的精力去应付这些人，据我所知，这正是宫廷法师职责中‘处理人际关系’这一部分的内容啊。 至于“法师”这个身份……嗯，她在变形术方面确实非常非常擅长。不过对于其他魔法流派，我就不太清楚了。不过既然她要住在你家，那么如果她想翻看妈妈以前的书籍或其他东西，只需要去河边走一趟就行了。" 或者，如果她愿意帮忙打理宅邸里的事务的话。 “我……”森雅的目轻型从撅着嘴的妹妹身上移开，看向你，然后又回到梅拉身上，而梅拉的撅嘴动作似乎变得更加明显了。“其实，如果你们能把这项任务安排成她的职责之一，我会很感激的。这样她就能比平时更多地帮忙打理宅邸了。自从母亲出了那件事之后……我就不得不承担更多的责任。也许和她一起去旅行也会对她产生同样的效果，不过我也不敢对这种可能性抱太大希望。 姐！” “你走吧……我知道我无法把你留在这里，而且让我让你做的任何事情，最终都只会弄得一团糟。也许只有当你全身心投入的时候，你才会真正对别人有所帮助。只是别惹太多麻烦 [pc.name]请吧。” “没关系的，你可以让梅拉待在你身边。如果发生什么事情，她住的地方离这里很近，所以遇到紧急情况时，你完全可以立刻把梅拉叫过来。不过，你还是应该弄清楚一点：你确实得到了森雅的允许，才能带她妹妹去她家吗？” 森雅听到这个问题，笑了起来，她的笑声中充满了真诚的幽默感：“我觉得你不需要我的允许才能这么做吧。 [pc.name]如果梅拉认为她做任何事情都需要我的许可……那么，也许母亲在她心中留下的影响比表面上看起来要大。” 好吧，你可以这样重新表达：她知道你在这里，打算把梅拉带走，让她为你工作吧？
