rows.raw: " [evergreen.dealtWith |As it so happens, you find Senja in the dining room with several of her full and half-'nuki sisters, corralling them to the table and staying there. So far, all of them are behaving, but with how airheaded some of the full 'nuki's are you get the feeling that the entire scene is but one misstep away from utter chaos. Poor Senja. You can understand why Meira wants to get away from all this. Senja looks up at the both of you in the midst of serving a squealing, chubby 'nuki some porridge, and gives you a weary smile. "[pc.name]. Meira. So, you've come to a decision, haven't you? There's only one reason you'd be here looking for me at mealtimes." "Sounds like you're less than happy with it, sis." "I can't stop you from doing whatever you please, Meira. But I do have to wonder why I went to all that trouble to get in touch with Mother's friends and explain the situation, let alone send you all the way down to the heartlands, if you were just going to end up going with [pc.name] anyway." "A girl's got to —" "— Keep her options open," Senja finishes, staring at her sister with all the look of a dead fish. "You say that a lot." You look between Senja and Meira — clearly things never have been easy between the sisters, even if they got along under their mother eye, and with Evergreen out of the picture even those restraints have been lifted. However, they aren't willing to squabble in front of you, and Meira takes the time to help her sister serve their more airheaded sisters in sullen silence. Eventually, though, Senja sets down the pot and takes the both of you aside to a corner of the dining room, brushing a sweaty strand of hair away from her brow. "Mom made it look easy, huh?" "It's a lot harder when I'm not willing to do the things she did. Meira, I'm not going to lie: it feels like a whole lot of wasted time getting in touch with the people Mother used to know, if you were just going to go with [pc.name] in the end. I know nothing was promised, but you went and made the trip — it felt like you had a vacation while I struggled with keeping our sisters together, and —" Meira scowls. "Look, sis, if you want to feel like your efforts weren't wasted you can send some of the bimbos down to that Duchess Hargrave you had me visit. She and her men have the means to care for a whole bunch of toys, I can assure you." "It doesn't feel right to —" "Trying to do magic, deal with the people who come by, and wrangle our frankly idiotic sisters is killing you, sis. The half-and-halfs like us are teachable, but the airheads Mom was planning on body-hopping into? They've been wiped clean and are never going to be useful for anything. You have to face it, sis — you have to let them go sometime." "Maybe," Senja mumbles. "But not now." Look, while this family drama is fascinating, you're presumably here to make sure Senja is properly informed that Meira's going to be moving into your Wayfort as your court mage. Senja eyes you wearily. "How long ago was it that she popped the question?" Just outside in the entrance foyer, in fact. "Of course. She does know how to convince people." She doesn't think it's a good idea? "For you? It's fine. Meira has plenty of energy to deal with people, which as I understand is the 'court' part of being a court mage. As for the 'mage' part... well, she's very, very good at transmutation. I can't speak for the other schools of magic, though if she's going to be living at your place then it's just a trip by the river if she wants to get at Mom's old books and other things." Or if she wants to help out around the mansion. "I..." Senja's eyes shift from her pouting sister, to you, then back to Meira, whose pout has only grown. "Actually, I would appreciate it if you could make that part of her duties. She'd get more done around the place than she usually does. Ever since what happened to Mother... happened, I've had to shoulder more responsibility. Maybe going off with you will do the same for her, although I wouldn't put money on such a faint hope." "Sis!" "Just... go. I know I can't keep you here, and any actual work I try to have you do winds up being a slapdash job at best. Maybe you'll finally be of use to someone when your heart is in it. Just don't make too much trouble for [pc.name], please." It'll be fine, you can keep Meira in hand. If anything happens, she's living but a stone's throw away, so it's not like you won't be able to send Meira over if there's an emergency. All that said, though, you ought to be clear: you have Senja's permission to take her sister from under her roof? Senja laughs at that, and there's genuine humor in the gesture. "I don't think you need permission from me for that, [pc.name]. If Meira thinks she needs permission from me to do anything... well, maybe Mother made more of an impression on her than what meets the eye." All right, you'll rephrase: she's aware that you're here to take Meira away into your employ? "Yes, I am. I know I've been rather sour throughout all this, but... hopefully she'll have a better life out there than in some mansion in the woods, fancy as it is. She likes people, so maybe being around plenty of them will do her some good, especially if she meets several who have neither obligations to Mother, nor compunctions about slapping her down." |As it so happens, the two of you find Evergreen in her sitting room being waited on hand and foot by her other daughters. She doesn't obviously have anything to occupy her at the moment, though, and if anything appears to have been expecting your arrival, sitting upright while taking drags from a Jassiran-style hookah. "Have we been keeping you long, Mom?" "Not really, my dear." Evergreen's eyes flit between the both of you. "It wasn't so long ago that I realized [pc.name] was heading this way. While it wasn't certain that [pc.heShe] would be charmed by what you had on offer, I chose to rouse myself just in case. And by the looks of it, I'm not wrong. "I'm not angry, dear Meira, but your mother's just a little sad at all the extra work that went into pulling strings just for you went up in smoke. Then there were those trips you took down to Yvennes and the like... even all the way to Valgarde to meet my old friends." "It wasn't all for pleasure, Mom. A girl's got to keep her options open." "Yes, yes; you like saying that so much. I really wonder if you really enjoyed your time at Duchess Hargrave's residence as much as you said you did. Oh well, that's water under the bridge now." Evergreen takes a long drag from her hookah, but is perfectly content to leave the both of you standing before her couch. "So, you're sure about going off with [pc.name]? While I'm a little disappointed that you didn't go with my more favored choices, I'm sure one of your sisters will gladly fill your shoes in that regard. Besides, I can see the merits of your case." "Yes, Mom. I'm going to go off with [pc.name]." "Now, there's no need to use that tone with me, young lady. I'm not even opposing your choice, just making sure that you aren't making a decision with no take-backs over the simple desire to be a contrarian." Smiling, Evergreen turns to you. "I'm sorry you had to see that. Little family discussion — Meira's always been a wilful one, and her talents would be wasted if I tried to keep her indoors being all domestic like her sisters. If she becomes too much of a handful while in your service, don't hesitate to... ah, offer her some much needed correction for her sassiness. Don't worry, she likes it." [meira.fucked |Oh, you know that full well from first-hand experience. You'll have absolutely no compunctions about taking Meira in hand if she starts acting like a brat |You get the feeling that Evergreen isn't referring to a lecture, or a stint in the stocks ]. So, you have her blessing to take Meira into your employ? "It would get her out of my hair; she's been quite mopey hanging around the house and given how she perks up whenever you visit maybe this is for the best. I used to make her do busywork, what with playing that little game she did with those she met in the forest, but as events have progressed that's not really a tenable solution anymore for a handful of a daughter." Evergreen chuckles. "Oh, don't look like that, Meira. It still taught you valuable lessons and kept you out of trouble. "Now, [pc.name]... being Meira's mother, I've been her keeper for a while, and she's going to be passing from under my roof to yours. Were she any other of my daughters, I'd tell you to take care of her, but Meira's the kind who makes sure she's well taken care of and raises a stink if you lapse in that regard." And does she think that Meira's ready to be someone's court mage? "I wouldn't be letting her go if I didn't think so, would I?" Evergreen chuckles. "I like you, [pc.name], and I'd rather my daughter be useful to you than be a drag. The girl's extremely good at transmutation — I think she has the potential to surpass me, given the chance. As for the other schools of magic... well, I'll be waiting here in order to give her remedial lessons if she needs them." Meira looks confused for a moment, then her eyes light up in realization and she huffs. "Mom! You weren't sending me down to the heartlands to be —" "— The duchess' court mage, no. At least, not as a primary occupation, although you'd probably have filled that role anyway. But why bring it up at this point? You're going with [pc.name], anyway." You clear your throat, drawing the attention of both mother and daughter. Anyway... you have permission to take Meira with you, then? Evergreen smiles, shrugs, and takes a deep draw from her hookah. "This very moment, if you so pleased. Practically speaking, though, I know the poor dear can't live without some of her comforts, so it'll take a day or two for her to pack her things up in preparation for leaving her mother's house. I'm sure the two of you can work things out between each other. Now, if you don't mind... I have to consider deeply just how I'm going to fill Meira's place once she's gone. Since one of my daughters has turned into a bratty delinquent, I guess there's no choice but for me to make another and try again. Maybe I'll have more luck the next time around, hmm?" ] "

rows.original: [evergreen.dealtWith |"Well, I never!" Meira huffs as she leads you through the manor's hallways. "I thought she might get cranky, but I really didn't expect her to explode just like that." She must have really wound up Senja, you don't remember her ever being as crabby as she was. "Hey! Why is it my fault?" Because you've known her for long enough to be comfortable in making that assumption, unless she's absolutely affirming that it's not her fault? "Hmph!" You thought as much. Does Senja really object so much to her looking around for options? "She says I should make a decision and stick to it instead of being so wishy-washy. That, and every option I don't take is wasted energy that could be better spent on something else." Hmm. For someone as beleaguered as Senja is in her role as the new Evergreen, you can see where she's coming from, but... well, it doesn't matter any more. Meira gives you a thin smile, then punches you lightly in the side. "No, it doesn't. First it was Mom, and then it was Senja. I'm getting out of this house, she isn't going to be the boss of me anymore." No. You are. "Yeah, but you're more fun on the whole, so I don't mind you being my boss." You'll take a rain check on whether that's supposed to be a good thing or not. So, when's she going to make the jump? Meira crosses her arms and thinks. "Well, it'll take me a day or two to sort through my stuff and pack it all up in preparation for moving to your place, [pc.name]. I can't sleep well in anything but my bed, so that'll have to go with me, there're the things I'll need to do my job, and there's a bunch of stuff that has sentimental value to me. "You don't have to worry about it, I'll handle it all by myself. Next time you see me, it'll be under your roof, as snug as a bug in a rug." And she'll announce herself, no doubt? "Oh, I think you'll know all right. Again... thanks for agreeing to this, [pc.name]. I mean it — those friends of Mother's that Senja dug up were nice enough, but there was something about each and every one of them that creeped me out. Best to send my airheaded sisters to them as toys in my place, right? That way, you get the benefit of having me around. "Now if you don't mind, I'll be going to get myself sorted. Be seeing you soon, okay? But not until then." Now that's the Meira you know — the idea that anything or anyone might not go her way is absolutely inconceivable to her. Without waiting for your reply, she [pc.heightRange 68 |stands on tiptoe |leans in ] to give you a kiss, then hitches up her skirts and scurries off. "Well, that went better than I expected. I was pretty sure Mom would raise a fuss, but she was pretty calm about everything. Hey, while you're not as familiar with Evergreen as any of the other candidates she wanted to foist Meira off to, you've been more useful to her in that shorter time. That has to count for something. rows.original:
"W-what?" Meira huffs. "You're saying no?"
    
    That's right, you're saying no. While you don't doubt Meira's skill with magic and her energy, you suspect that living with her under your roof is bound to get exhausting in short order. It's best to nip something like this in the bud and decline her outright instead of having to handle it down the line — maybe she should find someplace and someone more suited to handling her temperament.
    
    "Sheesh, fine. No means no, you don't need to go into some long-winded grand[pc.mf
        |p
        |m
    ]a explanation that's more for yourself than for me. It's your loss, I'll just have to look into that cute place in Tychris with a little more effort now, that's all. See, this is why a girl needs to keep her options open; imagine if I'd put all my eggs in one basket."
    
    Now, to be sure, this doesn't mean you dislike her or anything —
    
    "Yeah, yeah, you took me on a date and all, I get it. It's not as if I'll be disappearing from my [evergreen.dealtWith
        |sister's
        |mom's
    ] mansion tomorrow just because you said no." Meira waves you off. "If you still want to come and have some fun or get something done, I'm all for it. [evergreen.dealtWith
        |Helps me pass the days now that Mom's keeping me at home more
        |It's a nice break from having to help Senja wrangle all these airheads
    ].
    
    "Well, I guess that's that. Do you want something from me, or are you expecting me to get all huffy and skulk away?"

rows.original: All right, you've come pretty far into the heart of the cold bog that dominates the southeastern Frostwood — if there were ever boreal elf mines in this area for extracting bog iron, they ought to be around here. It's hard not to feel a little silly just walking in circles aimlessly and leaving your progress to fate, [flags.NINA_PSI |but Nina's shown herself to possess a measure of genuine power. Now whether that power extends to divination and clairvoyance is another matter, but it's something for you to have a start on trusting these visions of hers |but if nothing else an empty search will mean you'll be able to ignore Nina's ramblings from here on out ]. As events shape up, though, you don't have to search long; the lightning-blasted tree Nina described stands out in a clearing all of its own, a towering lump of charred ash rising from the bog. So far, so good... all right, north from here it is, then. It's but a short jaunt through the trees, but you'd never have found it without Nina's directions; several patches of dangerously soft mud suck at your feet as you leave the beaten trail, and you take care to stick to the sparser trees in this region of the Frostwood, trusting their roots to make for more solid footing. But eventually, foliage and undergrowth alike part, and you're faced with a large patch of gravel at the foot of a cut-away portion of a hill. The ground is firmer here, and weeds poke out from amidst the pebbles; the signs of civilization lie strewn about you here and there, albeit centuries old. What support beams you can see as the entrance tunnel leads off into the darkness are surprisingly well-preserved for the time they must've spent in neglect, but if anyone's going to be building things to last it's going to be the pale elves with their long lifespans. There aren't any tools or the like — no doubt rusted to dust in the bog's atmosphere by this point — but you see the foundations of a couple of ruined longhouses, stone and hardwood still clinging on to existence where the less durable materials have since long rotted away. All right, that's the second time that crazy bird got it right. Still doesn't prove anything beyond doubt, though. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn kiyoko azyrran agnimitra viviane atugia quintillus |"Ooooooo," Cait says, hopping up to the entrance and peering into the darkness. "A spooky mine. Think there're ghosts in there?" If the dead haunt the mine, at least that's something that Nina didn't warn you about. "Hey, [pc.name]..." What? "Ever consider that you're taking this way too seriously? Like, you're taking this vision thing as some kind of personal affront. I don't know that much magic and have never actually given any thought to fate, the future, and the ability to foretell either, but maybe we should just see what happens and enjoy the ride? That seems a lot more fun to me than getting worked up about this vision business. I don't know, [pc.name], just relax, okay? I can help you with being so wound up, if you'd like." That won't be necessary right here and now, but the thought is appreciated. It's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. But she's right, you're giving this far too much thought than it deserves. Let the chips fall where they may, as it were... |"Hey, [pc.name]," Brint says, coming up and clapping you on the shoulder. "Bothered by something?" Why, does it show? "Yeah. A lot, in fact. Everything's turned out just fine on this little adventure so far, so why're you so glum about it?" You're not glum. It's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. If she's right about the tree and the mine, which admittedly are relatively mundane, what else about her ramblings might she be right about? "Possibly everything. Possibly nothing." Brint scratches his brow, and shrugs. "I was never one for the great minotaur philosophers, I was more of an arena kid myself. But it makes sense to not worry so much about what you can't change. I'm personally more worried about there being bad gases in that hole over there; many a good minotaur's been lost in a shaft because he didn't realize he was breathing the wrong stuff until it was too late. I know that'd probably disprove your bird's visions if you keeled over and [party.som | |I |we ] had to rush you out, but that's a bit too far, I don't think." You sigh. Brint's right... there's no point in getting all worked up; you'll need a cool head on your shoulders if there's going to be danger ahead. And let's face it, by just telling you how to get to this place, Nina's already had a hand in making her own prophecy come true and tainted her own veracity. |"Hey, [pc.name]," Brienne says, coming up and clapping you on the shoulder. "Bothered by something?" Why, does it show? "Yeah. A lot, in fact. Everything's turned out just fine on this little adventure so far, so why're you so glum about it?" You're not glum. It's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. If she's right about the tree and the mine, which admittedly are relatively mundane, what else about her ramblings might she be right about? But it makes sense to not worry so much about what you can't change. I'm personally more worried about there being bad gases in that hole over there; many a good minotaur's been lost in a shaft because he didn't realize he was breathing the wrong stuff until it was too late. I know that'd probably disprove your bird's visions if you keeled over and [party.som | |I |we ] had to rush you out, but that's a bit too far, I don't think." H-hey, you never said anything about that. A smile. "I'm sorry. I just, well, worry about you sometimes; you can get really passionate without realizing it. I just don't want you to take unnecessary risks because you got mad. You're the leader here, after all." Well, you're not mad, and you're sorry for making her worry. Brienne leans down for a little kiss, and that tells you all you need to know. |Arona peers suspiciously down the entry shaft and into the gloom. "This just isn't right, I tell you." What isn't? "A mine. Kervus don't dig for metal of any sort, that a job for other people to do and then they give it to us." Sure, you can understand that, but it's not like you're handing out shovels and pickaxes with the intent of digging. Gods, you don't even know if what Nina wants you to get from this place is metallic at all — but if it is, then the elves will have dug it up in times long past and she'll get to carry it off. Does that satisfy her raider's sensibilities? Arona mulls it over. "I guess. Not as great when you're taking it from dead people as opposed to live ones, but it'll do." |Ryn's ears turn down as she peers down the entrance shaft and into the gloom. "Oh. I've never been in one of these..." Well, given that she's hardly been outside of the Winter City before all this started, she likely wouldn't have visited these old elven mines for herself. "Before great-grandmother made the decision to change to sluicing, convicts were sent to work in these mines. Digging into what solid ground the bog has to offer... the more fortunate ones at least worked the easy deposits in open-air mines. These, though... they were called a cruel necessity by the people of the time. They used golems as much as possible, constructs that didn't need to breathe and wouldn't be troubled by the bog gases, but oftentimes you need someone in there... "No one who was sent to the mines expected to serve out their sentence; it was an open secret that it was the death penalty in all but name." Oh. any chance that you'll be meeting embittered elven spirits while inside? "I... don't know. It's possible. But what I'd be more worried about is bog gas having built up in the place over the years — these tunnels haven't been properly ventilated in a long, long time. We should be fine, so long as we aren't going too deep — we aren't going deep, are we?" No, Nina was quite explicit about her directions. Ryn breathes a sigh of relief. "Then we should be fine. Just... be careful." |Kiyoko looks the mine's entrance up and down, then at the ruined buildings off to the side. Finally, she shakes her head. "Ah, a mausoleum. A house of the dead." That's not what this is. It's a mine. "I know what I said, Beloved. There really is no difference here. Can it not be both? Or perhaps I should be more precise in saying that this is a charnel house?" Well... even if you're no Tiran, you can feel the residual misery and death pouring out of the mine in spades. While Nina didn't say that you'd be meeting any spirits on your way in, you wouldn't be surprised if it happened anyway. "Oh, let us not argue and get this over with. I think we can both agree that this is a most unpleasant place." |"Hmm." Azyrran appears contemplative as she takes in the mine's entrance, then extends a hand and tests the air with her fingers. "Warm." After the miseries of the cold bog, that might be welcome. "Maybe, but it might get uncomfortably so deeper inside. There's a reason that we vesperans make sure to set up good air circulation in any hive, not just to prevent it from getting too warm, but also to prevent bad air from building up. Honestly, that's what I'd be more concerned about — it's far more likely the heat's coming from all the things rotting about us, as opposed to the earth itself." Well, she'll warn you if things get too bad, right? According to Nina's so-called vision, you're not going to need to get very far in. "I'll try. I'm not actually any more affected by that sort of thing than you'd be — Drones are the ones who're actually sensitive to this, since they're the ones responsible for the building and maintenance of any hive. Nevertheless, if you catch me getting woozy or dozing off on my feet, snap me out of it and we can beat a hasty retreat. Same goes for me to you, everyone gets that way if you can't breathe properly. Now, shall we begin?" |"You don't see these around that much anymore," Agni says, looking around contemplatively at the architecture. "Deep digging, that is. I... I have the distinct memory that this used to be a lot more common and it wasn't just a select few people like the minotaurs who still delve into the earth. It's all sluicing and open-air mines these days, amongst other things." That would make sense. Various places were hit to varying degrees by the Godswar, and sinking mines like these need considerable engineering and geological knowledge that would've been lost in that kind of conflict. With these elven mines, they'd have been a special case in that they were deliberately abandoned. "Yes, there's that, but... I can't quite place my finger on what exactly's irking me about all this. Never mind, it probably doesn't matter. Shall we?" |"Hmm. A vessel like these would have held good enchantments," Viviane murmurs, stepping up to what's left of an old, crumbling golem and reaching through the vines that cover it to test its surface. "One assumes that they'd have been used for brute labor, but..." But? "To hear your elven companion to speak of it, one of the primary dangers of sinking mines into the bog was the buildup of swamp gas. Using automatons to perform as many tasks as possible, including perhaps even the more cerebral ones... I'd love to be able to study the enchantments that animated these things and what their directives were." And she can tell all this just by examining an ancient, worn-down golem? Viv smiles. "Don't get me wrong, [pc.name] — all that's left here is a withered, dried-up husk of the construct that this used to be. But you can tell something about a liquid from the container intended to hold it, hmm? Now, be careful: if any of these are still wandering around down there, they might be a bother. I don't doubt they could be bespelled to be aggressive, in case there were threats to the mine, a convict tried to escape, or something." |"Hey, look at these!" While you've been busy peering into the gloom that permeates the mine's entrance, Atugia's wandered off and found the vine-covered remnants of a heavy stone golem sitting by a ruined longhouse. "The runes on this thing, they remind me of my own!" You hurry over to her, and indeed, there's enough left of the crumbling elven construct to make out runic indentations on its chest, stomach and arms, patterns that're similar, but not identical to those that crawl over Atugia's skin. Instead of replacing a gem focus, though, they appear to be supplementary to one, a hollow where the golem's heart ought to be in the middle of a web of runic sigils spidering away from that core. "Guess those elves were pretty smart to have the same idea, weren't they?" It is pretty fascinating. You wouldn't want to run into any of these powered up, though. Those fists on this thing look like sledge — no, one of them actually is a sledgehammer. "You're worrying too much. Come on, let's go!" |"This place is downright depressing," Quin mutters as he cranes his head into the mine's entrance and stares into the darkness. "I'd say it reeks of death, but it just plain reeks of so many other things that death alone isn't cutting it." You take a few sniffs, and make a face. Ugh, yeah, it stinks. "Given that it hasn't been ventilated for what must be years, I'd wager it does more than just stink." Quin grimaces. "Hey, [pc.name]... if you feel faint at any time while we're down there, don't hesitate to call uncle, okay? I don't want you suffocating or anything." Same could be said for him, in that case. "I'm not that much of a hard-headed smartass. Even I have my limits. But you... you're reacting really badly to that bird and all the stuff she said, like you've got some personal stake in proving her wrong." It's not a personal stake, it's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. If she's right about the tree and the mine, which admittedly are relatively mundane, what else about her ramblings might she be right about? "Possibly everything. Possibly nothing." Quin shrugs. "Way I see it, it doesn't make sense to make problems for yourself; life's already enough of a struggle without you tripping over your own feet; it makes sense to not worry so much about what you can't change. I'm personally more worried about there being bad gases in that hole over there; I think that's what I'm smelling, even if it's really faint. I know that'd probably disprove your bird's visions if you keeled over and [party.som | |I |we ] had to rush you out, but that's a bit too far, I don't think. Damn it, [pc.name], I may not wear my heart on my sleeve, but I'd hate to lose someone who gave a shit about me, and I think you'd, too." You sigh. Quin's right... there's no point in getting all worked up; you'll need a cool head on your shoulders if there's going to be danger ahead. And let's face it, by just telling you how to get to this place, Nina's already had a hand in making her own prophecy come true and tainted her own veracity. "Hey, it's a nice change from running around after that bald fucker and his demonness for once," Quin says, clapping you on the shoulder. "And it'd be interesting to actually come across a so-called prophet or clairvoyant who isn't spouting complete nonsense, too. Let's go in and see what we find, yeah?" ] Despite the entrance beckoning you forward, you take your time in examining the remnants of the mine's infrastructure; from what you can tell, what remains about the entrance is still relatively sturdy. The beams are dry but still hold well enough, and you won't be in any danger of a collapse here, at the very least. No, it'll be deeper in when stability becomes a problem, that's what you remember Nina saying... ...In any case, you can enter now if you like.
rows.translation: 好吧，你已经深入到了这片遍布在弗罗斯特伍德东南部的寒冷沼泽地的心脏地带了——如果这个地区真的存在用于开采沼铁的极北精灵矿场，那么它们应该就在这个附近吧。就这样漫无目的地绕圈子走，把自己的行进方向完全交给运气，实在让人觉得有点傻吧。 [flags.NINA_PSI |但是尼娜已经证明了自己拥有一定程度的真正力量。这种力量是否也包括预知能力和洞察力，那就另当别论了，不过至少你可以开始相信她所看到的那些景象了。 |但至少，如果搜索结果为空，那么从现在开始，你就可以忽略尼娜那些冗长的唠叨了。 ]然而，当各种事件逐渐明朗化时，你根本不需要费力寻找——尼娜描述过的那棵被闪电击中的树，在一片空地上格外显眼，那棵高耸的焦木堆从沼泽中突兀地耸立着。到目前为止，一切都很顺利……那么，接下来就该往北走了。 虽然这只是穿过树林的一段短途路程，但如果没有尼娜的指引，你永远也找不到这条路。当你离开那条被人踩出的小路时，有几处柔软得危险的泥泞会吸附住你的足部，因此你不得不小心地沿着 霜林 这一带较为稀疏的树木行走，依靠这些树木的根系来获得更稳固的支撑。 但最终，所有的植被和灌木丛都会被清除，你会看到在山坡被切开的地方下方，有一大片碎石。这里的地面更加坚实，杂草从鹅卵石中钻了出来；文明留下的痕迹零星地散布在周围，尽管这些痕迹已经存在了几个世纪。 当你看到入口隧道通向黑暗之处时，那些支撑梁的保存状况出人意料地好——考虑到它们肯定经历了漫长的无人照料时光，这种保存程度已经相当难得了。不过，如果说有什么种族能够建造出经久耐用的东西，那肯定就是寿命漫长的苍白精灵了。 这里没有任何工具之类的东西——毫无疑问，这些工具在沼泽的潮湿环境中早已锈蚀成尘了——但你可以看到几座废弃的长屋的基架，石头和硬木仍然坚守着，而那些较不耐久的材料早已腐烂掉了。 好吧，这是那只“疯狂的鸟”第二次做对了。不过，这也仍然不能确凿地证明什么。 [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn kiyoko azyrran agnimitra viviane atugia quintillus |哦哦哦哦哦，”凯特说着，跳到入口处，往黑暗中张望。“一个阴森森的矿井……我觉得里面可能有鬼吧？” 如果真的有鬼魂出没在这个矿井里，那么至少这也不是妮娜事先提醒过你的。 “嘿， [pc.name]……” “什么？” “你有没有想过，你把这件事看得太严肃了？你把这种预知能力当成了一种个人侮辱。我对魔法了解不多，也从未真正思考过命运、未来以及预知的能力这些事情，但也许我们应该顺其自然，看看会发生什么，然后享受这个过程吧？在我看来，这样比为这种预知的事情而烦恼有趣多了。 [pc.name]放松点，好吗？如果你愿意，我可以帮你缓解这种紧张情绪。” “现在来说，这可能并没有必要，但你的好意我还是很感激的。只是……Nina总有办法用一种极其自信的语气说出一些最离谱的事情，即使那些事情其实是真实的，也会让人感到非常尴尬。真的。 尤其是 如果它们真的是真实存在的的话。不过她说得对，你把这件事想得太复杂了，其实没必要这样。就顺其自然吧…… |嘿， [pc.name]怎么了？”布林特走上前来，拍了拍你的肩膀问道，“是不是遇到了什么麻烦？” “啊，难道看得出来吗？” “是啊，确实看得出来。不过这次小小的冒险到目前为止一切都很顺利，那你为什么看起来这么沮丧呢？” 你并不是沮丧，只是……只是尼娜有时候会说一些极其离谱的事情，而且她说得如此自信，以至于即使那些事情其实是真的，也会让人感到非常尴尬。不，其实并不是这样 尤其是 如果那些事情真的存在的话……如果她关于那棵树和那座矿的猜测是正确的——而事实上，这些事物确实相当普通、平凡——那么，她那些其他的胡言乱语，又有哪些可能是正确的呢？ “也许全部都是正确的。也许什么都不是。布林特挠了挠眉头，耸了耸肩说道：“我从来就不是那种热衷于研究弥诺陶洛斯哲学的人，我自己更喜欢在竞技场里拼搏。不过，确实没有必要过分担心那些自己无法改变的事情。我个人更担心的是，那边那个洞里可能含有有害气体——很多优秀的弥诺陶洛斯就是因为没有意识到自己正在吸入有害物质，等到发现时就已经为时已晚了。 我知道，如果你倒下的话，那很可能会证明你的那些预感是错误的。 [party.som | |我 |我们 ] 我本来想催你快点离开的，但那样做未免有些太过分了，我觉得。” 你叹了口气。布林特说得对……大动肝火根本没有任何意义；如果前方真的有危险，你还需要保持冷静的头脑。说实话，仅仅通过告诉你如何来到这个地方，尼娜就已经在某种程度上帮助自己的预言成真了，同时也让自己的话失去了真实性。 |嘿， [pc.name]布蕾妮说道，走上前来拍了拍你的肩膀，‘是不是有什么烦心事？’” “怎么会呢，有吗？” “嗯，其实有很多。不过这次小小的冒险到目前为止一切都很顺利，那你为什么看起来这么沮丧呢？” “我并没有沮丧……只是……尼娜有时候会说一些非常离奇的事情，而且她说得那么自信，以至于即使那些事情其实是真的，也会让人感到很不自在。 尤其是 如果那些东西真的是存在的话……如果她关于那棵树和那座矿的猜测是正确的——而事实上，这些事物确实相当普通、平凡——那么，她那些其他的胡言乱语，又有哪些可能是正确的呢？ “也许全部都是正确的。也许什么都不是。布蕾妮挠了挠眉头，耸了耸肩：“我从来就不是那种热衷于研究弥诺陶洛斯哲学的人，我自己更喜欢在竞技场里拼搏。不过，确实没有必要为那些无法改变的事情过分担忧。我个人更担心的是，那边那个洞里会不会有有害气体——很多优秀的弥诺陶洛斯就是因为没有意识到自己正在吸入有害物质，等到发现时就已经为时已晚了。 我知道，如果你倒下的话，那很可能会证明你的那些预感是错误的。 [party.som | |我 |我们 ] 我本来想尽快让你离开的，但那样做似乎有点过分了，我觉得。” “嘿，你之前可从来没提过这件事啊。” 他笑了笑：“对不起。我只是有时候会担心你；你有时候会变得非常激动，甚至自己都没有意识到这一点。 我只是不希望你因为生气就去冒不必要的风险。毕竟，你才是这里的领导者。 嗯，你现在并没有生气，而且也为让她担心而感到抱歉。 布蕾妮俯下身子给了你一个轻吻，这个举动已经说明了一切。 |阿罗娜怀疑地朝入口处望去，那里一片昏暗。“我觉得有点不对劲，真的。” “哪里不对劲呢？” “这根本不是矿井。凯尔维斯族从不挖掘任何金属，这种工作本来就是应该让别人来做，然后他们才会把成果分给我们。” 嗯，你这么说也有道理，但总不至于你们真的分发铁锹和镐头，打算亲自去挖掘吧……天啊，你们甚至都没有这么做啊。 知道 如果妮娜希望你从这个地方得到的东西确实是金属制品的话——那么精灵们早在很久以前就应该已经把它们挖出来了，现在她就可以把它们带走了。这样，是否能够满足她作为一个“掠夺者”的心理需求呢？ 阿罗娜仔细考虑了一下，说道：“我想应该是可以的。虽然从死人那里获取这些东西并不像从活人那里获取那样令人满意，但至少也还算可以吧。 |瑞恩低下头，透过入口的通道望向那片昏暗之中，她的耳朵微微耷了下来。“哦……我从来没进过这样的地方……” 嗯，考虑到在这一切发生之前，她几乎从未离开过冬城，她很可能自己也不会去这些古老的精灵矿井里。 在曾祖母决定改用冲刷开采方法之前，囚犯们都被派来在这些矿场工作。他们需要在沼泽地中挖掘那些坚实的地面……至少那些运气较好的人可以在露天矿场里开采那些较容易开采的矿层。 不过，当时的人们将这些称为“残酷的必要手段”。他们尽可能多地使用魔像——这些不需要呼吸、也不会受到沼泽气体的影响的机械生物，但很多时候，还是需要有人亲自进入其中去操作它们。被送到矿井里的人，没有人期望自己能真正完成刑期；事实上，这几乎等同于死刑，只是没有明说而已。” 哦……在矿井里，有没有可能遇到那些心怀怨恨的精灵灵魂呢？ 我……也不确定。有可能吧。但我更担心的是，这些隧道多年来可能积累了沼气——它们已经很久没有得到适当的通风了。只要我们不要挖得太深，应该就不会有问题 不是吧 我们要深入进去吗？” “不，尼娜已经把她的要求说得很清楚了。” 瑞恩松了一口气：“那我们应该就没问题了。只是……要小心点。 |清子上下打量着矿井的入口，又看了看旁边那些被毁坏的建筑物，最终摇了摇头。“啊，原来是一座陵墓……一座供死者安息的地方。” 但这里根本不是陵墓，而是一座矿井。 我知道我说了什么，亲爱的。这里确实没有任何区别。难道不能两者兼而有之吗？或者，或许我应该更准确地说，这里其实是一处停尸房？” 嗯……即使你不是提兰人，也能感受到从这座矿井中散发出来的那种深深的痛苦与死亡的气息。 虽然妮娜没有说过在进入这个地方的过程中会遇到什么鬼魂，但就算真的遇到了，你也不会感到惊讶。 “哦，咱们别争论了，赶紧把这件事解决掉吧。我想我们都会同意，这个地方确实非常糟糕。" |嗯。”阿兹兰若有所思地望着矿井的入口，然后伸出手，用手指触了触空气。“暖和。” 在经历了寒冷沼泽地的折磨之后，这样的温度未免太令人感到欣慰了。 也许吧，但情况可能会变得非常糟糕。我们这些‘晚星族’之所以会确保在任何蜂巢中都保持良好的空气流通，不仅仅是为了防止温度过高，也是为了防止污浊的空气在蜂巢中积聚。 说实话，这才是我更担心的地方——更有可能的是，这些热量其实是来自我们周围正在腐烂的各种物质，而不是地球本身。 嗯，如果情况变得太糟糕，她总会提醒你的，对吧？ 根据尼娜所谓的“预知”，你其实不需要深入太远。 “我会试试的。其实我并不会像你那样受到那种东西的影响——真正对此敏感的是无人机，因为它们负责建造和维护整个蜂巢。 不过，要是你们发现我开始头晕或者站在那里打瞌睡，就立刻叫醒我，这样我们就可以赶紧撤退了。反过来也一样，如果大家呼吸不畅，也会出现这种情况的。那么，我们现在开始吧？ |现在这种景象已经不多见了，”阿格尼沉思地环顾四周的建筑说道，“那种深入地下的挖掘活动……我清楚地记得，过去这种做法曾经非常普遍，而不仅仅是像弥诺陶洛斯那样的少数人会从事这种工作。 这些天来，到处都是这样的滑坡和露天矿场。 这也确实说得通。在“神战”中，许多地区都受到了不同程度的破坏，而修复这些沉陷的矿场需要大量的工程技术和地质知识，而在那样的冲突中，这些知识很可能已经丢失了。 有了这些精灵矿场，它们本应该属于一个特殊的案例——因为这些矿场是被人故意废弃的。 “是的，确实有这个因素，但是……我实在想不明白，究竟是什么让我对这一切感到不满。算了，也许这真的没什么大不了的。 我们走吧？ |嗯，这样的容器应该会用来存放一些强大的魔法道具吧，”薇薇安轻声说道，她走到那个已经破败不堪的古老魔像残骸旁，伸手穿过覆盖在它上面的藤蔓，仔细检查其表面。“一般来说，这类容器应该是被用来从事重体力劳动的，不过……但是？” “听你的精灵同伴说，将矿井沉入沼泽地所带来的主要危险之一，就是沼泽气体的积聚。使用自动机器来完成尽可能多的任务，甚至包括那些需要较高智慧的任务，也是个有效的解决办法。我真的很想研究一下那些让这些物体动起来的魔法机制，以及它们具体的运作指令。” 那么，她仅仅通过观察一个古老而破旧的魔像，就能了解到这一切吗？ 薇芙笑了。 别误会， [pc.name] — 现在这里只剩下这个原本存在的物质的干枯外壳罢了。不过，从用来盛放这种液体的容器中，我们还是能了解到一些关于这种液体的信息，对吧？现在，要小心了：如果这些液体还残留在下面，它们可能会带来麻烦。我毫不怀疑，如果矿井面临威胁，或者有囚犯试图逃跑之类的情况，这些液体很可能会被施加魔法而变得具有攻击性。 |嘿，看看这些！”当你一直忙于凝视矿井入口处弥漫的黑暗时，阿图吉娅却走开了，她在一座废弃的长屋旁发现了那些被藤蔓覆盖的、残破的巨石傀儡的残骸。“这些东西上面的符文，让我想起了我自己的符文！你急忙走向她，果然，那座正在崩解的精灵建筑残骸上，还能清晰地看到胸膛、腹部和手臂上刻着的符文痕迹。这些图案与覆盖在阿图吉娅皮肤上的那些图案相似，但又不完全相同。 然而，这些结构似乎并不是用来替代宝石聚焦点的，而是对其起到补充作用——在那些从核心部位向外延伸的符文图案之中，有一个凹陷处，那里本该是魔像的心脏所在。 “看来那些精灵也挺聪明的，他们也想到了同样的办法，不是吗？这确实非常有趣。不过，你肯定不想碰到这些被强化了的生物。这家伙手上的那些拳头看起来就像重锤一样——不，实际上其中一只确实如此。 是 你担心得太多了。来吧，我们出发吧！ |这个地方简直让人感到压抑极了，”奎因一边说着，一边把头伸进矿井的入口，凝视着黑暗。“我本来想说这里弥漫着死亡的气息，但实际上，这里散发出的味道太多了，单是死亡的气息根本无法形容这一切。” 你闻了了几下，顿时做出了一个皱眉的表情。呃，确实，这里的味道很难闻。 “考虑到这个矿井肯定已经有好几年没有进行通风了，我敢打赌，这里散发出来的不仅仅是难闻的气味。”奎因皱着眉头说道，“嘿 [pc.name]……如果我们在下面的时候你感到头晕或者不舒服，一定要立刻叫我，好吗？我可不想你窒息或者发生什么意外。” 在这种情况下，对他来说也是一样。 “我其实并不是那种固执己见、自以为聪明的人。 就连我也有自己的极限。但是你……你对那只鸟以及它所说的一切反应实在太过激烈了，就好像你在乎证明它是错的这件事，而且这件事与你自己有着某种个人关联一样。 其实并没有什么个人关联，只是这样而已。……只是尼娜说那些最离谱的事情时，总带着一种让人咬牙切齿的自信，就算那些事情最终被证明是真实的，也会让人感到非常难受。不，真的是这样。 尤其是 如果那些事情真的存在的话……如果她关于那棵树和那座矿的猜测是正确的——而事实上，这些事物确实相当普通、平凡——那么，她那些其他的胡言乱语，又有哪些可能是正确的呢？ “也许全部都是正确的。也许什么都不是。奎因耸了耸肩，说道：‘在我看来，自找麻烦实在没有意义；生活已经够艰难了，我们没必要再给自己增添麻烦；对于那些无法改变的事情，其实没必要太过担忧。 我个人更担心的是，那边那个洞里可能有有害气体；我觉得我闻到的是那种味道，尽管非常微弱。我知道，如果你倒下的话，那肯定能证明你的鸟所看到的那些景象并不是真的 [party.som | |我 |我们 ] 我本来想赶紧让你离开的，但我觉得那样做有点太过分了。该死 [pc.name]我可能不会把内心的情感表露得淋漓尽致，但我真的不想失去一个真正关心我的人。我想你也是同样的感受吧。” 你叹了口气。奎因说得对……大动肝火并没有什么意义；如果前方有危险，你还需要保持冷静的头脑。 说实话，仅仅通过告诉你如何到达这个地方，尼娜就已经在某种程度上帮助自己的预言成真了，同时也让自己的话失去了真实性。 “嘿，这次终于不用再追着那个光头混蛋和他的女魔头跑了，真是件好事啊，”奎因一边说，一边拍了拍你的肩膀。 要是真的能遇到一个所谓的先知或通灵者，而且他说的话也不是完全无稽之谈，那该有多有趣啊。我们进去看看吧，看看能发现什么，怎么样？ ] 尽管入口在召唤你前进，但你还是花了一些时间仔细观察矿井基础设施的残余部分。从你观察的情况来看，入口处的结构仍然相当坚固。那些横梁虽然已经干枯，但依然能够支撑得住，至少在这里，你不会遇到坍塌的危险。不，真正会遇到稳定性问题的地方应该是在更深处……你记得尼娜是这么说的…… ……无论如何，如果你想的话，现在就可以进入去了。
rows.raw: " All right, you've come pretty far into the heart of the cold bog that dominates the southeastern Frostwood — if there were ever boreal elf mines in this area for extracting bog iron, they ought to be around here. It's hard not to feel a little silly just walking in circles aimlessly and leaving your progress to fate, [flags.NINA_PSI |but Nina's shown herself to possess a measure of genuine power. Now whether that power extends to divination and clairvoyance is another matter, but it's something for you to have a start on trusting these visions of hers |but if nothing else an empty search will mean you'll be able to ignore Nina's ramblings from here on out ]. As events shape up, though, you don't have to search long; the lightning-blasted tree Nina described stands out in a clearing all of its own, a towering lump of charred ash rising from the bog. So far, so good... all right, north from here it is, then. It's but a short jaunt through the trees, but you'd never have found it without Nina's directions; several patches of dangerously soft mud suck at your feet as you leave the beaten trail, and you take care to stick to the sparser trees in this region of the Frostwood, trusting their roots to make for more solid footing. But eventually, foliage and undergrowth alike part, and you're faced with a large patch of gravel at the foot of a cut-away portion of a hill. The ground is firmer here, and weeds poke out from amidst the pebbles; the signs of civilization lie strewn about you here and there, albeit centuries old. What support beams you can see as the entrance tunnel leads off into the darkness are surprisingly well-preserved for the time they must've spent in neglect, but if anyone's going to be building things to last it's going to be the pale elves with their long lifespans. There aren't any tools or the like — no doubt rusted to dust in the bog's atmosphere by this point — but you see the foundations of a couple of ruined longhouses, stone and hardwood still clinging on to existence where the less durable materials have since long rotted away. All right, that's the second time that crazy bird got it right. Still doesn't prove anything beyond doubt, though. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn kiyoko azyrran agnimitra viviane atugia quintillus |"Ooooooo," Cait says, hopping up to the entrance and peering into the darkness. "A spooky mine. Think there're ghosts in there?" If the dead haunt the mine, at least that's something that Nina didn't warn you about. "Hey, [pc.name]..." What? "Ever consider that you're taking this way too seriously? Like, you're taking this vision thing as some kind of personal affront. I don't know that much magic and have never actually given any thought to fate, the future, and the ability to foretell either, but maybe we should just see what happens and enjoy the ride? That seems a lot more fun to me than getting worked up about this vision business. I don't know, [pc.name], just relax, okay? I can help you with being so wound up, if you'd like." That won't be necessary right here and now, but the thought is appreciated. It's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. But she's right, you're giving this far too much thought than it deserves. Let the chips fall where they may, as it were... |"Hey, [pc.name]," Brint says, coming up and clapping you on the shoulder. "Bothered by something?" Why, does it show? "Yeah. A lot, in fact. Everything's turned out just fine on this little adventure so far, so why're you so glum about it?" You're not glum. It's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. If she's right about the tree and the mine, which admittedly are relatively mundane, what else about her ramblings might she be right about? "Possibly everything. Possibly nothing." Brint scratches his brow, and shrugs. "I was never one for the great minotaur philosophers, I was more of an arena kid myself. But it makes sense to not worry so much about what you can't change. I'm personally more worried about there being bad gases in that hole over there; many a good minotaur's been lost in a shaft because he didn't realize he was breathing the wrong stuff until it was too late. I know that'd probably disprove your bird's visions if you keeled over and [party.som | |I |we ] had to rush you out, but that's a bit too far, I don't think." You sigh. Brint's right... there's no point in getting all worked up; you'll need a cool head on your shoulders if there's going to be danger ahead. And let's face it, by just telling you how to get to this place, Nina's already had a hand in making her own prophecy come true and tainted her own veracity. |"Hey, [pc.name]," Brienne says, coming up and clapping you on the shoulder. "Bothered by something?" Why, does it show? "Yeah. A lot, in fact. Everything's turned out just fine on this little adventure so far, so why're you so glum about it?" You're not glum. It's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. If she's right about the tree and the mine, which admittedly are relatively mundane, what else about her ramblings might she be right about? "Possibly everything. Possibly nothing." Brienne scratches her brow, and shrugs. "I was never one for the great minotaur philosophers, I was more of an arena kid myself. But it makes sense to not worry so much about what you can't change. I'm personally more worried about there being bad gases in that hole over there; many a good minotaur's been lost in a shaft because he didn't realize he was breathing the wrong stuff until it was too late. I know that'd probably disprove your bird's visions if you keeled over and [party.som | |I |we ] had to rush you out, but that's a bit too far, I don't think." H-hey, you never said anything about that. A smile. "I'm sorry. I just, well, worry about you sometimes; you can get really passionate without realizing it. I just don't want you to take unnecessary risks because you got mad. You're the leader here, after all." Well, you're not mad, and you're sorry for making her worry. Brienne leans down for a little kiss, and that tells you all you need to know. |Arona peers suspiciously down the entry shaft and into the gloom. "This just isn't right, I tell you." What isn't? "A mine. Kervus don't dig for metal of any sort, that a job for other people to do and then they give it to us." Sure, you can understand that, but it's not like you're handing out shovels and pickaxes with the intent of digging. Gods, you don't even know if what Nina wants you to get from this place is metallic at all — but if it is, then the elves will have dug it up in times long past and she'll get to carry it off. Does that satisfy her raider's sensibilities? Arona mulls it over. "I guess. Not as great when you're taking it from dead people as opposed to live ones, but it'll do." |Ryn's ears turn down as she peers down the entrance shaft and into the gloom. "Oh. I've never been in one of these..." Well, given that she's hardly been outside of the Winter City before all this started, she likely wouldn't have visited these old elven mines for herself. "Before great-grandmother made the decision to change to sluicing, convicts were sent to work in these mines. Digging into what solid ground the bog has to offer... the more fortunate ones at least worked the easy deposits in open-air mines. These, though... they were called a cruel necessity by the people of the time. They used golems as much as possible, constructs that didn't need to breathe and wouldn't be troubled by the bog gases, but oftentimes you need someone in there... "No one who was sent to the mines expected to serve out their sentence; it was an open secret that it was the death penalty in all but name." Oh. any chance that you'll be meeting embittered elven spirits while inside? "I... don't know. It's possible. But what I'd be more worried about is bog gas having built up in the place over the years — these tunnels haven't been properly ventilated in a long, long time. We should be fine, so long as we aren't going too deep — we aren't going deep, are we?" No, Nina was quite explicit about her directions. Ryn breathes a sigh of relief. "Then we should be fine. Just... be careful." |Kiyoko looks the mine's entrance up and down, then at the ruined buildings off to the side. Finally, she shakes her head. "Ah, a mausoleum. A house of the dead." That's not what this is. It's a mine. "I know what I said, Beloved. There really is no difference here. Can it not be both? Or perhaps I should be more precise in saying that this is a charnel house?" Well... even if you're no Tiran, you can feel the residual misery and death pouring out of the mine in spades. While Nina didn't say that you'd be meeting any spirits on your way in, you wouldn't be surprised if it happened anyway. "Oh, let us not argue and get this over with. I think we can both agree that this is a most unpleasant place." |"Hmm." Azyrran appears contemplative as she takes in the mine's entrance, then extends a hand and tests the air with her fingers. "Warm." After the miseries of the cold bog, that might be welcome. "Maybe, but it might get uncomfortably so deeper inside. There's a reason that we vesperans make sure to set up good air circulation in any hive, not just to prevent it from getting too warm, but also to prevent bad air from building up. Honestly, that's what I'd be more concerned about — it's far more likely the heat's coming from all the things rotting about us, as opposed to the earth itself." Well, she'll warn you if things get too bad, right? According to Nina's so-called vision, you're not going to need to get very far in. "I'll try. I'm not actually any more affected by that sort of thing than you'd be — Drones are the ones who're actually sensitive to this, since they're the ones responsible for the building and maintenance of any hive. Nevertheless, if you catch me getting woozy or dozing off on my feet, snap me out of it and we can beat a hasty retreat. Same goes for me to you, everyone gets that way if you can't breathe properly. Now, shall we begin?" |"You don't see these around that much anymore," Agni says, looking around contemplatively at the architecture. "Deep digging, that is. I... I have the distinct memory that this used to be a lot more common and it wasn't just a select few people like the minotaurs who still delve into the earth. It's all sluicing and open-air mines these days, amongst other things." That would make sense. Various places were hit to varying degrees by the Godswar, and sinking mines like these need considerable engineering and geological knowledge that would've been lost in that kind of conflict. With these elven mines, they'd have been a special case in that they were deliberately abandoned. "Yes, there's that, but... I can't quite place my finger on what exactly's irking me about all this. Never mind, it probably doesn't matter. Shall we?" |"Hmm. A vessel like these would have held good enchantments," Viviane murmurs, stepping up to what's left of an old, crumbling golem and reaching through the vines that cover it to test its surface. "One assumes that they'd have been used for brute labor, but..." But? "To hear your elven companion to speak of it, one of the primary dangers of sinking mines into the bog was the buildup of swamp gas. Using automatons to perform as many tasks as possible, including perhaps even the more cerebral ones... I'd love to be able to study the enchantments that animated these things and what their directives were." And she can tell all this just by examining an ancient, worn-down golem? Viv smiles. "Don't get me wrong, [pc.name] — all that's left here is a withered, dried-up husk of the construct that this used to be. But you can tell something about a liquid from the container intended to hold it, hmm? Now, be careful: if any of these are still wandering around down there, they might be a bother. I don't doubt they could be bespelled to be aggressive, in case there were threats to the mine, a convict tried to escape, or something." |"Hey, look at these!" While you've been busy peering into the gloom that permeates the mine's entrance, Atugia's wandered off and found the vine-covered remnants of a heavy stone golem sitting by a ruined longhouse. "The runes on this thing, they remind me of my own!" You hurry over to her, and indeed, there's enough left of the crumbling elven construct to make out runic indentations on its chest, stomach and arms, patterns that're similar, but not identical to those that crawl over Atugia's skin. Instead of replacing a gem focus, though, they appear to be supplementary to one, a hollow where the golem's heart ought to be in the middle of a web of runic sigils spidering away from that core. "Guess those elves were pretty smart to have the same idea, weren't they?" It is pretty fascinating. You wouldn't want to run into any of these powered up, though. Those fists on this thing look like sledge — no, one of them actually is a sledgehammer. "You're worrying too much. Come on, let's go!" |"This place is downright depressing," Quin mutters as he cranes his head into the mine's entrance and stares into the darkness. "I'd say it reeks of death, but it just plain reeks of so many other things that death alone isn't cutting it." You take a few sniffs, and make a face. Ugh, yeah, it stinks. "Given that it hasn't been ventilated for what must be years, I'd wager it does more than just stink." Quin grimaces. "Hey, [pc.name]... if you feel faint at any time while we're down there, don't hesitate to call uncle, okay? I don't want you suffocating or anything." Same could be said for him, in that case. "I'm not that much of a hard-headed smartass. Even I have my limits. But you... you're reacting really badly to that bird and all the stuff she said, like you've got some personal stake in proving her wrong." It's not a personal stake, it's just that... just that Nina has a way of saying the most outlandish things with a degree of confidence that makes for a teeth-grinding time even if they turn out to be real. No, especially if they turn out to be real. If she's right about the tree and the mine, which admittedly are relatively mundane, what else about her ramblings might she be right about? "Possibly everything. Possibly nothing." Quin shrugs. "Way I see it, it doesn't make sense to make problems for yourself; life's already enough of a struggle without you tripping over your own feet; it makes sense to not worry so much about what you can't change. I'm personally more worried about there being bad gases in that hole over there; I think that's what I'm smelling, even if it's really faint. I know that'd probably disprove your bird's visions if you keeled over and [party.som | |I |we ] had to rush you out, but that's a bit too far, I don't think. Damn it, [pc.name], I may not wear my heart on my sleeve, but I'd hate to lose someone who gave a shit about me, and I think you'd, too." You sigh. Quin's right... there's no point in getting all worked up; you'll need a cool head on your shoulders if there's going to be danger ahead. And let's face it, by just telling you how to get to this place, Nina's already had a hand in making her own prophecy come true and tainted her own veracity. "Hey, it's a nice change from running around after that bald fucker and his demonness for once," Quin says, clapping you on the shoulder. "And it'd be interesting to actually come across a so-called prophet or clairvoyant who isn't spouting complete nonsense, too. Let's go in and see what we find, yeah?" ] Despite the entrance beckoning you forward, you take your time in examining the remnants of the mine's infrastructure; from what you can tell, what remains about the entrance is still relatively sturdy. The beams are dry but still hold well enough, and you won't be in any danger of a collapse here, at the very least. No, it'll be deeper in when stability becomes a problem, that's what you remember Nina saying... ...In any case, you can enter now if you like. "

rows.original:
[var0
        |Once more, you step into the chamber; once more, the golem grinds to life and starts its advance, the pulsing blue veins upon its body flaring to life. Fully dedicated to whatever final commands its masters may have issued before their departure, the automaton is no less fearsome for being repurposed from its original capabilities to serve as a guardian.
        |Apprehensively, you make your way deeper into the mine, the [dayNight|sun|moon]light from outside rapidly vanishing into nothingness by the heavy darkness. Even with whatever light source you might have at hand, the atmosphere is stifling, pressing inwards upon any illumination as if consciously suppressing it. The air is still, and your footsteps ring in the claustrophobic confines as you press forward...

        ...Until they don't. Suddenly, the entrance tunnel opens up into a large chamber crumbling in disrepair — while the support beams still hold, they're probably not going to last another decade or two, which considering the general longevity of pale elf architecture is saying something. This cavern was clearly used as a staging area for the miners' work, with the tools of their trade left neatly abandoned; they sure didn't leave in a hurry, and perhaps even intended to return. Odd, that...
        
        An eerie glow emanates from somewhere deeper in the mine, and you're about to cross the chamber and examine further when a loud rumbling, grinding noise off to the side draws your attention. Arrayed against one of the far walls is a trio of of stocky stone golems, decayed with age; one of them, however, is clearly still functional as it stands and assumes a humanoid shape. Veins of blue threading out from its core, the ancient work automaton lumbers to life and squares its alabaster shoulders, its glowing eyes peering down at the intruder[party.hasCompanions|s] in front of it as it moves to block your path. There's a moment's tension in the heavy air as you reach for your [pc.weapon] in response to its clear aggression, and then the golem starts advancing upon you, raising its sledgehammer of a hand at you threateningly.
    ]
rows.translation:
[var0
        |你再次走进那个房间；那个魔像又一次苏醒过来，开始向前移动，它身体上那些脉动的蓝色血管也重新亮了起来。这个自动机器完全致力于执行它的主人在离开之前下达的最终指令，尽管它的功能已经被改变，用来担任守护者的角色，但它依然令人胆寒。
        |你忧心忡忡地继续向矿井深处走去。 [dayNight|太阳|月亮]外界的轻型线在浓厚的黑暗中迅速消失得无影无踪。无论你手头有什么轻型源，这种氛围都显得令人窒息，仿佛有一种力量在刻意压制任何轻型线。 空气静止不动，你的脚步声在这个令人窒息的空间里回荡，你继续向前走去……

……直到脚步声消失了。突然，入口通道通向了一个破败不堪的大厅——虽然支撑梁还完好无损，但它们恐怕再撑不过一二十年了。而考虑到苍白精灵建筑的通常耐久性，这一点实在不容忽视。 这个洞穴显然曾被矿工们用作工作场所，他们的工具也被整齐地留在了那里；看来他们并不是匆忙离开的，甚至可能还打算回来。真是奇怪……

矿井深处某个地方散发着诡异的轻型芒，你正准备穿过这个洞室继续探查时，突然听到旁边传来一阵巨大的轰鸣声和摩擦声，吸引了你的注意。 在远处的墙壁旁，排列着三个粗壮的石制魔像，它们因年代久远而已经腐朽不堪；然而其中有一个显然仍然可以正常运作，它保持着人形的姿态。蓝色的脉络从它的核心部分延伸出来，这个古老的自动机械缓缓苏醒过来，将它那雪花石膏般的肩膀挺直，它那发轻型的眼睛俯视着入侵者。[party.hasCompanions|s] 当它移动过来挡住你的去路时，你就站在它的面前。在那一刹那，空气中弥漫着紧张的气氛，而你则迅速伸手去抓住 [pc.weapon] 作为对其明显侵略行为的回应，那个魔像开始向你发起攻击，它那像大锤一样的手威胁性地朝你挥来。
    ]

rows.original: As the oversized hunk of rock lumbers forward, you cast a glance at Etheryn. Can she do something? [etheryn.lowConfidence |Ryn glances back at you over her [etheryn.weapon]. "W-what do you mean? Please don't joke with me n-now!" No, you're quite serious. She's a boreal elf, and of royal blood to boot. If these mines were sanctioned by the — You don't get to complete your sentence before the golem's hammer-hand smashes into the stone floor, throwing up splinters and sending the both of you diving away from the impact. Ears ringing and vision shaky, you realize just how close you were to being flattened there and then. [pc.isDK |Well, if she doesn't mind at least trying something before you're genuinely forced into combat with this thing, you'd really appreciate it! |There isn't much time left — another moment, and you'll be forced into combat with this thing. If she would please at least try doing something? ] Ryn looks genuinely confused at what you want her to do, then snaps out of it as her eyes meet yours and receive a commanding glance. It can't have been more than the blink of an eye, but it feels like an aeon passes as Ryn balls her fists, takes a deep breath, and steps up shakily to the golem. Raising a hand to the construct, she speaks a couple of sentences in her native tongue, doing her best to sound authoritative. While you don't understand the words yourself, you can guess at their meaning from the tone she's using — or at least, is attempting to use — with the automaton. And it works. Amazingly, it works. The golem hesitates, then respectfully lowers its arms and returns to the wall to rest alongside its ruined, decaying kin. Moments later, the blue lines of pulsing energy that spider across its body retreat into its chest, and then it's an inanimate hunk of stone once more. It's only then that Ryn wipes the cold sweat from her brow and sags against you as you step up to her and catch her by under the shoulders. Impressive. What exactly did she say to it, if you might ask? "Well, what you s-said. Long story short, I asserted my lineage and told it to stand down. It obeyed. Gods, I was so terrified." [pc.isDK |But she was more terrified of you than she was of a hunk of junk. Wise decision, that |But she overcame her fear in order to act in defense of herself and her friends. That's the important thing ]. As for the golem, it doesn't look like it's going to be standing back up. No harm in making sure that's not a possibility, though, even if Ryn's clearly able to countermand whatever orders it was given last before this place was abandoned. "Oh. O-of course!" Ryn doesn't give herself any time to think about it — no doubt realizing that if she does consider her actions she'll shy away from them. Skittering up to the inert golem, your elven companion clambers up onto what passes for its hefty thigh and reaches up into its torso. 她向那个机械装置举起手部，用她的母语说了几句话，尽力让自己的肌肉度听起来充满权威性。虽然你听不懂那些话语的具体内容，但根据她说话时的肌肉度——或者至少是她试图营造出来的那种肌肉度——你还是能够猜出这些话的大意。 rows.original: As the oversized hunk of rock lumbers forward, you cast a glance at Viv. Can she do something? "Do something?" Viv quirks an eyebrow at you, completely unperturbed by the ground trembling with each step the golem takes. "When you ask a witch to do 'something', that's very broad indeed." She's an enchantress; automatons would surely fall within her expertise, even if they're on the periphery, right? Perhaps — You don't get to complete your sentence before the golem's hammer-hand smashes into the stone floor, throwing up splinters and sending the both of you diving away from the impact. Ears ringing and vision shaky, you realize just how close you were to being flattened there and then. [pc.isDK |Well, if she doesn't mind at least trying something before you're genuinely forced into combat with this thing, you'd really appreciate it! |There isn't much time left — another moment, and you'll be forced into combat with this thing. If she would please at least try doing something? ] "Of course. Hold its attention for me while I work, okay?" Much easier said than done, given that the golem's already raised its hands for another blow. Still, so long as you're the one poking at it while Viv is by all appearances merely standing off to the side, concentrating furiously. You dodge out of the way as the golem pounds the ground again, sending dust pouring down from the cavern ceiling, and moves to recover for yet another strike. That's when Viv leaps into action — quite literally, as bindings of shimmering energy lash out from her arm with the flick of her wrist and strike the golem while its back is turned to her. The sight of the enchantress sailing through the air to perch atop the craggy automaton is something to behold as half-turns to deal with this new threat, making to pull her off its back; you take the opportunity to press your attack, forcing the golem to divide its attention between Viv and you and subsequently not doing very much against either. Not a very smart thing, but then one supposes that it was never intended for more than manual labor. Viv herself wears an expression of furious concentration as the golem tries to throw her off, clinging furiously to her magical tether as her hat billows off her head from all the jerking about and falls to the ground. Yet she stays on — it can't be more than ten or so seconds, yet it feels like hours before the web of blue lines that courscate across the golem's skin retract into its torso and go dull. Bereft of its animating force, the construct stutters and falls on its side with a crash, sending Viv tumbling off its back; she stands up, dusts herself off, then retrieves her hat with no small amount of smug before surveying her handiwork. "And thus it was shown to be demonstrated." [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion |Indeed. |Huh? "Old Imperial saying." ] Satisfied with what she's seeing, Viv steps over to the golem, confident that it's out of commission for good; she reaches into its torso, grabs at something, and tugs firmly. A chunk of mica the size of her head comes loose from within the construct, and she tests its weight in her hands with no small satisfaction. "I'll be keeping this, if you don't mind; I think I'll be getting far more use out of it than you would. The druidic enchantments that animated this thing are unique enough that I'd like to study them further on my own time — they certainly differ in form from the classical methods, even if the fundamentals don't differ." Which is presumably how she managed to shut this thing down? "Schools of magic don't change depending on who's invoking them, dear. Pull out the bottom block, and the rest comes tumbling down." She chuckles, and you notice she's a lot more enthusiastic about this entire venture than before. "Even if you don't find anything else of worth in this dingy mine, this trip will have been worth it. While this isn't what the silly bird sent you here to get, it's nevertheless quite the valuable find; wonder what else we'll discover inside? She was right about the golem, wonder what else she's right about?" Come on, it's time to finish this silly errand and be done with it.
rows.translation: 当那块巨大的岩石缓缓向前移动时，你瞥了眼薇芙。她能做些什么吗？ “做些什么？”薇芙挑了挑眉毛看着你，对于魔像每走一步都会引起的地面震动，她似乎完全毫不在意。 当你要求一位女巫去做某件事时，这个要求其实相当模糊。” 她是一位女巫；自动机这类东西肯定也在她的专业范围之内，即使它们属于比较边缘的领域吧？也许吧—— 但你还没来得及把话说完，那个魔像的锤状手部就已经砸在了石地上，溅起了许多碎片，你们俩也被这冲击力逼得不得不向后跳开。 耳朵嗡嗡作响，视线也变得模糊不清，你这才意识到，自己刚才真是差一点就被彻底击倒在地了。 [pc.isDK |嗯，如果她不介意的话……至少是这样。 尝试中 在真正被迫与这个东西交战之前，要是能有点什么准备或提示，那真的会非常有用！ |时间不多了——再过一会儿，你就不得不与这个东西展开战斗了。如果她能稍微……的话。 尝试一下吧。 在做什么吗？ ] 当然可以。在我操作的时候，帮我吸引它的注意力，好吗？” 说起来容易做起来难，因为那个魔像已经举起了手部，准备再次攻击。不过，只要是你去惹它，而薇芙显然只是站在一旁，全神贯注地观察着局势就行。当魔像再次猛地砸向地面，导致洞穴的天花板掉落大量灰尘时，你迅速躲开，然后准备迎接它的下一次攻击。 就在这时，薇芙立刻采取了行动——她手部腕一抖，闪烁着能量的束缚就从她的手部臂中射出，击中了那个背对她的魔像。看到这位女巫在空中飞掠，最终落在那个崎岖不平的自动机械身上，这一幕实在令人惊叹。那个魔像转过身来应对这个新的威胁，试图将薇芙从它的背上拉开；而你则趁这个机会发动攻击，迫使那个魔像不得不将注意力分在薇芙和你身上，结果它对你们俩的攻击都显得力不从心。 这并不是什么明智的做法，但想来，这种设计本来也就只适用于体力劳动而已。 薇芙本人也露出了全神贯注、怒不可遏的表情。当那个魔像试图扰乱她的注意力时，她紧紧抓住自己的魔法纽带，拼命保持平衡。由于不断的晃动，她的帽子从头上脱落，掉在了地上。然而，她依然没有放弃——虽然这段时间不超过十秒钟，但对她来说，却仿佛过了好几个小时。最终，那些覆盖在魔像皮肤上的蓝色线条逐渐缩回它的躯干，变得暗淡无光。 失去了驱动它的力量，那个装置开始颤抖，最终侧翻在地，发出巨大的声响，导致薇芙从它的背上摔了下去。她站起身来，拍掉身上的灰尘，然后得意洋洋地捡起了自己的帽子，接着仔细审视了自己造成的“成果”。 就这样，事实得到了证明。 [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion |确实如此。 |古时的皇室谚语。 ] 看到眼前的景象，薇芙满意地走到那个魔像面前，确信它已经彻底无法使用了。她伸手部进入它的躯干，抓住某个东西，用力一拉——一块和她头差不多大的云母碎片从魔像体内脱落下来，她将这块碎片拿在手部中，满意地感受着它的重量。 如果你不介意的话，我就把它留下来吧。我觉得我会比你更经常用到它。赋予这个物品生命力的德鲁伊魔法非常独特，我希望能利用业余时间进一步研究它们——尽管这些魔法的基本原理与传统的做法并无不同，但它们的表现形式确实有所不同。大概就是通过这种方式，她才成功让这个装置停止运行的吧？ “亲爱的，魔法学院并不会因为使用它们的人不同而发生改变。只要拔掉最下面的那个部件，其余的部分就会依次倒下。她轻声笑了起来，你可以看出，她对这次冒险充满了前所未有的热情。“即使在这座破旧的矿井里什么有价值的东西都没有找到，这次旅行也绝对是值得的。虽然这并不是那个傻姑娘让你来这里要找的东西，但这个发现确实非常珍贵——不知道我们还能在里面发现什么呢？ 她关于那个魔像的判断是正确的，不知道她还在哪些事情上判断正确呢？ 快吧，是时候完成这个愚蠢的任务，把它彻底解决了。
rows.raw: " As the oversized hunk of rock lumbers forward, you cast a glance at Viv. Can she do something? "Do something?" Viv quirks an eyebrow at you, completely unperturbed by the ground trembling with each step the golem takes. "When you ask a witch to do 'something', that's very broad indeed." She's an enchantress; automatons would surely fall within her expertise, even if they're on the periphery, right? Perhaps — You don't get to complete your sentence before the golem's hammer-hand smashes into the stone floor, throwing up splinters and sending the both of you diving away from the impact. Ears ringing and vision shaky, you realize just how close you were to being flattened there and then. [pc.isDK |Well, if she doesn't mind at least trying something before you're genuinely forced into combat with this thing, you'd really appreciate it! |There isn't much time left — another moment, and you'll be forced into combat with this thing. If she would please at least try doing something? ] "Of course. Hold its attention for me while I work, okay?" Much easier said than done, given that the golem's already raised its hands for another blow. Still, so long as you're the one poking at it while Viv is by all appearances merely standing off to the side, concentrating furiously. You dodge out of the way as the golem pounds the ground again, sending dust pouring down from the cavern ceiling, and moves to recover for yet another strike. That's when Viv leaps into action — quite literally, as bindings of shimmering energy lash out from her arm with the flick of her wrist and strike the golem while its back is turned to her. The sight of the enchantress sailing through the air to perch atop the craggy automaton is something to behold as half-turns to deal with this new threat, making to pull her off its back; you take the opportunity to press your attack, forcing the golem to divide its attention between Viv and you and subsequently not doing very much against either. Not a very smart thing, but then one supposes that it was never intended for more than manual labor. Viv herself wears an expression of furious concentration as the golem tries to throw her off, clinging furiously to her magical tether as her hat billows off her head from all the jerking about and falls to the ground. Yet she stays on — it can't be more than ten or so seconds, yet it feels like hours before the web of blue lines that courscate across the golem's skin retract into its torso and go dull. Bereft of its animating force, the construct stutters and falls on its side with a crash, sending Viv tumbling off its back; she stands up, dusts herself off, then retrieves her hat with no small amount of smug before surveying her handiwork. "And thus it was shown to be demonstrated." [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion |Indeed. |Huh? "Old Imperial saying." ] Satisfied with what she's seeing, Viv steps over to the golem, confident that it's out of commission for good; she reaches into its torso, grabs at something, and tugs firmly. A chunk of mica the size of her head comes loose from within the construct, and she tests its weight in her hands with no small satisfaction. "I'll be keeping this, if you don't mind; I think I'll be getting far more use out of it than you would. The druidic enchantments that animated this thing are unique enough that I'd like to study them further on my own time — they certainly differ in form from the classical methods, even if the fundamentals don't differ." Which is presumably how she managed to shut this thing down? "Schools of magic don't change depending on who's invoking them, dear. Pull out the bottom block, and the rest comes tumbling down." She chuckles, and you notice she's a lot more enthusiastic about this entire venture than before. "Even if you don't find anything else of worth in this dingy mine, this trip will have been worth it. While this isn't what the silly bird sent you here to get, it's nevertheless quite the valuable find; wonder what else we'll discover inside? She was right about the golem, wonder what else she's right about?" Come on, it's time to finish this silly errand and be done with it."

rows.original: There doesn't seem to be any other recourse. With the golem bringing itself to bear down upon you once more, you're forced to ready your [pc.weapon] and meet it in combat. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 看来没有其他办法了。当那个魔像再次朝你扑来时，你只能做好准备应对了。 [pc.weapon] 并在战斗中与之交锋。 这是一场激烈的战斗！
rows.raw: " There doesn't seem to be any other recourse. With the golem bringing itself to bear down upon you once more, you're forced to ready your [pc.weapon] and meet it in combat. It's a fight!"

rows.original: You can't take much more of this — the golem is following its last received orders to play sentry with single-minded determination and an effective, heavy-handed approach to carrying out said orders. [party.hasCompanions |Gathering up [party.compNames] |Choosing to disengage while you still can ], you beat a quick retreat into the entrance tunnel. While the golem's not so large as to not being able to fit into the egress, it doesn't choose to pursue you, presumably so as to not let itself be drawn away from its post. Perhaps you should reconsider your strategy before making another attempt; it's not as if Nina's given you a deadline by which you have to return with the goods. She wasn't wrong about the nasty construct bit, though... especially the nasty part.
rows.translation: 你再也无法忍受这种状况了——这个魔像正严格按照它最后接收到的指令，以极其执着的态度执行守卫任务，其执行方式也显得粗暴而有效。 [party.hasCompanions |开始行动吧 [party.compNames] |在还来得及的时候选择退出吧。 ]你迅速撤退到了入口隧道中。虽然那个魔像体型不小，但应该还是能够通过出口的；不过它并没有选择追击你，大概是因为它不想离开自己的岗位吧。 或许在再次尝试之前，你应该重新考虑一下自己的策略吧……毕竟尼娜并没有给你规定必须在这个时间内带回货物的期限。不过，她关于那个讨厌的魔像的描述确实没错……尤其是那一点 糟糕的 部分。

[party.hasCompanions |Gathering up [party.compNames] |Choosing to disengage while you still can ], you beat a quick retreat into the entrance tunnel. While the golem's not so large as to not being able to fit into the egress, it doesn't choose to pursue you, presumably so as to not let itself be drawn away from its post. Perhaps you should reconsider your strategy before making another attempt; it's not as if Nina's given you a deadline by which you have to return with the goods. She wasn't wrong about the nasty construct bit, though... especially the nasty part."

rows.original:
With a final blow, the golem teeters off-balance, topples, and smashes into several pieces upon the cavern floor, the lines of blue glowing light that wind over its body winking out as it fails. You approach carefully, cautious that some pieces of it might still be ambulatory in some form, but after getting close and a bit of prodding it looks like the construct is well and truly out of commission. You search the spot in its torso where the web of enchantment had originated from, but to your dismay the head-sized chink of mica which presumably had served to power the spells that fueled it has shattered into chunks. 
    
    [pc.isMage
        |You focus for a bit, seeing if there's still anything with salvaging, but it l
        |L
    ]ooks like there's nothing of worth here unless you're into semi-precious stones of dubious value. Dusting yourself off, you eye the remaining two golems lying against the wall, but they aren't inclined to rise up and avenge their fallen kin.
    
    Well then. Time to move on...
rows.translation:
随着最后一击，那个魔像失去了平衡，倒了下来，摔成了好几块，散落在洞穴的地面上。它身上那些蓝色的轻型芒也随着它的毁灭而熄灭了。你小心翼翼地靠近，担心其中某些碎片可能还具备活动能力，但当你靠近并稍微拨动了一下那些碎片后，你确定这个魔像已经彻底不能再使用了。 你在它的躯干上寻找那片蕴含着魔法力量的地方，但令你失望的是，那块原本用来为那些支撑它的法术提供能量的、有头那么大的云母片已经碎成了碎片。 
    
    [pc.isMage
        |你集中注意力看了一会儿，想确认是否还有什么可以抢救的东西，但结果……
        |L
    ]看来这里没什么有价值的东西，除非你对那些价值不明的半宝石感兴趣。你拍掉身上的灰尘，看了看靠在墙边的那两个魔像，但它们似乎并没有想要站起来为它们倒下的同伴报仇的意愿。

那好吧，是时候继续前进了……

rows.original: Well, then. You're still relatively new to the wings that were part of the package deal for your soul, but these are valkyrie wings, unlike any other in the world. Scalding steam and upwells of sulfurous air? Not a problem for who you are now! Or at least, that's how it should go. Once the rush of realization passes and you're considering your situation more seriously, the obstacles present themselves in full: the constant updraft rising from the sinkholes, accompanied by the occasional bust of steam, promises to make your crossing all the more troublesome for the heat and turbulence it'll create. The sound of rushing water comes from deep within the sinkholes, and while it might conceivably cushion a fall there's no telling where you might be swept to, or if there's even anything breathable down there. Nina did say misstep and perish... but that doesn't necessarily mean that not stepping at all to begin with means that one won't perish.
rows.translation: 那么，好吧。你才刚刚开始使用那些与你的灵魂一同被赋予的翅膀，但这些可是独一无二的、属于女武神的翅膀。灼热的蒸汽与充满硫磺气味的空气？对你现在这样的存在来说，根本不是问题！ 或者至少，应该是这样的。当最初的兴奋感消退，你开始更认真地思考自己的处境时，那些阻碍就会完全显现出来：从坑洞中不断升起的上升气流，再加上偶尔喷发的蒸汽，这些因素所带来的高温和湍流，一定会让你的穿越过程变得异常艰难。 从那些天坑的深处传来了湍急的水流声。虽然这样的水流或许能在一定程度上减轻坠落的冲击力，但谁也说不准自己会被冲到哪里去，更不知道那里是否还有可供呼吸的空气。尼娜确实说过：一旦踏错一步，就会丧命。…但这并不一定意味着如此。 不是 首先，采取任何行动就意味着某人 不会 灭亡吧。

Nina did say misstep and perish... but that doesn't necessarily mean that not stepping at all to begin with means that one won't perish."

rows.original: Thankfully, you've got not just one, but two companions with you who're more experienced flyers: giggling and looking all kinds of smug, both Azzy and Agni come up from either side, sandwiching you between their teasing bodies. "Nervous?" Agni says. Just a little. You still have to test your wings under tumultuous flying conditions, and it's good that you've two lovely ladies with you who've been doing this all their lives — and in Agni's case, many lives. At the very least, there'll be someone to make sure that any silly mistakes you make won't necessarily be fatal. "That's us, all right," Azzy adds, pushing herself against your side and chuckling. "We're good helpers." Helpers? That would imply that you're more experienced at this than either of them, peoples born to it. "Oh, hush your silver tongue. Now, pay attention — this isn't anything for a hive knight like me, but you've still got much to learn. Keep an eye out, and stay close to us, okay?"
rows.translation: 幸运的是，你拥有的不仅仅是一个，而是多个。 两个 那些飞行经验更丰富的伙伴们也加入了你们：阿齐和阿格尼从两边走过来，一边咯咯笑着，一边露出得意的表情，他们的身体将你们夹在中间，不断地逗弄你们。 “紧张吗？”阿格尼问道。 只是稍微需要一些时间而已。你仍然需要在充满挑战的飞行环境中测试自己的能力，而好在你有两位经验丰富的女性陪伴在你身边——对阿格尼来说，这甚至意味着她已经经历了许多次这样的考验。至少，有她们在，可以确保你犯下的任何小错误都不会带来严重的后果。 就是我们啦，”阿齐说着，靠在你的身侧，轻声笑了起来，“我们可是很称职的帮手哦。” 帮手？这么说来，你在这一方面应该比他们两个——那些天生就适合做这件事的人——更有经验吧？ 哦，别再夸夸其谈了。现在，注意听好了——这种事情对我这样的蜂巢骑士来说根本不算什么，但你还有很多需要学习的地方。仔细观察，跟在我们身边，好吗？
