rows.original: You don't set off immediately, though, instead taking several minutes to watch the steam plumes and see if there's any pattern to their spouting. Agni might be able to shrug off being caught in one, but neither Azzy nor you are as resistant to scalding as she is. Eventually, though, the two ladies give you a nod and beckon you forward. "I think I've worked out a path away from the worst of the updrafts and steam spouts," Agni says, pointing into the darkness. "The former might not be as hot as the latter, but who knows what kinds of air's being blown up from beneath the earth. Flying can take it out of you, and you don't want to take a breath of something bad while you're at it." Makes sense. "Are you ready now?" As ready as you'll ever be. Just stick close to the both of them, right? "Right, and use your eyes and ears, call out if you see something." Agni goes first, taking a few steps back and breaking into a running start before launching herself out over the sinkholes, flapping furiously; you're next to go, and finally Azzy brings up the rear, buzzing along behind. The crossing's as difficult as you'd expected it to be — Agni has to focus on keeping everyone moving in the correct direction through the gloom, which leaves you and Azzy to spot obstacles in time to prevent the three of you from running face-first into them. More than once either of you calls out a plume of steam gushing up from below just in time for the three of you to swerve away, and you have to stop on an island of solid ground midway to take a breather and refresh yourselves before heading off the rest of the way. Eventually, though, you make it over, and you wipe the sweat from her brow — not so much from the heat, but more from being jolted and tossed mid-air. It's good to have solid ground under your feet again — sure, being in the air will probably become second nature to you in the days to come, but here and now you've never been gladder to be out of danger. "Phew. That was quite the steamy affair." Well, if Agni's still in the mood to joke around, she presumably still has the strength to go on without a rest. "Oh, don't you worry about it," Azzy purrs. "I'll be able to handle both the both of you, should it come to that. Now, if you don't mind, I'm rather interested in seeing just what it is that we came all the way here to get. Aren't you excited?" Yes... even if you're a bit winded from the flight, there is a certain curiosity there. Time to move on...
rows.translation: 不过，你并没有立即出发，而是花了几分钟时间观察那些蒸汽柱，试图找出它们喷发的规律。虽然阿格尼可能不会被蒸汽烫伤，但阿齐和你显然没有她那么耐热。最终，两位女士点了点头，示意你继续前进。 我想我已经找到了一条可以避开那些最强烈的上升气流和蒸汽喷发的路径，”阿格尼一边说，一边指向黑暗中的方向。“那些上升气流可能没有蒸汽喷发那么炙热，但谁知道从地下吹出来的空气里究竟含有什么有害物质呢。飞行会让人精疲力竭，而你肯定不希望在飞行的过程中吸入那些有害的东西。 你现在准备好了吗？” “我已经准备得尽可能充分了。只要紧跟在他们俩身边就行了，对吧？” “没错，一定要仔细观察周围，如果看到什么异常情况，立刻大声呼喊。 阿格尼先走了，她后退了几步，然后突然加速奔跑，接着便飞越了那些坑洞，翅膀剧烈地拍动着；接下来就该你了，最后阿齐跟在后面，嗡嗡作响地飞着。 这个穿越过程确实如你预想的那样困难——Agni必须专注于引导大家在黑暗中朝着正确的方向前进，而你和Azzy的任务就是及时发现障碍物，避免你们三人撞上它们。 不止一次，你们中的某个人及时发现了从下方喷涌而出的蒸汽柱，于是你们三人立刻躲开了。在继续前行的途中，你们不得不在半路的一个坚实陆地上停下来，休息片刻，重新调整状态，然后再继续前进。 不过，最终你还是成功克服了那些困难，帮她擦去了额头上的汗水——这些汗水并非因为高温，而是因为在半空中不断被颠簸所造成的。能够再次站在坚实的地面上，这种感觉真是太好了。当然，在未来的日子里，待在半空中或许会变得习以为常，但此刻，你能脱离危险，心中自然是无比欣喜的。 呼，刚才那一幕真是够激烈的啊。” 既然阿格尼还愿意开玩笑，那她应该还有足够的精力继续下去吧。 “哦，别担心，”阿齐柔声说道，“如果真到了那一步，我完全有能力应付你们两个。现在，如果你们不介意的话，我其实很想知道我们究竟是为什么来到这里的。你们难道不觉得兴奋吗？ 是的……即使你在飞行中有些疲惫，でも 是 还是有些好奇的……是时候继续前进了……
rows.raw: " You don't set off immediately, though, instead taking several minutes to watch the steam plumes and see if there's any pattern to their spouting. Agni might be able to shrug off being caught in one, but neither Azzy nor you are as resistant to scalding as she is. Eventually, though, the two ladies give you a nod and beckon you forward. "I think I've worked out a path away from the worst of the updrafts and steam spouts," Agni says, pointing into the darkness. "The former might not be as hot as the latter, but who knows what kinds of air's being blown up from beneath the earth. Flying can take it out of you, and you don't want to take a breath of something bad while you're at it." Makes sense. "Are you ready now?" As ready as you'll ever be. Just stick close to the both of them, right? "Right, and use your eyes and ears, call out if you see something." Agni goes first, taking a few steps back and breaking into a running start before launching herself out over the sinkholes, flapping furiously; you're next to go, and finally Azzy brings up the rear, buzzing along behind. The crossing's as difficult as you'd expected it to be — Agni has to focus on keeping everyone moving in the correct direction through the gloom, which leaves you and Azzy to spot obstacles in time to prevent the three of you from running face-first into them. More than once either of you calls out a plume of steam gushing up from below just in time for the three of you to swerve away, and you have to stop on an island of solid ground midway to take a breather and refresh yourselves before heading off the rest of the way. Eventually, though, you make it over, and you wipe the sweat from her brow — not so much from the heat, but more from being jolted and tossed mid-air. It's good to have solid ground under your feet again — sure, being in the air will probably become second nature to you in the days to come, but here and now you've never been gladder to be out of danger. "Phew. That was quite the steamy affair." Well, if Agni's still in the mood to joke around, she presumably still has the strength to go on without a rest. "Oh, don't you worry about it," Azzy purrs. "I'll be able to handle both the both of you, should it come to that. Now, if you don't mind, I'm rather interested in seeing just what it is that we came all the way here to get. Aren't you excited?" Yes... even if you're a bit winded from the flight, there is a certain curiosity there. Time to move on..."

rows.original: Thankfully, you're not alone in being able to fly: Agni comes up by your side as you survey the sinkhole-riddled cavern, peering out over the treacherous ground. "You have to wonder if the elves knew they were digging right above a steam bath like this, or if something happened to turn their dig into this mess," she remarks. "Nervous?" Just a little. You haven't had your wings very long compared to her, so it's reassuring to have someone more experienced at your side while making the crossing. At the very least, there'll be someone to make sure that any silly mistakes you make won't necessarily be fatal. "You could have had your wings your whole life, and you still wouldn't have had them very long compared to me," Agni replies with a chuckle. "I guess that makes me a good helper, huh?" Helper? That'd imply that you're the leader in this endeavor. Come now, when you just got done flattering her on how she's far more experienced at flight than you? "Oh, hush your silver tongue. Now, pay attention, and stay close to me while we're in the air. The cavern may be large, but there's a lot less space to get around with than if we were under open skies." Agni thinks a moment, then [party.manyCompanions |turns to [comp2.name], having a brief conversation with [comp2.himHer] that you don't quite make out. Eventually, she refocuses her attention on you and nods. "Okay, we're ready to go. [comp2.name] will wait here until we're over, and then I'll come back to fetch [comp2.himHer]." Oh? Wouldn't it be better to bring [comp2.himHer] along with you on the trip as well? Not only would you be able to share the load between yourselves, but you'd only have to make one trip to boot. "Yeah, but we aren't practised at carrying loads through the air together — look, I'd have to use my legs, and you'd be using your hands. Not the most intuitive way to go about it, right? That, and the second time around will be easier when we've figured out a clear route instead of having to deal with the weight and watching out for each other. You made me the lead here, so you can follow along, can't you?" The thought of [comp2.name] wedged between Agni's drumsticks does lend itself to a [pc.isBimbo |giggle |snort ] |thins her lips. "I don't think we can glean anything further from watching the steam geysers. Let's go — and remember, say something if you aren't well. I'm more resistant to the heat than you are, so I won't necessarily know if you're suffering. Are you ready?" Will do, you're as ready as you'll ever be ]. Very well, lead the way, then. It is a bit of a struggle — Agni focuses on scouting out a path ahead, which leaves you to focus on staying aloft while following her lead. More than once she swerves away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you even if she's largely impervious to heat, and the both of you have to stop on an island of solid ground to rest for several moments and take a breather. Maybe it's just the heat, maybe it's something in the air, but you feel like you're tiring far easier than you ought to be for such a relatively short crossing over what's effectively a collection of pits and soaked, crumbling stone. Eventually, though, you make it over, and Agni wipes the sweat from her brow. "Phew, that was something. [party.manyCompanions |I still have to go back to bring [comp2.name] over, don't I?" If she doesn't mind. She's the one who convinced you to leave [comp2.himHer] behind, after all. Or is she having second thoughts now? "No, no, this was just a little harder than I expected; if anything, it makes what I said earlier all the more pertinent. I'll just need a breather before I head on back." A good idea. She should take plenty of time to rest up before bringing [comp2.name] over; there's no rush while you make sure that this side of the sinkhole-dotted cavern is safe. You don't want anything happening to either of them while in flight. "Trust me, I don't want that, either. All right, give me a moment." And a moment is what she needs. After ten minutes or so of rest, Agni goes flapping back over the updrafts and returns shortly with [comp2.name] sandwiched between her knees and thighs, looking a bit uncomfortable and perhaps even embarrassed, but not daring to squirm. The two land by your side with a heavy, exhausted thump, and Agni breathes a huge sigh of relief. There, there. With your party re-assembled on safe footing, it's time to see what this side of the mines holds for you... |Quite the steamy affair that crossing was, aren't I right?" Well, she's still in the mood to joke around, so you have to agree. "It wasn't that bad, but still, it's not something that I'd do every day. Staying at the temple has given me a little appreciation for how much fire's underground in these parts, but still! I wonder just what the return trip will be like, but that depends on how heavy what we've been sent to fetch will weigh, right?" Right. And since you have no idea as to what it might be, she ought to be prepared for just about any eventuality she can imagine. "Aah, it won't be too bad. Not with you around, at any rate. Truth be told, I'm rather interested in seeing just what it is that we came all the way here for. Aren't you excited?" With her like this? Now you are. Time to take a look-see, then... ]

"I'm sure we'll be able to handle it together. Now, if you don't mind, with you talking up this thing so much, I'm rather interested in seeing just what it is that we came all the way here for. Aren't you excited?" Hey, no need to rush things — but yes... there is a certain curiosity there, if nothing else. You'll move on when the time is ripe... ]
rows.translation: 幸运的是，能够飞行的并不只有你：当你环顾这个布满天坑的洞穴，小心翼翼地观察那些危险的地面时，Azzy飞到了你身边。 “你肯定会想知道，那些精灵是否知道他们正在这样的一个蒸汽浴室上方挖掘，还是说发生了什么事情，让他们把挖掘工作搞得一团糟，”她说道。 紧张吗？” 只是有点而已。与她相比，你的翅膀才刚刚长出来不久，所以在跨越这个阶段时，有经验丰富的人在身边确实会让人感到安心。至少，有人会在你犯下那些愚蠢的错误时，确保这些错误不会带来致命的后果。 我大部分的飞行时间都是和我的姐妹们一起编队飞行的，而不是独自飞行，”阿齐笑着回答，“我想这也说明我是个不错的团队成员吧？” 甚至可以说她是个优秀的领导者，因此她也不介意带领那些经验不如她的人，对吧？ 哦，别再花言巧语了；如果你想骗过我，就得用更巧妙的方式来讨好我。现在，注意听，在我们飞行的时候要紧跟着我。虽然这个洞穴很大，但活动空间却比在露天环境中要小得多。阿齐思考了一会儿，然后 [party.manyCompanions |转向 [comp2.name]与……进行了简短的交谈 [comp2.himHer] 你似乎没有完全理解我的意思。最终，她又将注意力重新集中在你身上，点了点头：“好了，我们可以出发了。 [comp2.name] 我会在这里等着，直到我们结束，然后我会回来把东西取走。 [comp2.himHer]哦？带过来不是更好吗？ [comp2.himHer] 是啊，但我们还不习惯一起把重物举到空中再运送吧——我以前和姐妹们一起练习过这种搬运方式，但还没和你一起试过。不过，等我们找到一条明确的运输路线后，第二次操作就会容易多了，也不用再为重量问题而烦恼了。 以及 互相照应吧。你让我在这里担任领导角色，所以你也可以跟着我的节奏来，对吧？” 一想到阿齐会跟着我的节奏行事，我就觉得 [comp2.name] 放在她的怀里”这个表达确实很适合用来描述这种场景。 [pc.isBimbo |轻声笑 |哼了一声 ] |她抿了抿嘴唇说道：“我觉得通过观察这些蒸汽喷口，我们不会再得到任何有用的信息了，而且时间也在一分一秒地流逝。你准备好了吗？” “好了，你已经准备得足够充分了。 ]好吧，那你就带路吧。” 这段路程确实有些艰难——Azzy一直在前方探路，而你则必须保持飞行状态，紧随她的步伐。有好几次，她都及时躲开了那些会将你们俩烤熟的蒸汽喷流，因此你们不得不在某个坚实的陆地上停下来，休息片刻，喘口气。 也许只是因为天气太热，也许空气中有什么特殊的东西，但你会觉得，在走过这些布满坑洞、湿软且摇摇欲坠的石头路段之后，自己感到疲惫的程度远远超出了应有的范围。 不过，最终你还是成功通过了难关，而你的黄蜂朋友也擦去了额头上的汗水。“呼！至少没有烟雾，只有水蒸气而已。 [party.manyCompanions |给我一点时间活动一下这些肌肉，然后我就回去继续做。 [comp2.name]你知道，阿齐就是那种活泼好动的人，但在再次开始行动之前，她或许应该好好休息一下，不要一直忙个不停。让她一个人去做所有的工作，而自己则留在后面休息吧。 [pc.isDK |这让你显得很糟糕，哈哈 |这是否让你感到有些内疚呢？ ]你肯定不希望自己的朋友因为她过度劳累而出什么事。 阿齐笑着摆了摆手部，表示不需要担心：“哦，别担心这个。我妈妈以前总是让我和我的姐妹们接待那些想见她的访客们。 我已经习惯了。但为了你……我还是会再休息一会儿，比原本计划的要久一些。 在黑暗中，你们俩静静地休息了几分钟，然后阿兹用脚后跟一蹬，消失在了黑暗中。 这段等待实在令人煎熬，但十分钟后，她终于随着上升的气流哼着歌回来了 [comp2.name] 被她抱在手部中时，那只小动物明显显得很不自在，但却不敢在你的同伴手部中扭动。它们俩重重地落在你身边，发出疲惫的声音，而阿齐则满意地拍掉手部上的灰尘。 “都搞定了！看吧，你之前根本没什么好担心的。” 安全总比后悔好，尤其是考虑到还有返程的路要走。当你的队伍重新聚集在安全的地方后，是时候看看这片矿区还能为你带来什么了…… |我想知道回程会是什么样子，但这当然取决于我们被派去取回的东西有多重，对吧？ 没错。既然你根本不知道会是什么东西，那么她就应该为可能发生的任何情况做好准备。 哦，别担心，”阿齐轻声说道，“我相信我们一定能一起解决这个问题。现在，如果你不介意的话，既然你一直这么强调这件事，我其实很想知道，我们究竟是为什么来到这里的。 你难道不感到兴奋吗？” 嘿，没必要急于一时——不过，至少我确实感到有些好奇。等到时机成熟的时候，你就会继续前进的…… ]
rows.raw: " Thankfully, you're not alone in being able to fly: Azzy buzzes over to your side as you survey the sinkhole-riddled cavern, peering out over the treacherous ground. "You have to wonder if the elves knew they were digging right above a steam bath like this, or if something happened to turn their dig into this mess," she remarks. "Nervous?" Just a little. You haven't had your wings very long compared to her, so it's reassuring to have someone more experienced at your side while making the crossing. At the very least, there'll be someone to make sure that any silly mistakes you make won't necessarily be fatal. "Most of my time flying was in formation with my sisters as opposed to being solo," Azzy replies with a chuckle. "I guess that makes me a good team player, huh?" A good leader, even, which is why she wouldn't mind taking point in guiding someone less experienced than her, right? "Oh, hush your silver tongue; you've to be a little more subtle in your flattery if you're to pull one over me. Now, pay attention, and stay close to me while we're in the air. The cavern may be large, but there's a lot less space to get around with than if we were under open skies." Azzy thinks a moment, then [party.manyCompanions |turns to [comp2.name], having a brief conversation with [comp2.himHer] that you don't quite make out. Eventually, she refocuses her attention on you and nods. "Okay, we're ready to go. [comp2.name] will wait here until we're over, and then I'll come back to fetch [comp2.himHer]." Oh? Wouldn't it be better to bring [comp2.himHer] along with you on the trip as well? Not only would you be able to share the load between yourselves, but you'd only have to make one trip to boot. "Yeah, but we aren't practised at carrying loads through the air together — I've practiced ferrying people with my sisters, but not with you. That, and the second time around will be easier when we've figured out a clear route instead of having to deal with the weight and watching out for each other. You made me the lead here, so you can follow along, can't you?" The thought of Azzy buzzing along with [comp2.name] in her arms does lend itself to a [pc.isBimbo |giggle |snort ] |thins her lips. "I don't think we can glean anything further from watching the steam geysers, and time's a-wasting. Are you ready?" Will do, you're as ready as you'll ever be ]. Very well, lead the way, then. It is a bit of a struggle — Azzy focuses on scouting out a path ahead, which leaves you to focus on staying aloft while following her lead. More than once she swerves away from a sudden plume of steam that would've cooked you both, and the both of you have to stop on an island of solid ground to rest for several moments and take a breather. Maybe it's just the heat, maybe it's something in the air, but you feel like you're tiring far easier than you ought to be for such a relatively short crossing over what's effectively a collection of pits and soaked, crumbling stone. Eventually, though, you make it over, and your hornet friend wipes the sweat from her brow. "Phew! At least there wasn't any smoke, just steam. [party.manyCompanions |Give me a bit to loosen up these muscles, and I'll go back for [comp2.name]." You know Azzy's the boisterous type, but maybe she should take more than just a bit for a breather before making the crossing again. Staying behind while she does all the work [pc.isDK |is making you look bad, aha |is weighing on your conscience a little ]. You'd rather not have something happen to your friends because she strained herself. Azzy laughs and waves off your concern. "Oh, don't worry about it. Mother had me and my sisters ferry all kinds of visitors who wanted audiences with her all the time. I'm used to it. But still, just for you... I'll take a break for just a bit longer than I'd intended." Several minutes pass in the darkness while the both of you catch your breaths, and then Azzy pushes off on her heels and buzzes off into the darkness. It's an agonizing wait, but ten minutes later she comes humming back over the updrafts with [comp2.name] in her hands, looking distinctly uncomfortable but not daring to squirm in your hornet companion's grasp. The two land by your side with a heavy, exhausted thump, and Azzy dusts off her hands with no small satisfaction. "All done! See, you were worried about nothing at all." Better safe than sorry, especially since there's a return trip involved. With your party re-assembled on safe footing, it's time to see what this side of the mines holds for you... |I wonder just what the return trip will be like, but that depends on how heavy what we've been sent to fetch will weigh, right?" Right. And since you have no idea as to what it might be, she ought to be prepared for just about any eventuality she can imagine. "Oh, don't you worry about it," Azzy purrs. "I'm sure we'll be able to handle it together. Now, if you don't mind, with you talking up this thing so much, I'm rather interested in seeing just what it is that we came all the way here for. Aren't you excited?" Hey, no need to rush things — but yes... there is a certain curiosity there, if nothing else. You'll move on when the time is ripe... ]"

rows.original: [party.hasCompanions |At length, [party.compNames] come[party.oneCompanion |s ] up to your side to join you in taking stock of what lies ahead. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn kiyoko viviane atugia quintillus |Cait purrs, then leans herself back against you with a lazy smile. "Looks like you're going to have to carry me across, then." It does look that way. She giggles. "[cait.maxThicc |Maybe I shouldn't have put on all that weight? Oh, I couldn't have seen something like this coming — I'm so sorry that I'm going to be quite literally dragging you down." Oh, you'll handle her quite fine. If valkyrie wings are capable of holding jotuns aloft, they're more than capable of keeping one chubby cat in the air |"You know, Calla and I dreamed of being able to fly when we were younger — it's one of the reasons she'd keep on climbing up to high places without considering how she'd get down afterwards. I didn't quite imagine back then that this is how I'd wind up sailing through the air. You won't drop me, will you?" Gods forbid! You'll keep a hold on her even if it means plummeting into the abyss by her side ]. Truth be told, you're more worried about keeping a firm grip on her mid-flight. Cait can be quite squishy when she has the mind to be. Your pink kitten just laughs and taps you with her tail. "Well! If you want a firm handhold or two on me, I've got some suggestions for places you could put your hands!" And cop a feel while at it? "Maybe, but not right now. We need you focused on the task at hand, right?" |After a while of quiet contemplation by your side, Brint gently elbows you and clears his throat. He's got that face he wears when he's thinking. A coin for what's on his mind, then? "Oh. I was just considering how you'd probably need to fly me over, and well..." Brint gestures at himself. "I do weigh quite a bit. That, and you might have trouble getting a good grip on someone as bulky as me." Is he saying that he'd rather stay behind on this side of the cavern? "I wouldn't mind, that's true. Stay behind and guard the rear, as it were — I'm not so full of myself to not realize that I wouldn't be a drag in this kind of situation. There shouldn't be much left ahead, according to the vision the bird gave you. Isn't that right?" Well, you don't want to give Nina the benefit of the doubt too early, either. That being said... if these wings can't bear the weight of a minotaur in addition to yours, you'll have made a poor deal for your soul, indeed. Happily, you know for a fact that there are jotun valkyries flapping around no problem, so he doesn't have to worry about it. You'd be more concerned about keeping a firm grip on him rather than your ability to keep the both of you aloft. Brint laughs at that. "Well, if that's your only problem, then how about I hold onto you instead of you holding onto me? That way, you don't have to worry about it." He's going to hold onto you with those big, strong arms of his? Oh no, whatever are you going to do? "All right, no need to get too excited, there'll be time for that after we're through here. But it's good to see you back in high spirits." |After a while of quiet contemplation by your side, Brienne gently elbows you and clears her throat. She's got that face she wears when she's worried. A coin for what's on his mind, then? "Oh. I was just considering how you'd probably need to fly me over, and well..." Brienne gestures at himself. "I do weigh quite a bit. That, and you might have trouble getting a good grip on someone as bulky as me. Not that I'd mind, but..." Is she saying that she'd rather stay behind on this side of the cavern? "I wouldn't like it, but I'd do it if you told me to. Stay behind and guard the rear, as it were — I'm not so full of myself to not realize that I wouldn't be a drag in this kind of situation. There shouldn't be much left ahead, according to the vision the bird gave you. Isn't that right?" Well, you don't want to give Nina the benefit of the doubt too early, either. That being said... if these wings can't bear the weight of a cowgirl in addition to yours, you'll have made a poor deal for your soul, indeed. Happily, you know for a fact that there are jotun valkyries flapping around no problem, so she doesn't have to worry about it. You'd be more concerned about keeping a firm grip on Brienne rather than your ability to keep the both of you aloft. She laughs at that. "Well, if that's your only problem, then how about I hold onto you instead of you holding onto me? That way, you don't have to worry about it." So long as she doesn't crush you in the bargain! You know from personal experience how tight her hold can be. "O-oh! I'll be sure to be careful, then." All right, there's no need to get too excited, there'll be time enough for that kind of thing after you're done here. That being said, seeing Brienne in high spirits does make you feel better yourself. | "Looks pretty nasty," Arona says, shielding her eyes out of sheer habit as she peers out even through you're deep underground. "I hear water below, though, lots of it. My grandma used to tell me tales of rivers and seas deep beneath the earth, huge bodies of water that never see the light from start to end — wonder what it'd be like to sail down one of those?" As tempting as it might be for her, you'd rather not have a very personal introduction to whatever river's flowing down there, given that there's steam escaping from the sinkholes. That, and she herself said it looked pretty nasty. Your orcish companion taps the side of her head with a finger. "Oh, yes. There's a difference between bravery and bravado — even I'm not stupid enough to try and fight darkness or steam. Don't drop me while we're out over the air, okay? Lumia herself gave you those wings, so if we go down it'll be all your fault." Knowing Arona, she won't let you tire mid-fight, anyway; she's just that kind of orc. "Damn right I am," she guffaws, clapping you on the shoulder. "Just being around me makes you all raring to go that bit further, doesn't it? Well, I won't let you down!" While you get the feeling that this is a little backwards considering that you're the one hefting Arona across the sinkholes, seeing her in such good spirits is undoubtedly going to take the edge off her weight and bulk. | "You're going to fly me across?" Ryn says as she comes up aside you and peers out into the darkness. "I guess you'll know what Harrick feels like when he comes up to me with a rabbit that's almost as big as he is." Whoa there. Did she just make a joke? [etheryn.lowConfidence |Ryn's expression falls immediately. "W-was it not funny? I'm sorry, I just... well, I was hoping to bring a little levity to the situation, given that you look so serious..." Damn right you look serious "Y-yes, but you've been that way s-since we entered..." That doesn't change one jot or tittle of what you said |Ryn smiles. "Yes, I did. Wasn't it funny?" It was, a little. But she's no helpless rabbit, or at least, not any more: if you're going to be carrying her across the cavern, it'll be because she gets into your arms, and not because you happened to scoop her up. There's an important difference there, one that she should've learned since leaving the Winter City for the first time. "I suppose, but I still think it's funny." Of course it is ]. Now, is there anything she's come across in the histories of her great-grandmother's time that might help in the crossing? "Not really. We've always known fire came close to the earth's surface in this part of the Frostwood, hence the Temple of Terrestrial Fire, but that was mostly under the purview of the religious and the druids kept their records in their temples." You see. Well, you'll just have to take things as they come, and it's a good thing that Ryn's quite light compared to other denizens of the Marches. Come to think of it, could Harrick help guide you across? He may not be made for spelunking, but another pair of eyes and wings would be a help regardless. Ryn thinks a moment, then nods and turns to her bird. Something passes between the two of them, and then she shakes him off her wrist and he flaps off into the darkness ahead; you wait for a couple of minutes before he returns, settling back on Ryn's wrist with an indignant squawk. "He didn't get very far, but that was enough to see the worst of it. Just follow him while you're carrying me over, okay?" Will do. She should let him know that his help's appreciated. |Pressing in at your side, Kiyoko rubs herself against you in that way that tells you all she wants to convey without saying a single word. All right, all right, you get it. Was there ever any doubt that you would be ferrying her across in the first place? "Who knows, beloved?" your fox-wife titters. [silly |"I've been secretly hiding the fact that I can twirl two of my tails and fly about like a helicopter all this while; it's just too undignified for me to ever do it, so I don't." What, really? "We've got to get some practical use out of all these tails aside from cushions and pillows. Do you ever wonder how we actually sit down with all this stuff attached to our butts? Maybe that's why we're all about cushions instead of chairs." |"Even if I didn't bring it up, I'm sure you were intending to do it all along. That's why I'm with you — you really are the thoughtful kind, hmm?" Someone else might be suspected of laying it on thickly, but Kiyoko is simply so earnest about it that it's hard to suspect her of flattery... or maybe that's the exact impression that she wants to put forward. ] So, does she have any input on the dangers ahead? "My homeland has plenty of places where the fire beneath the earth rises close to the surface. The scalding steam is dangerous enough on its own, but you have to be sure that you're not breathing anything bad — which can be difficult, because it often doesn't smell. There was a tale about a mountainside some centuries back where evil spirits were supposedly killing people along the roads, but as it turned out rents had opened up in the stone and were spilling toxic fumes all over the pathway below." You'll keep that in mind. |Viv clicks her tongue in annoyance, stifling a scowl and her eyes sweep the cavern from one end to the other. What's got her down? Two coppers for her thoughts. "One of the problems with enchanting is that once you've created the items, you've to bring them along with you for them to be of any use, and you can only bring along so many things while traveling, if you remember to grab them in the first place." She sighs. "I'm sure I've something at home that could easily solve this problem for all of us, but it's become more and more obvious ever since I started traveling with you — and without my home with me at all times — that the problem's made itself this clear." You've heard about bags and other containers which are bigger on the inside than on the outside. Would one of those help? "With carrying enchanted items around? Sure. But even those have their limits, and that doesn't solve the second part of the problem." Viv sighs. "Oh well. [silly |You can't run away from inventory issues in any RPG — it's a small mercy that the developers aren't forcing us to play inventory tetris with what space we have, that'd be just cruel |Even if I'd studied another school of the arcane arts more in-depth, I'm sure I'd run into problems as well. You can't be prepared for everything, I suppose ]." Well, that's what other people are for. Like you, for example. That bring a little good humor back to Viv. "Like you, yes. I'm sure you'll be holding me as tightly as I'll be holding you when we make our crossing, hmm? Even though I don't have anything that'll outright solve the problem for us, I'll see what I have in my current repertoire that might at least help us make it over in one piece. Can't let you do all the work, after all." Anything that she can pull out of her bag of tricks would be appreciated. | "Ohh, this one looks nasty," Atugia says as she surveys the cavern and sinkholes. "Not deadly nasty, but still pretty nasty. Reminds me of one of the trips that Carmen and I took some years back." Hmm. Does she have any pertinent advice? You're going to be flying her over, looks like. She smiles sheepishly and shrugs. "Sorry, can't tell you much, this sort of thing isn't really what I'm good at." Oh, she doesn't have to knock herself too badly — she's already helping you by being compact enough for you to get a good grip on her. Doesn't necessarily mean she's light, given that she's a powerful girl, but there's something to be said for not being bulky. "H-hey!" Even in the gloom, you spy Tui's cheeks color. "Teasin' me right now just ain't done — we're supposed to be all serious, it's dangerous around here..." And hence the need to keep morale up. You pat Tui on the shoulder, and tell her that it'll be all right — you don't doubt that she'll be holding onto you with those strong arms of hers as tightly as you'll be onto her. It's an exercise in trust, after all. "Ooh, that I know something about. Don't worry, yeah?" |Quin snorts at the sight, then shakes his head and steps away from the edge, even though it's clear that his feet are raring to go already. It takes a conscious act of will to deny what he instinctively and desperately wants to do... which should go to show what he really thinks of the matter. It's that bad, huh? "There's still this little voice in the back of my head that's saying it should be nothing to a taeleer," Quin replies with a rueful chuckle. "It's gotten me into trouble more than once now, so I take anything it says with a grain of salt... but that doesn't stop it from speaking up." Could he make it across? "Maybe. The ground's wet from all the steam that's coming up, I don't know if the air's safe to breathe, and the footing's apt to crumble... on the other hand, there're enough land bridges and footholds, and I ought to be able to recover from stuff shifting underfoot if I kept the possibility in mind. Still, it's easily enough of a stretch that I wouldn't want to risk it unless my life depended on it, which it doesn't." He smiles. "Without you, I'd decide that whatever's on the other side simply wouldn't be worth making the attempt to cross." Why, you're flattered. "You ought to be. After all, you're going to be sticking your fingers real close to this runner's body of mine. Isn't just anyone who gets that kind of privilege, you know." Oh, now he's getting cocky? Well then, he should hold on really tight during the crossing, because with how quick and nimble he is you might just have trouble holding onto him. A grin. "You bet my fingers will be deep inside of you, every step of the way. All right, are we going to make a move?" ] Once you figure that there's nothing more to be gleaned from watching and waiting, there's nothing for it. You instruct [comp1.name] to stand near the edge with [comp1.hisHer] arms slightly spread out, then take a few steps back before breaking into a sprint right for [comp1.himHer]. There's that moment of shuddering exhilaration as your bodies collide and pitch forward towards the steaming sinkholes, and then with a burst of effort your back, the both of you are aloft. [comp1.name] clutches at your forearms as tightly as you've got yours hooked under [comp1.hisHer] shoulders, and a couple of heart-wrenching flaps you settle into a steady rhythm under the added weight and press forward at a steady pace. The Lady of Light prevails in all things, and this is no exception. Not that it doesn't take effort, of course. Barely have you set out over the cavernous sinkholes that you're hit by the moist heat rising from within; it saps your strength and leaves you breathing harder that you ought to be. It's tempting to seek one of the several updrafts for additional lift, but thoughts of turbulence and more importantly, odorless yet deadly mine gases. More than once you swerve away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you clean, and thankfully there are several islands of rock that jut out from the darkness below that offer you respite during your crossing. There's little doubt about it: you're tiring far easier than you ought to be for such a relatively short crossing over what's effectively a collection of pits and soaked, crumbling stone. Eventually, though, you make it to the other side without incident; a shudder of relief runs through your body as you first set [comp1.name] down on solid ground, followed by your own heels striking the dirt. Wiping the sweat from your brow, you take in your new surroundings, and try not to think too hard about [party.manyCompanions |having to go back for [comp2.name] as well. Then there's the matter of the return trip, and whatever prize that Nina sent you here for will surely be added to the weight of everything you've to ferry across... |the return trip that you'll have to make with whatever Nina sent you here to get in tow ]... With great power comes great responsibility, after all. [party.manyCompanions |Once you've had a short rest, it's time to head back and collect [comp2.name]; the trip is easier this time given that you know where most of the obstacles already are, and can focus on keeping the both of yourself aloft. Thankfully, the trip is as uneventful as the first, and you make it to the other side unscathed despite the dangers. ]With everyone on this side of the cavern, it's time to take a closer look at just what warranted all this effort... |Well, it looks like you're all on your own for this. On the good side, you won't have to watch out for anyone else but yourself... but on the bad side, there won't be anyone to watch out for you. You'll have to be extra careful, since there'll be no one to save you if something happens during the crossing. With that thought in mind, you take a few steps back, break into a sprint, and leap out over the chasm while spreading your goddess-given wings. Barely have you set out over the cavernous sinkholes that you're hit by the moist heat rising from within; it saps your strength and leaves you breathing harder that you ought to be. It's tempting to seek one of the several updrafts for additional lift, but thoughts of turbulence and more importantly, odorless yet deadly mine gases. More than once you swerve away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you clean, and thankfully there are several islands of rock that jut out from the darkness below that offer you respite during your crossing. There's little doubt about it: you're tiring far easier than you ought to be for such a relatively short crossing over what's effectively a collection of pits and soaked, crumbling stone. Eventually, though, you make it to the other side without incident; a shudder of relief runs through your body as your heels touch upon solid ground and you breathe easier for it. Wiping the sweat from your brow, you take in your new surroundings, and try not to think too hard about the return trip that you'll have to make with whatever Nina sent you here to get in tow... ]

不止一次，你侥幸躲过了那些本会把你烤得干干净净的蒸汽喷流；幸运的是，在下方黑暗中，有几块岩石突了出来，为你在穿越过程中提供了暂时的庇护。毫无疑问，对于这样一段实际上只是由一些坑洞和湿软、正在崩解的石头组成的路线来说，你感到疲惫的程度远远超出了应有的范围。 然而，最终你还是顺利地到达了另一边；当你第一次踏上那里的土地时，一股如释重负的感觉瞬间涌上心头。 [comp1.name] [party.manyCompanions |稍作休息后，就该回去把东西取回来了。 [comp2.name]这一次，由于你已经知道了大部分障碍物的位置，所以旅途变得容易多了，你也可以专心致志地保持自己的平衡。幸运的是，这次旅途和第一次一样顺利，尽管途中充满了危险，但你还是平安无恙地到达了目的地。 ]既然洞穴这一侧的所有人都到齐了，是时候仔细看看究竟是什么事情值得我们付出这么大的努力了…… |看来这次你只能靠自己了。从好的方面来看，你只需要关心自己，不需要为别人着想……但坏处也是显而易见的，因为没有人会来照顾你。所以你必须格外小心，因为在穿越过程中如果发生了什么，根本没有人能够救你。 怀着这样的想法，你后退几步，突然加速奔跑，展开女神赐予你的翅膀，跳过了那道深渊。然而，当你刚刚飞越那些巨大的坑洞时，从地下升起的潮湿热气立刻袭击了你，它消耗着你的体力，使你的呼吸变得比平时更加急促。你很想借助那些上升气流来获得更多的升力，但一想到随之而来的湍流，以及那些无色无味却极其致命的矿井气体，你就放弃了这个念头。 不止一次，你险些被那些足以将你烤焦的蒸汽浪吞没；幸运的是，下方黑暗中耸立着几座岩石小岛，它们在你穿越这段由坑洞和湿软、摇摇欲坠的石头构成的区域时，为你提供了暂时的庇护。毫无疑问，对于这样一段相对短暂的旅程来说，你感到疲惫的程度远远超出了应有的范围。 然而，最终你还是顺利地到达了另一边；当你的足部后跟终于踩到坚实的地面时，一股如释重负的感觉涌上心头，呼吸也变得顺畅了许多。你擦去额头上的汗水，环顾四周，尽量不去想接下来还得带着尼娜派你来这里的那个东西，重新返回去的路…… ]
rows.raw: " [party.hasCompanions |At length, [party.compNames] come[party.oneCompanion |s ] up to your side to join you in taking stock of what lies ahead. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn kiyoko viviane atugia quintillus |Cait purrs, then leans herself back against you with a lazy smile. "Looks like you're going to have to carry me across, then." It does look that way. She giggles. "[cait.maxThicc |Maybe I shouldn't have put on all that weight? Oh, I couldn't have seen something like this coming — I'm so sorry that I'm going to be quite literally dragging you down." Oh, you'll handle her quite fine. If valkyrie wings are capable of holding jotuns aloft, they're more than capable of keeping one chubby cat in the air |"You know, Calla and I dreamed of being able to fly when we were younger — it's one of the reasons she'd keep on climbing up to high places without considering how she'd get down afterwards. I didn't quite imagine back then that this is how I'd wind up sailing through the air. You won't drop me, will you?" Gods forbid! You'll keep a hold on her even if it means plummeting into the abyss by her side ]. Truth be told, you're more worried about keeping a firm grip on her mid-flight. Cait can be quite squishy when she has the mind to be. Your pink kitten just laughs and taps you with her tail. "Well! If you want a firm handhold or two on me, I've got some suggestions for places you could put your hands!" And cop a feel while at it? "Maybe, but not right now. We need you focused on the task at hand, right?" |After a while of quiet contemplation by your side, Brint gently elbows you and clears his throat. He's got that face he wears when he's thinking. A coin for what's on his mind, then? "Oh. I was just considering how you'd probably need to fly me over, and well..." Brint gestures at himself. "I do weigh quite a bit. That, and you might have trouble getting a good grip on someone as bulky as me." Is he saying that he'd rather stay behind on this side of the cavern? "I wouldn't mind, that's true. Stay behind and guard the rear, as it were — I'm not so full of myself to not realize that I wouldn't be a drag in this kind of situation. There shouldn't be much left ahead, according to the vision the bird gave you. Isn't that right?" Well, you don't want to give Nina the benefit of the doubt too early, either. That being said... if these wings can't bear the weight of a minotaur in addition to yours, you'll have made a poor deal for your soul, indeed. Happily, you know for a fact that there are jotun valkyries flapping around no problem, so he doesn't have to worry about it. You'd be more concerned about keeping a firm grip on him rather than your ability to keep the both of you aloft. Brint laughs at that. "Well, if that's your only problem, then how about I hold onto you instead of you holding onto me? That way, you don't have to worry about it." He's going to hold onto you with those big, strong arms of his? Oh no, whatever are you going to do? "All right, no need to get too excited, there'll be time for that after we're through here. But it's good to see you back in high spirits." |After a while of quiet contemplation by your side, Brienne gently elbows you and clears her throat. She's got that face she wears when she's worried. A coin for what's on his mind, then? "Oh. I was just considering how you'd probably need to fly me over, and well..." Brienne gestures at himself. "I do weigh quite a bit. That, and you might have trouble getting a good grip on someone as bulky as me. Not that I'd mind, but..." Is she saying that she'd rather stay behind on this side of the cavern? "I wouldn't like it, but I'd do it if you told me to. Stay behind and guard the rear, as it were — I'm not so full of myself to not realize that I wouldn't be a drag in this kind of situation. There shouldn't be much left ahead, according to the vision the bird gave you. Isn't that right?" Well, you don't want to give Nina the benefit of the doubt too early, either. That being said... if these wings can't bear the weight of a cowgirl in addition to yours, you'll have made a poor deal for your soul, indeed. Happily, you know for a fact that there are jotun valkyries flapping around no problem, so she doesn't have to worry about it. You'd be more concerned about keeping a firm grip on Brienne rather than your ability to keep the both of you aloft. She laughs at that. "Well, if that's your only problem, then how about I hold onto you instead of you holding onto me? That way, you don't have to worry about it." So long as she doesn't crush you in the bargain! You know from personal experience how tight her hold can be. "O-oh! I'll be sure to be careful, then." All right, there's no need to get too excited, there'll be time enough for that kind of thing after you're done here. That being said, seeing Brienne in high spirits does make you feel better yourself. | "Looks pretty nasty," Arona says, shielding her eyes out of sheer habit as she peers out even through you're deep underground. "I hear water below, though, lots of it. My grandma used to tell me tales of rivers and seas deep beneath the earth, huge bodies of water that never see the light from start to end — wonder what it'd be like to sail down one of those?" As tempting as it might be for her, you'd rather not have a very personal introduction to whatever river's flowing down there, given that there's steam escaping from the sinkholes. That, and she herself said it looked pretty nasty. Your orcish companion taps the side of her head with a finger. "Oh, yes. There's a difference between bravery and bravado — even I'm not stupid enough to try and fight darkness or steam. Don't drop me while we're out over the air, okay? Lumia herself gave you those wings, so if we go down it'll be all your fault." Knowing Arona, she won't let you tire mid-fight, anyway; she's just that kind of orc. "Damn right I am," she guffaws, clapping you on the shoulder. "Just being around me makes you all raring to go that bit further, doesn't it? Well, I won't let you down!" While you get the feeling that this is a little backwards considering that you're the one hefting Arona across the sinkholes, seeing her in such good spirits is undoubtedly going to take the edge off her weight and bulk. | "You're going to fly me across?" Ryn says as she comes up aside you and peers out into the darkness. "I guess you'll know what Harrick feels like when he comes up to me with a rabbit that's almost as big as he is." Whoa there. Did she just make a joke? [etheryn.lowConfidence |Ryn's expression falls immediately. "W-was it not funny? I'm sorry, I just... well, I was hoping to bring a little levity to the situation, given that you look so serious..." Damn right you look serious "Y-yes, but you've been that way s-since we entered..." That doesn't change one jot or tittle of what you said |Ryn smiles. "Yes, I did. Wasn't it funny?" It was, a little. But she's no helpless rabbit, or at least, not any more: if you're going to be carrying her across the cavern, it'll be because she gets into your arms, and not because you happened to scoop her up. There's an important difference there, one that she should've learned since leaving the Winter City for the first time. "I suppose, but I still think it's funny." Of course it is ]. Now, is there anything she's come across in the histories of her great-grandmother's time that might help in the crossing? "Not really. We've always known fire came close to the earth's surface in this part of the Frostwood, hence the Temple of Terrestrial Fire, but that was mostly under the purview of the religious and the druids kept their records in their temples." You see. Well, you'll just have to take things as they come, and it's a good thing that Ryn's quite light compared to other denizens of the Marches. Come to think of it, could Harrick help guide you across? He may not be made for spelunking, but another pair of eyes and wings would be a help regardless. Ryn thinks a moment, then nods and turns to her bird. Something passes between the two of them, and then she shakes him off her wrist and he flaps off into the darkness ahead; you wait for a couple of minutes before he returns, settling back on Ryn's wrist with an indignant squawk. "He didn't get very far, but that was enough to see the worst of it. Just follow him while you're carrying me over, okay?" Will do. She should let him know that his help's appreciated. |Pressing in at your side, Kiyoko rubs herself against you in that way that tells you all she wants to convey without saying a single word. All right, all right, you get it. Was there ever any doubt that you would be ferrying her across in the first place? "Who knows, beloved?" your fox-wife titters. [silly |"I've been secretly hiding the fact that I can twirl two of my tails and fly about like a helicopter all this while; it's just too undignified for me to ever do it, so I don't." What, really? "We've got to get some practical use out of all these tails aside from cushions and pillows. Do you ever wonder how we actually sit down with all this stuff attached to our butts? Maybe that's why we're all about cushions instead of chairs." |"Even if I didn't bring it up, I'm sure you were intending to do it all along. That's why I'm with you — you really are the thoughtful kind, hmm?" Someone else might be suspected of laying it on thickly, but Kiyoko is simply so earnest about it that it's hard to suspect her of flattery... or maybe that's the exact impression that she wants to put forward. ] So, does she have any input on the dangers ahead? "My homeland has plenty of places where the fire beneath the earth rises close to the surface. The scalding steam is dangerous enough on its own, but you have to be sure that you're not breathing anything bad — which can be difficult, because it often doesn't smell. There was a tale about a mountainside some centuries back where evil spirits were supposedly killing people along the roads, but as it turned out rents had opened up in the stone and were spilling toxic fumes all over the pathway below." You'll keep that in mind. |Viv clicks her tongue in annoyance, stifling a scowl and her eyes sweep the cavern from one end to the other. What's got her down? Two coppers for her thoughts. "One of the problems with enchanting is that once you've created the items, you've to bring them along with you for them to be of any use, and you can only bring along so many things while traveling, if you remember to grab them in the first place." She sighs. "I'm sure I've something at home that could easily solve this problem for all of us, but it's become more and more obvious ever since I started traveling with you — and without my home with me at all times — that the problem's made itself this clear." You've heard about bags and other containers which are bigger on the inside than on the outside. Would one of those help? "With carrying enchanted items around? Sure. But even those have their limits, and that doesn't solve the second part of the problem." Viv sighs. "Oh well. [silly |You can't run away from inventory issues in any RPG — it's a small mercy that the developers aren't forcing us to play inventory tetris with what space we have, that'd be just cruel |Even if I'd studied another school of the arcane arts more in-depth, I'm sure I'd run into problems as well. You can't be prepared for everything, I suppose ]." Well, that's what other people are for. Like you, for example. That bring a little good humor back to Viv. "Like you, yes. I'm sure you'll be holding me as tightly as I'll be holding you when we make our crossing, hmm? Even though I don't have anything that'll outright solve the problem for us, I'll see what I have in my current repertoire that might at least help us make it over in one piece. Can't let you do all the work, after all." Anything that she can pull out of her bag of tricks would be appreciated. | "Ohh, this one looks nasty," Atugia says as she surveys the cavern and sinkholes. "Not deadly nasty, but still pretty nasty. Reminds me of one of the trips that Carmen and I took some years back." Hmm. Does she have any pertinent advice? You're going to be flying her over, looks like. She smiles sheepishly and shrugs. "Sorry, can't tell you much, this sort of thing isn't really what I'm good at." Oh, she doesn't have to knock herself too badly — she's already helping you by being compact enough for you to get a good grip on her. Doesn't necessarily mean she's light, given that she's a powerful girl, but there's something to be said for not being bulky. "H-hey!" Even in the gloom, you spy Tui's cheeks color. "Teasin' me right now just ain't done — we're supposed to be all serious, it's dangerous around here..." And hence the need to keep morale up. You pat Tui on the shoulder, and tell her that it'll be all right — you don't doubt that she'll be holding onto you with those strong arms of hers as tightly as you'll be onto her. It's an exercise in trust, after all. "Ooh, that I know something about. Don't worry, yeah?" |Quin snorts at the sight, then shakes his head and steps away from the edge, even though it's clear that his feet are raring to go already. It takes a conscious act of will to deny what he instinctively and desperately wants to do... which should go to show what he really thinks of the matter. It's that bad, huh? "There's still this little voice in the back of my head that's saying it should be nothing to a taeleer," Quin replies with a rueful chuckle. "It's gotten me into trouble more than once now, so I take anything it says with a grain of salt... but that doesn't stop it from speaking up." Could he make it across? "Maybe. The ground's wet from all the steam that's coming up, I don't know if the air's safe to breathe, and the footing's apt to crumble... on the other hand, there're enough land bridges and footholds, and I ought to be able to recover from stuff shifting underfoot if I kept the possibility in mind. Still, it's easily enough of a stretch that I wouldn't want to risk it unless my life depended on it, which it doesn't." He smiles. "Without you, I'd decide that whatever's on the other side simply wouldn't be worth making the attempt to cross." Why, you're flattered. "You ought to be. After all, you're going to be sticking your fingers real close to this runner's body of mine. Isn't just anyone who gets that kind of privilege, you know." Oh, now he's getting cocky? Well then, he should hold on really tight during the crossing, because with how quick and nimble he is you might just have trouble holding onto him. A grin. "You bet my fingers will be deep inside of you, every step of the way. All right, are we going to make a move?" ] Once you figure that there's nothing more to be gleaned from watching and waiting, there's nothing for it. You instruct [comp1.name] to stand near the edge with [comp1.hisHer] arms slightly spread out, then take a few steps back before breaking into a sprint right for [comp1.himHer]. There's that moment of shuddering exhilaration as your bodies collide and pitch forward towards the steaming sinkholes, and then with a burst of effort your back, the both of you are aloft. [comp1.name] clutches at your forearms as tightly as you've got yours hooked under [comp1.hisHer] shoulders, and a couple of heart-wrenching flaps you settle into a steady rhythm under the added weight and press forward at a steady pace. The Lady of Light prevails in all things, and this is no exception. Not that it doesn't take effort, of course. Barely have you set out over the cavernous sinkholes that you're hit by the moist heat rising from within; it saps your strength and leaves you breathing harder that you ought to be. It's tempting to seek one of the several updrafts for additional lift, but thoughts of turbulence and more importantly, odorless yet deadly mine gases. More than once you swerve away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you clean, and thankfully there are several islands of rock that jut out from the darkness below that offer you respite during your crossing. There's little doubt about it: you're tiring far easier than you ought to be for such a relatively short crossing over what's effectively a collection of pits and soaked, crumbling stone. Eventually, though, you make it to the other side without incident; a shudder of relief runs through your body as you first set [comp1.name] down on solid ground, followed by your own heels striking the dirt. Wiping the sweat from your brow, you take in your new surroundings, and try not to think too hard about [party.manyCompanions |having to go back for [comp2.name] as well. Then there's the matter of the return trip, and whatever prize that Nina sent you here for will surely be added to the weight of everything you've to ferry across... |the return trip that you'll have to make with whatever Nina sent you here to get in tow ]... With great power comes great responsibility, after all. [party.manyCompanions |Once you've had a short rest, it's time to head back and collect [comp2.name]; the trip is easier this time given that you know where most of the obstacles already are, and can focus on keeping the both of yourself aloft. Thankfully, the trip is as uneventful as the first, and you make it to the other side unscathed despite the dangers. ]With everyone on this side of the cavern, it's time to take a closer look at just what warranted all this effort... |Well, it looks like you're all on your own for this. On the good side, you won't have to watch out for anyone else but yourself... but on the bad side, there won't be anyone to watch out for you. You'll have to be extra careful, since there'll be no one to save you if something happens during the crossing. With that thought in mind, you take a few steps back, break into a sprint, and leap out over the chasm while spreading your goddess-given wings. Barely have you set out over the cavernous sinkholes that you're hit by the moist heat rising from within; it saps your strength and leaves you breathing harder that you ought to be. It's tempting to seek one of the several updrafts for additional lift, but thoughts of turbulence and more importantly, odorless yet deadly mine gases. More than once you swerve away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you clean, and thankfully there are several islands of rock that jut out from the darkness below that offer you respite during your crossing. There's little doubt about it: you're tiring far easier than you ought to be for such a relatively short crossing over what's effectively a collection of pits and soaked, crumbling stone. Eventually, though, you make it to the other side without incident; a shudder of relief runs through your body as your heels touch upon solid ground and you breathe easier for it. Wiping the sweat from your brow, you take in your new surroundings, and try not to think too hard about the return trip that you'll have to make with whatever Nina sent you here to get in tow... ]"

rows.original: You stop at the edge of the first large sinkhole, pondering your options. The easiest way to get across would be to have someone experienced fly you over — assuming that you brought someone with you who fits the bill, of course. [pc.hasWings |You may have wings of your own, but trusting them under these treacherous conditions would probably be more dangerous than not using them |Besides, just having wings doesn't guarantee success and safety ]. She did say misstep and perish... but that doesn't necessarily mean that not stepping at all to begin with means that one won't perish.[pc.bg acolyte | You should know — when it comes to prophecies, visions and the like, the specific wording is pretty important. ] That being said, one's footing isn't the only peril to be had here. The constant updraft rising from the sinkholes, accompanied by the occasional bust of steam, promises to make your crossing all the more troublesome. The sound of rushing water comes from deep within the sinkholes, and while it might conceivably cushion a fall there's no telling where you might be swept to, or if there's even anything breathable down there. All in all, though, dancing one's way through the damp crossings, steam plumes and rushing air is just asking for trouble; making the crossing unaided would be immensely stupid. There's no rush, though — there's nothing stopping you from heading back out and getting who or what you need to cross this treacherous terrain. So, what'll it be?
rows.translation: 你停在了第一个大型天坑的边缘，仔细思考着该怎么做。最简单的办法就是让有经验的人带你飞过去——当然，前提是你身边有合适的人选。 [pc.hasWings |你或许拥有自己的翅膀，但在这种危险的环境中依赖它们，可能会比不使用它们更加危险。 |此外，仅仅拥有翅膀并不能保证成功与安全。 ]她确实说过“犯错就会灭亡”……但这也并不一定意味着什么。 不是 首先，采取任何行动就意味着某人 不会 灭亡吧。[pc.bg acolyte | 你应该明白——在预言、幻象这类事情上，具体的表述方式是非常重要的。 ] 话虽如此，但在这里，稳定的立足点并不是唯一需要面对的危险。从天坑中不断升起的上升气流，再加上偶尔冒出的蒸汽，一定会让你的穿越过程变得更加艰难。从天坑深处传来的湍急水流声虽然可能在一定程度上减轻坠落的冲击，但谁也无法预料自己会被冲到哪里去，更不知道那里是否还有可供呼吸的空气。 不过，总的来说，在潮湿的路口、蒸腾的雾气和湍急的空气中跳舞，无异于自寻麻烦；如果不借助任何帮助就试图穿过这些地方，那简直太愚蠢了。不过也不必着急——你完全可以回头去获取所需的帮助或工具，然后再尝试穿越这片危险的地带。 那么，你想要什么呢？

rows.original: Hey, she's capable of it, isn't she? That, and the steam coming up from beneath won't bother her in the least, aside from a little dampness. Agni looks between you and the multiple sinkholes that riddle the chamber, the occasional plume of scalding steam geysering out in a thick plume before dissipating. "Hmm, I don't know about that." Well, what you do know is that harpies are well-known for grabbing people, picking them up right off the ground, and dashing them on the rocks below. By the same extent, a fine specimen of harpy-ness like Agni could most certainly fly [party.som | |you over to the other side |you and [comp2.name] over to the other side one at a time ], couldn't she? Or is she saying that she isn't up to a task that even her feathery cumrags of juniors are more than capable of? "Hey, if you're trying to provoke me into some kind of action in order to prove myself, you're going about it the wrong way.[pc.isDK |" | And no, I know you're teasing me, but that smile of yours isn't going to get you out of everything, you know." It's certainly worked up till now. ] Agni sighs, then stares out over the cavern once more, her eyes rolling over the scene from wall to wall. You help her point out where you think the worst of the updrafts will be, and the patterns you notice with regards to the steam geysers — they actually are quite regular in firing off, now that you're paying attention to them. "Think the elves knew what they had bubbling under them all the time while digging for ore?" Perhaps? The temple of terrestrial fire isn't too far off, after all. There's a lot of fire under the surface of this cold bog. Now, if she doesn't mind... "All right, all right. Seriously, I think you just want to feel my thighs about you, hmm?" It's a nice side benefit, to be sure. Agni rolls her eyes as you flash her a grin, then pushes off in earnest, breaking into a sprint and lunging for you. The extra effort has her flapping and squawking in complaint, but before you know it her legs wrap about your neck and shoulders, talon-tips prodding at your belly. A grunt of effort, and she lifts your feet clean off the ground to start the perilous crossing together. "Gods, you're heavy for your size," Agni mutters. "Ever considered losing some weight?"

rows.original: It is a bit of a struggle — Agni has to focus on keeping the both of you aloft, which leaves you to spot obstacles in time to prevent her from running face-first into them. More than once she swerves away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you even if she's largely impervious to heat, and you have to stop on an island of solid ground to rest for several moments while Agni takes a breather and refreshes herself for the rest of the crossing. Eventually, though, you make it over, and Agni wipes the sweat from her brow [party.manyCompanions |[party.has azyrran |before heaving a big sigh. "Phew, that was something. At least Azyrran has wings of her own, so I don't have to —" Actually she ought to make the crossing a second time, to guide Azzy over if nothing else. Agni stares at you in a mixture of disbelief and disgust, then claps her forehead and starts laughing dryly to herself. "We-ll, can't argue with that. Give me a little time to have a breather before I head on back, though. That being said... if you had the both of us around, why didn't you ask us to carry you together? At least each of us would only have to carry half the weight." And you'd need thrice the coordination — not just between you and Agni, but between Azzy and you, as well as Agni and Azzy. If the two of you were able to make the forward crossing on your own, then many hands doesn't necessarily mean light work. The two ladies aren't practised at sharing loads mid-air, especially given that arm-wings versus back-wings necessarily mean different styles of fight, and you have no desire to find out personally what the bottom of the sinkhole is like. "Ugh, that makes sense, but it still feels like you're making excuses for something you should've thought of earlier." Now, now. That's the exhaustion speaking. She'll have plenty of time to rest up and then bring Azzy over, there's no rush while you make sure that this side of the sinkhole-dotted cavern is safe. And that's what happens. After ten minutes or so of rest, Agni goes flapping back over the updrafts and returns shortly with Azzy buzzing along behind her; the latter looks considerably more put out by the hot damp than your phoenix companion is, but doesn't complain as the both of them touch down on solid ground. With your party re-assembled on safe footing, it's time to see what this side of the mines holds for you... |before heaving a big sigh. "Phew, that was something. I still have to go back to bring [comp2.name] over, don't I?" If she doesn't mind. She's the only one in this party to have the functionality and experience with wings to make the haul, after all. "We-ll, can't argue with that; I should have seen it coming myself. Give me a little time to have a breather before I head on back, though, won't you?" No worries. She should take a breather before making the crossing again, though; she'll have plenty of time to rest up and then bring [comp2.name] over, there's no rush while you make sure that this side of the sinkhole-dotted cavern is safe. You don't want anything happening to either of them while in flight. "Trust me, I don't want that, either. All right, give me a moment." And a moment is what she needs. After ten minutes or so of rest, Agni goes flapping back over the updrafts and returns shortly with [comp2.name] between her knees and thighs, looking a bit uncomfortable but not daring to squirm; the two land by your side with a heavy, exhausted thump and Agni breathes a huge sigh of relief. There, there. With your party re-assembled on safe footing, it's time to see what this side of the mines holds for you... ] |. "Phew. That was quite the steamy affair." Well, she's still in the mood to joke around, so she presumably still has the strength to go on without a rest. "H-hey, I didn't say that! Give me a moment to catch my breath, okay? Gods, to think that you'll weigh even more on the return trip..." Hah, yeah. Maybe she should indeed catch her breath before you head off to see what this side of the mines holds for you... ]
rows.translation: 这确实有点棘手部——Agni必须专注于让你们俩保持悬浮状态，因此你就需要及时发现前方的障碍物，以免她直接撞上它们。有好几次，她都成功躲过了那些会烫伤你们的蒸汽喷发；尽管她对高温基本上毫无反应，但你还是不得不在某个坚实的陆地上停下来休息片刻，让Agni也有机会喘口气、恢复精力，以便继续完成这段旅程。 然而，最终你还是成功克服了困难，而阿格尼则帮她擦去了额头上的汗水。 [party.manyCompanions |[party.has azyrran |在他长叹一声之后，说道：“呼，真是够呛的。至少阿兹兰有自己的翅膀，所以我不用——” 其实，她至少应该再过一次河，至少也要引导阿兹兰过去才行。 阿格尼用难以置信又充满厌恶的眼神盯着你，然后拍了拍自己的额头，开始干笑起来。“嗯，这个确实无可争辩。不过，在我回去之前，给我一点时间喘口气吧。 话虽如此……既然有我们两个人在，你为什么不让我们一起帮你搬运呢？这样至少我们每个人只需要承担一半的重量。 而且这样一来，所需的协调性也会增加三倍——不仅仅是你和阿格尼之间的协调，还有你和阿齐之间的协调，以及阿格尼和阿齐之间的协调。 如果你们两个人能够自己完成那次前向穿越，那么多人帮忙并不一定意味着工作会变得轻松。这两位女士并不擅长在半空中共同分担负担，尤其是考虑到使用前臂翅膀与使用后臂翅膀必然意味着不同的战斗风格，而你们肯定也不想亲自去体验那些“无底洞”的底部究竟是什么样子的。 呃，这么说也有道理，但还是 感觉起来…… 感觉你像是在为一些本应该提前考虑到的事情找借口。” “好了好了，肯定是太累了才会这么说。她以后有的是时间休息，等确认这个布满天坑的洞穴区域是安全的之后，再把阿齐带过来也没关系。 事情就是这样。在休息了大约十分钟后，阿格尼重新振翅飞向上升气流，不久之后便带着嗡嗡作响的阿齐回到了地面；与她那火凤凰般的伙伴相比，阿齐显然更受炎热潮湿空气的影响，但它并没有抱怨，当它们俩最终降落在坚实的地面上时，阿齐依然没有发出任何声音。 当你的队伍重新集结在安全的地方后，是时候去看看这片矿区里还有什么等着你了…… |在他长叹一声之后，说道：“呼，真是够呛的。我还是得回去把那些东西拿回来。 [comp2.name] 好了，不是吗？” 如果她不介意的话……毕竟，在这个团队里，只有她具备使用翅膀进行长途飞行的能力和相关经验。 “嗯，这一点确实无可争议；我早该预料到会这样。 给我一点时间，让我喘口气再回去，好吗？” “没关系。不过，在再次过河之前，她确实应该休息一下；她有足够的时间来休息，然后再继续前进。 [comp2.name] 放心，我也不希望发生那种事。好吧，给我一点时间。” 而她确实需要一点时间。休息了大约十分钟后，阿格尼重新振翅飞向上升气流，不久之后就回来了。 [comp2.name] 她的膝盖和大腿之间，看起来有些不舒服，但却不敢扭动；那两个东西重重地落在你身边，发出沉闷的声音，阿格尼也长舒了一口气。 好了，好了。现在你的队伍已经重新聚集在安全的地方，是时候看看矿井的这一侧还能为你带来什么了…… ] |呼，刚才真是够激烈的啊。” 嗯，她现在还愿意开玩笑，看来她应该还有足够的精力继续下去吧。 “喂，我可没那么说！给我点时间喘口气，好吗？天啊，想想看，回去的路上你的体重肯定还会再增加一些……” 哈哈，没错。也许在你继续探索矿井的这一侧之前，她确实应该先喘口气才行…… ]

rows.translation: 让阿格尼带你飞过去吧。

rows.original:
Hey, she's capable of it, isn't she? That, and the steam coming up from beneath won't bother her in the least, aside from a little dampness.

        Azzy looks between you and the multiple sinkholes that riddle the chamber, the occasional plume of scalding steam geysering out in a thick plume before dissipating. "Hmm, I don't doubt my strength. What I'm worried about is you doing something silly while we're in the air. Don't squirm about too much, okay?"
        
        With those strong arms of hers wrapped about you? Oh, that's a big ask, but since it's coming from her you'll be more than happy to oblige.
        
        A chuckle. "There's a good [pc.mf
            |boy
            |girl
        ]. Come on, then — let's not waste any more time."
        
        Now, there's no need to rush things. This could be quite the perilous journey, and you have no desire to find out firsthand what the bottom of a sinkhole looks like, or how it feels to be hit with scalding steam. Azzy sighs, then stares out over the cavern once more, her eyes rolling over the scene from wall to wall. You help her point out where you think the worst of the updrafts will be, and the patterns you notice with regards to the steam geysers — they actually are quite regular in firing off, now that you're paying attention to them.
        
        "Think the elves knew what they had bubbling under them all the time while digging for ore?"
        
        Perhaps? The temple of terrestrial fire isn't too far off, after all. There's a lot of fire under the surface of this cold bog.
        
        "Doesn't look too bad, really. Now, if you don't mind, let's get this over with already."
        
        All right, all right. Azzy takes a few steps back, breaks into a sprint, and uses the running start to hook her arms under yours and lift you clean off your feet. Her insect wings strain for a moment while she gets used to your weight, then settle into a steady rhythm as you start off over the sinkholes.

More than once she swerves away from a plume of steam that would've cooked you mid-air, and you have to stop on an island of solid ground to rest for several moments while she takes a breather and refreshes herself for the rest of the crossing. Eventually, though, you make it over, and Azzy wipes the sweat from her brow. "Phew, that was more tiring than I'd imagined; we used to fly people to and from the hive all the time without problems. Wonder if it's because of the heat?" Well, she'd better rest up before [party.manyCompanions |[party.has agnimitra |returning to guide Agni across as well. The phoenix may have wings of her own, but the updrafts and steam plumes do make for a treacherous crossing. Despite being clearly worn out, Azzy smiles and straightens her back. "Sure thing, it'll take more than a little turbulence to take a hive knight out of commission." Of course. You don't doubt her strength, but she still should take a little time to work some life into those muscles of hers before heading on back, though. "That being said..." Yes? "If you had the both of us around, why didn't you ask us to carry you together? At least each of us would only have to carry half the weight, and we'd only need to make one trip." And you'd need thrice the coordination — not just between you and Agni, but between Azzy and you, as well as Agni and Azzy. "That shouldn't be an issue, my sisters and I used to fly people to and from the hive all the time, anywhere from two to four hive knights to one passenger." That's true, but she's used to working with her sisters on ferrying people and items through the air, not with Agni. If she and you were able to make the forward crossing on your own, then many hands doesn't necessarily mean light work. The two ladies aren't practised at sharing loads mid-air, especially given that arm-wings versus back-wings necessarily mean different styles of fight, and you have no desire to wager your safety on a sudden, impromptu exercise. Not to worry, you've noted all the work she's doing now and will make it up to her later. A chuckle. "I'll hold you to that promise. It still feels like you're making excuses for something you should've thought of earlier, though." Hey, if she's going to take that tack, she didn't think of it, either. "Well, I can't deny that. All right, I think that's enough rest — off I go, then!" And that's what happens. After ten minutes or so of rest, Azzy goes flapping back over the updrafts and returns shortly with Agni flapping along behind her; the latter looks considerably less put out by the hot damp than Azzy is, but you note that she isn't unscathed as the both of them touch down on solid ground. With your party re-assembled on safe footing, it's time to see what this side of the mines holds for you... |returning for [comp2.name]. She's the only one in this party to have the functionality and experience with wings to make the haul, after all, and you'd rather not have something happen to your friends because she strained herself. Azzy laughs and waves off your concern. "Oh, don't worry about it. Mother had me and my sisters ferry all kinds of visitors who wanted audiences with her all the time. I'm used to it." Before you can protest, she's pushed off on her heels and buzzed off into the darkness. It's an agonizing wait, but ten minutes later Azzy comes humming back over the updrafts with [comp2.name] in her hands, looking distinctly uncomfortable but not daring to squirm. The two land by your side with a heavy, exhausted thump, and Azzy dusts off her hands with no small satisfaction. "All done! See, you were worried about nothing at all." All right, she wins this one. With your party re-assembled on safe footing, it's time to see what this side of the mines holds for you... ] |the return trip — you'll be weighing even more with whatever it is that you're here to fetch. "Oh, don't you worry about it," Azzy purrs. "I'll be able to handle both it and you. Now, if you don't mind, I'm rather interested in seeing just what it is that we came all the way here to get. Aren't you excited?" Hey, no need to rush things — you don't know what lies ahead. But yes... there is a certain curiosity there, if nothing else. Time to move on, then... ]
rows.translation: 即使对于像阿齐这样体格强健的人来说，这也是一件相当困难的事情——她必须全力保持你们两人的平衡，这样才能让你及时发现前方的障碍物，避免她直接撞上去。不止一次，她都成功地躲过了那些会在半空中将你们烧成灰烬的蒸汽喷流；而你也必须偶尔在某个坚实的陆地上停下来休息片刻，让她有机会喘口气、恢复体力，以便继续完成这段旅程。 不过，最终你还是成功完成了任务，阿齐擦了擦额头上的汗水，说道：“呼，这可比我想象中要累得多啊；我们以前经常运送人们往返于蜂巢之间，从来都没有遇到过任何问题。不知道是不是因为天气太热的原因呢？嗯，她最好先休息一下再 [party.manyCompanions |[party.has agnimitra |也需要回来引导阿格尼穿过这些区域。凤凰虽然拥有自己的翅膀，但上升气流和蒸汽柱确实会使得穿越变得极其危险。 尽管明显已经精疲力竭，阿齐还是微笑着挺直了身子。“当然，想要让一位蜂巢骑士失去行动能力，仅仅是一些湍流是远远不够的。 当然。你并不怀疑她的实力，但在她再次出发之前，还是应该花些时间来锻炼那些肌肉，让它们变得更加结实一些。 “话虽如此……” 嗯？ 如果你有我们两个人在身边，为什么不让我们一起帮你搬运呢？这样我们每个人只需要承担一半的重量，而且只需要往返一次就可以了。” 不过这样一来，就需要三倍的协调能力——不仅是你和阿格尼之间的协调，还有你和阿齐之间的协调，以及阿格尼和阿齐之间的协调。 那应该不是问题，我和我的姐妹们以前经常负责运送人们往返于蜂巢之间，每次通常会有两到四名蜂巢骑士陪同一名乘客。 如果她和你能独自完成那次前冲穿越动作，那么人多并不一定意味着工作会变得轻松。这两位女士并不擅长在空中共同分担负担，尤其是考虑到使用前臂翅膀与使用后臂翅膀所带来的战斗风格差异，你肯定也不愿意将自己的安全押在这样一次即兴的练习上。 别担心，你已经注意到了她现在所做的一切，以后一定会补偿她的。 一阵轻笑。“我会遵守那个承诺的。这件事仍然 感觉起来…… 就好像你在为一些本应该早点想到的事情找借口一样。” “嘿，如果她也要采取这种态度的话，那说明她其实也没想到这些事情。” “嗯，这一点我确实无法否认。 好吧，我想休息的时间已经够了——那我就出发吧！” 果然，大约休息了十分钟后，Azzy重新振翅飞向上升气流，不久之后就带着Agni回到了地面；与Azzy相比，Agni似乎并没有受到那么大的影响，但当它们俩降落在坚实的地面上时，你还是会发现她并没有毫发无损。 当你的队伍重新集结在安全的地方后，是时候去看看这片矿区里还有什么等着你了…… |返回 [comp2.name]毕竟，在这个团队中，只有她具备使用翅膀进行运输所需的技能和经验。你肯定不希望因为她的失误而导致朋友们遇到危险。 阿齐笑着摆了摆手部，表示不用担心。“哦，别担心这个。妈妈以前总是让我和我的姐妹们接待那些想见她的访客们，我已经习惯了。” 你还没来得及抗议，她就转身跑进了黑暗中。 这段等待实在令人煎熬，但十分钟后，阿齐终于伴随着上升气流哼着歌回来了 [comp2.name] 她双手部紧握着那些东西，看起来明显很不舒服，但却不敢乱动。那两个东西重重地落在你身边，发出沉闷的声音，阿兹满意地拍掉手部上的灰尘。 “都搞定了！看吧，你根本没什么好担心的。” 好吧，这次她赢了。既然你的团队已经安全地重新聚集在一起，是时候去看看矿井的这一侧还有什么等着你们了…… ] |回程的时候，你带着要取回的东西，体重肯定会更重一些。 “哦，别担心这个，”阿齐轻声说道，“我既能照顾好那些东西，也能照顾好你。现在，如果你不介意的话，我真的很想知道我们大老远跑过来到底是要取回什么东西。 你难道不感到兴奋吗？” 嘿，没必要急于一时——你毕竟不知道未来会发生什么。不过，至少我确实感到有些好奇。那么，是时候继续前进了…… ]

rows.translation: 让阿兹兰带你飞过去吧。

rows.original:
Opening up your camping supplies, you draw out the rope, stakes, and other bits and pieces meant for securing a camp — they'll do just as well to get you across the cavern in one piece. While they won't stand up to the scalding plumes of steam, they'll be invaluable in getting you across some of the deeper chasms.

        With that in mind, you start planning a way across the cavern, noting which bridges of land look more stable and more likely to hold up as you go about crossing them. There's also the matter of securing a rope about your waist so you don't go careening into the darkness within one of the sinkholes, a threat that's doubly present given the damp floor within a good radius of each steam spout.
        
        The going is slow and uncomfortably warm to boot; it's not just the faintly sulfurous stench that lingers in the air, but also the constant tepid moistness that clings to your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] and starts dripping off your body. You're more worried about the former and there not being proper air to breathe inside of this confined space, but you don't find yourself growing drowsy or faint so long as you stay away from the worst of the updrafts.
        
        Eventually, you make it — and just as the last of your rope runs out crossing one of the larger sinkholes. Sure, it was rather uneventful, but that's probably because of having had a lifeline to save you should you slip off an edge. Now to see what this trouble is all about...
rows.translation:
当你打开露营用品包时，会拿出绳子、木桩以及其他用于固定营地的工具——这些工具同样也能帮助你安全地穿过洞穴。虽然它们无法抵挡灼热的蒸汽，但在穿越一些较深的沟壑时，它们会发挥至关重要的作用。

        考虑到这些因素，你开始思考如何穿过这个洞穴，留意哪些陆桥看起来更加稳固，过桥时更有可能保持稳定。此外，你还需要在腰间系上一根绳子，这样就不会在经过那些天坑时突然坠入黑暗之中——考虑到每个蒸汽喷口周围一定范围内的地面都非常潮湿，这种危险就更加明显了。
        
        进展得很慢，而且环境闷热得让人难以忍受；空气中不仅弥漫着淡淡的硫磺味，那种持续的潮湿气息也让人浑身不自在。 [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] 汗水开始从你的身上滴落下来。你更担心的是，在这个封闭的空间里，是否会有足够的空气供你呼吸；不过，只要避开那些最强烈的上升气流，你并不会感到昏昏欲睡或头晕目眩。
        
        最终，你成功了——就在你最后的绳子在穿过其中一个较大的天坑时用完了。当然，这个过程相当平淡无奇，但那很可能是因为有了一条救生绳在，以防你从边缘滑落。 现在，让我们来看看这个麻烦到底是怎么回事……

rows.original: You don't have any camping supplies.

You take another look at the sinkhole-dotted cavern and are briefly tempted to attempt the crossing unaided, but caution gets the better of you and you abandon the idea. It's not worth the risk... and even if you did make the crossing, you'd have to return saddled with whatever it is that Nina wants you to retrieve. For all you know, it could be pretty bulky.

        No point being foolhardy about it, it's not like you have anything to prove. You can always return when you've got the tools or people needed to make it across safely; there's no time limit on this little errand, after all.
rows.translation:
你再次凝视着那些布满天坑的洞穴，一时真想尝试独自穿越，但理智最终占了上风，你放弃了这个念头。这种风险实在不值得……而且即使你真的成功穿过了，也必须带着妮娜要求你取回的东西回来。 谁知道呢，它可能会变得相当笨重。

没必要冒这个险，反正你也没有什么必须证明的事情。等你准备了所需的工具或找到了能帮助你安全完成这项任务的人，随时都可以再回去；毕竟，这次小差事并没有时间限制。
