rows.original: The rotting crates and boxes are as empty as they're unassuming, save for one: a lacquered box that's survived in much better condition than its fellows. Its metal bandings are still intact with but a few flecks of tarnish, it draws into view as you continue your search, complete with the most unorthodox locking mechanism. [party.has quin |You glance at Quin and ask the bunny-man if he knows anything about this kind of lock. Can he do anything about it? Quin takes all of three seconds to study the box before shaking his head. "Lockpicks won't work on this one, it's a wordlock chest; what it's doing here is anyone's guess, maybe there's more to this old mine than meets the eye. If we could find a fence willing to take it no questions asked, it might be worth more than what's in it. It's an antique in and of itself, and the mechanism isn't something just anyone can make any more." Would he? "I don't know, I'd be tempted to keep it for myself just for the novelty of having such a relic. There're people in the Tael Alliance who'd pay much for one of these... but we don't have the time for that right now. Still, you want to know how these things work, right? There's a password, and you make the tumblers spell it out, simple as that. People also had a riddle inscribed on the chest just in case they forgot their password; solve that, and it opens." Hmm. [pc.bg scholar noblescion acolyte |Based on your own studies, you know Quin's not talking out of his ass; servants of Belharan nobility were not educated and could not read. |Riddles, eh? Shouldn't be too hard to figure out, if ancient Belharan security was testing someone's ability to read. ] The bigger question is what a wordlock chest is doing here in a mine staffed by convicts and golems is a question in and of itself, but the answer has almost certainly been lost to history. Quin chuckles and shakes his head. "Look around you. It's obvious there was more going on here than just digging — maybe the overseers were crooked, maybe the crooks themselves were really in charge; the fact that a Belharan relic was up here in the hands of the frost elves speaks volumes to the magnitude of what was going on here, even if we don't know what it is. Maybe that's why your silly little bird sent us here?" |[party.has cait |"Father used to tell Calla and I about these," Cait pipes up as she studies the chest. "They're wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly |players |servants ]. Each combination lock was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was a riddle was often posed on the chest itself." So if you solved this thing, the lock would just pop open and you could just help yourself to anything inside. "Yep!" The bigger question is what a wordlock chest is doing here in a mine staffed by convicts and golems is a question in and of itself, but the answer has almost certainly been lost to history. "I don't know!" Cait chirps. "But think about it, [pc.name] — that something like this was dragged up all the way from the Heartlands where it originated suggests that these elves weren't just digging up ore for the elven crown." Does she think they were running a side business? Perhaps there might have been an overseer or something, but the people working the mine were all convicts... it wouldn't have been impossible for them to hide any illicit activity from a handful of officials. "Maybe! But if I were an elven thug, I wouldn't run my business out of this kind of place, even if it'd keep people away!" |[pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte |You've come across these before in your past — wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly |players |servants ]. Each of these combination locks was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was, a riddle was often posed on the chest itself. If you could solve it and thereby rotate the tumblers into the right position, the chest would unlock and allow you to claim its contents. |Hmm, what can this all mean? It certainly seems like a thoroughly roundabout way to secure a container, but at least it isn't likely to be trapped in the bargain. You test the mechanism a few times, turn the tumblers, but nothing happens. ] The bigger question is what a wordlock chest is doing here in a mine staffed by convicts and golems is a question in and of itself, but the answer has almost certainly been lost to history. ] ] With its previous owners departed, the wordlock chest and its contents are yours, if you can get it open...
rows.translation: 那些腐烂的木箱和盒子看上去普普通通，其实都是空的，只有一个例外：一个上了漆的箱子，它的保存状况比其他箱子要好得多。它的金属绑带依然完好无损，只有一点点锈迹。当你继续搜寻时，这个箱子会映入你的视线，而它的锁具机制也显得格外不寻常。 [party.has quin |你瞥了瞥奎因，然后问那个兔人是否了解这种锁的原理，以及是否能够解决这个问题。 奎因花了整整三秒钟来观察那个箱子，最终摇了摇头说道：“开锁工具对这种锁根本不起作用，这是一个需要通过解谜来打开的箱子；至于它为什么会出现在这里，那就只有天知道了……也许这个古老的矿井里隐藏着一些不为人知的东西。 如果我们能找到一个愿意毫无条件接受它的买家，那么它的价值可能会远远超过它里面的东西。它本身就是一件古董，而那种制作机制也已经不是任何人都能复制的了。 他会愿意吗？ 我也不确定啊，光是因为拥有这样一件稀有物品带来的新鲜感，我就很想把它留下来。在泰尔联盟里，肯定有人愿意花大价钱购买这样的东西……但我们现在实在没有时间去考虑这些。不过，你肯定想知道这些东西到底是怎么运作的，对吧？ 需要输入一个密码，然后让那些转盘拼出这个密码，就是这么简单。如果人们忘记了密码，箱子上还刻有一条谜语；解开这条谜语，箱子就能打开。 嗯 [pc.bg scholar noblescion acolyte |根据你自己的研究，你应该知道昆的话并非无稽之谈；贝尔哈兰贵族的仆从们根本没有受过教育，也不识字。 |谜语，嗯？如果古代贝尔哈兰的安全系统是用来测试某人的阅读能力的话，这些谜语应该不会太难解吧。 ] 更重要的问题是：在一个由囚犯和傀儡组成的矿场里，为什么会出现这样的“单词锁箱”？这个问题本身就很值得探讨，但它的答案恐怕早已湮灭在历史的长河中了。 奎因轻笑一声，然后摇了摇头。 看看你周围的环境。很明显，这里发生的事情远不止挖掘这么简单——也许那些监督者本身就不诚实，又或许真正掌权的是那些腐败之徒；而一件贝拉兰的遗物竟然落在了霜之精灵的手部中，这一事实本身就足以说明这里发生的事情有多么严重，尽管我们还不清楚具体细节是什么。 是也许这就是为什么你那只傻乎乎的小鸟把我们带到这里的原因吧？ |[party.has cait |父亲过去常常给我们讲这些，”凯特边研究着那个箱子边说道，“这些是密码锁箱子，是老贝拉兰贵族们最喜欢的物品，用来保护贵重物品，防止那些不识字的人偷走它们。 [silly |玩家们 |仆从们 ]每个密码锁都需要输入正确的密码才能打开，而为了帮助主人记住密码，人们通常会在箱子本身上设置一个谜语。 因此，如果你解开了这个谜语，锁就会自动打开，你就可以取走箱子里里的任何东西了。 没错！” 不过，更值得思考的是：为什么在一个由囚犯和傀儡组成的矿场里，会出现这样的词锁箱？这个疑问本身就很有意思，但它的答案恐怕早已湮没在历史的长河中了。 我不知道！”凯特轻声说道，“但是仔细想想 [pc.name] 像这样的东西竟然从它的发源地——心脏地带被带了过来，这说明这些精灵不仅仅是在为精灵王室开采矿石。” 她难道认为他们还在从事其他秘密生意吗？ 或许本来应该有监督人员之类的存在，但那些在矿场工作的人全都是囚犯……对于他们来说，隐藏一些非法活动，对那寥寥几名官员来说，根本不是什么不可能的事。 也许吧！但如果我是个精灵恶棍，我肯定不会在这种地方做生意，即使这样会让人们远离我！ |[pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte |你在过去曾经见过这类东西——字锁箱。这种箱子曾是贝尔哈兰老贵族们的最爱，他们用它来保护贵重物品，防止那些不识字的人偷走它们。 [silly |玩家们 |仆从们 ]这些组合锁每一把都需要输入密码才能打开，为了帮助主人记住密码，人们通常会在箱子上设置谜语。如果你能够解开这个谜语，将锁芯旋转到正确的位置，箱子就会打开，让你取走里面的物品。 |嗯，这一切到底意味着什么呢？这种方式看起来确实挺迂回的，但至少不会让人陷入什么麻烦之中。你试了几次这个装置，转动了那些旋钮，但什么反应也没有发生。 ] 更值得探讨的是：在一个由囚犯和傀儡组成的矿场里，为什么会出现这样的“单词锁箱”？这个问题本身就很有意义，但它的答案恐怕早已湮没在历史的长河中了。 ] ] 随着之前的主人离开，这个密码锁箱以及里面的物品就归你所有了……只要你能把它打开的话……
rows.raw: " The rotting crates and boxes are as empty as they're unassuming, save for one: a lacquered box that's survived in much better condition than its fellows. Its metal bandings are still intact with but a few flecks of tarnish, it draws into view as you continue your search, complete with the most unorthodox locking mechanism. [party.has quin |You glance at Quin and ask the bunny-man if he knows anything about this kind of lock. Can he do anything about it? Quin takes all of three seconds to study the box before shaking his head. "Lockpicks won't work on this one, it's a wordlock chest; what it's doing here is anyone's guess, maybe there's more to this old mine than meets the eye. If we could find a fence willing to take it no questions asked, it might be worth more than what's in it. It's an antique in and of itself, and the mechanism isn't something just anyone can make any more." Would he? "I don't know, I'd be tempted to keep it for myself just for the novelty of having such a relic. There're people in the Tael Alliance who'd pay much for one of these... but we don't have the time for that right now. Still, you want to know how these things work, right? There's a password, and you make the tumblers spell it out, simple as that. People also had a riddle inscribed on the chest just in case they forgot their password; solve that, and it opens." Hmm. [pc.bg scholar noblescion acolyte |Based on your own studies, you know Quin's not talking out of his ass; servants of Belharan nobility were not educated and could not read. |Riddles, eh? Shouldn't be too hard to figure out, if ancient Belharan security was testing someone's ability to read. ] The bigger question is what a wordlock chest is doing here in a mine staffed by convicts and golems is a question in and of itself, but the answer has almost certainly been lost to history. Quin chuckles and shakes his head. "Look around you. It's obvious there was more going on here than just digging — maybe the overseers were crooked, maybe the crooks themselves were really in charge; the fact that a Belharan relic was up here in the hands of the frost elves speaks volumes to the magnitude of what was going on here, even if we don't know what it is. Maybe that's why your silly little bird sent us here?" |[party.has cait |"Father used to tell Calla and I about these," Cait pipes up as she studies the chest. "They're wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly |players |servants ]. Each combination lock was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was a riddle was often posed on the chest itself." So if you solved this thing, the lock would just pop open and you could just help yourself to anything inside. "Yep!" The bigger question is what a wordlock chest is doing here in a mine staffed by convicts and golems is a question in and of itself, but the answer has almost certainly been lost to history. "I don't know!" Cait chirps. "But think about it, [pc.name] — that something like this was dragged up all the way from the Heartlands where it originated suggests that these elves weren't just digging up ore for the elven crown." Does she think they were running a side business? Perhaps there might have been an overseer or something, but the people working the mine were all convicts... it wouldn't have been impossible for them to hide any illicit activity from a handful of officials. "Maybe! But if I were an elven thug, I wouldn't run my business out of this kind of place, even if it'd keep people away!" |[pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte |You've come across these before in your past — wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly |players |servants ]. Each of these combination locks was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was, a riddle was often posed on the chest itself. If you could solve it and thereby rotate the tumblers into the right position, the chest would unlock and allow you to claim its contents. |Hmm, what can this all mean? It certainly seems like a thoroughly roundabout way to secure a container, but at least it isn't likely to be trapped in the bargain. You test the mechanism a few times, turn the tumblers, but nothing happens. ] The bigger question is what a wordlock chest is doing here in a mine staffed by convicts and golems is a question in and of itself, but the answer has almost certainly been lost to history. ] ] With its previous owners departed, the wordlock chest and its contents are yours, if you can get it open..."

rows.original: An untiring servant, Carrying loads across earth, Yet cannot return to, The place of its birth.
rows.translation: 一位不知疲倦的仆人， 肩负重担在大地之上奔走， 却始终无法回到， 它诞生的地方。
rows.raw: "An untiring servant, Carrying loads across earth, Yet cannot return to, The place of its birth."

rows.original: Open it up! What's in the box?
rows.translation: 把它打开吧！盒子里有什么？
rows.raw: "Open it up! What's in the box?"

rows.original: This isn't worth the trouble. Just let it be.
rows.translation: 这不值得费这个劲。就让它保持原样吧。
rows.raw: "This isn't worth the trouble. Just let it be."

rows.original: You rub your temples and sigh. The riddle's right there in front of you, but its words might as well have been unscalable walls. Whatever's in the chest is going to have to stay inside until you figure this out.
rows.translation: 你揉了揉太阳穴，叹了口气。这个谜题就摆在你的眼前，但它的答案仿佛就是一道无法逾越的墙。直到你解开这个谜题，箱子里的东西才会被取出。
rows.raw: "\n    You rub your temples and sigh. The riddle's right there in front of you, but its words might as well have been unscalable walls. Whatever's in the chest is going to have to stay inside until you figure this out."

rows.original: Something within the chest clicks, followed by a loud thump as the mechanisms within disengage. Instinctively, you step back, fearing a trap, but your fears are soon allayed as the spring-loaded lid pops open, revealing the chest's contents for the first time in over a couple centuries. Booze, lots of it, overflows from the chest — bottles, sealed jugs, and other containers of all shapes and sizes, still good despite the passage of time. Whatever managed to preserve the wordlock chest to this day has clearly kept its contents from souring into vinegar over the years. [party.randComp etheryn arona |"Just look at the variety," Ryn says, shaking her head. "I find it hard to believe myself, but we didn't always use to be recluses, and ranged far further than just the one city-state that we hold today." Smuggling under the crown's nose, and out of a criminal work camp to boot? A rueful smile. "Well, they were able to get it, and without official channels. Would we have such capability these days..." |Arona's eyes widen at the sight. "Well, shit, would you look at this haul. I think we're fit to stop for a break right about now." As tempting as that might be, there's still the little matter of having to return across the sinkhole-filled chamber, this time weighed down with your loot in tow. Sure, she can call you a coward, but you'd rather not make the attempt while drunk or hung over. As great as aged booze might be, one can't enjoy it very much when one's broken body is lying in a heap in the deep dark. Your orcish companion looks thoughtful for a moment, tapping her fingers on her [arona.weapon], then to your mild surprise, nods. "Yeah, you're right. Let's get this haul over to the other side, then we can talk about drinking. Nothing like working up a sweat to work up a good thirst as well, after all." ] Well, time to see just how much of this stash you'll actually be able to carry away with you — for something that came out of the wordlock chest, there is a lot of booze. How it managed to all fit in there is anyone's guess...
rows.translation: 箱子里的某个装置发出了咔嗒声，随后随着内部机械装置的松动，传来一声沉重的撞击声。出于本能，你向后退了一步，担心这是个陷阱，但很快你的担忧就消散了——弹簧装置驱动的盖子猛地弹开，几个世纪以来首次让人们看到了箱子里的物品。 酒，大量的酒——各种形状和大小的瓶子、密封的罐子，全都装在那个箱子里。尽管时间已经流逝，但这些酒依然完好无损。显然，是某种神秘的力量让这个密封箱得以保存至今，也让里面的酒没有变质变成醋。 [party.randComp etheryn arona |看看这些各种各样的东西吧，”瑞恩摇着头说，“我自己都很难相信——但我们以前并不总是与世隔绝的，我们的活动范围也远不止如今这个城邦而已。” 在王室的眼皮底下走私，而且还是从一个罪犯劳改营里逃出来的？ 她苦笑着回答：“嗯，他们确实做到了，而且还是通过非官方渠道。要是在现在，我们还有这样的能力吗…… |看到这一幕，阿罗娜的眼睛瞪得大大的：“哇，天哪，看看我们捡到了什么！我觉得我们现在真的该停下来休息一下了。” 虽然这样很吸引人，但还有一个问题需要解决——我们必须再次穿过那些布满天坑的房间，而这次还得拖着这些战利品一起走。 当然，她可以骂你胆小鬼，但如果你在喝醉或宿醉的情况下尝试，结果只会更糟。虽然陈年酒确实很美味，但当你的身体在黑暗中痛苦地躺着时，你就无法真正享受它了。 你的兽人同伴似乎陷入了沉思，她用手指轻轻敲打着 [arona.weapon]然后，令你略感惊讶的是，他点了点头。“没错，你说得对。我们把这些货物搬到另一边去吧。 然后 我们可以聊聊喝酒的事。毕竟，在辛苦工作之后，确实会让人特别想喝点东西来解渴。 ] 好吧，是时候看看你究竟能带走这些物品中的多少了——毕竟这些东西可是从那个密码锁箱里拿出来的，所以 很多 那些酒。究竟是怎么全部塞进那里去的，谁也猜不出来……

rows.original: Are you finished with everything here? Once you leave with the goods, you won't be able to return.
rows.translation: 你把这里的所有事情都处理完毕了吗？一旦你带着这些东西离开，就再也不能回来了。
rows.raw: "\n Are you finished with everything here? Once you leave with the goods, you won't be able to return."

rows.original: This must be it, then — a large crate sitting by the side of an ancient firepit, surrounded by the rotted and dessicate remains of an equally aged leather tarpaulin. The so-called super important thing that Nina would be so glad to get your hands on, in her own words, the prize that you picked your way over this treacherous hollowed-out cavern to acquire... You can't take it any more, your curiosity has to be sated. While the wood is in terrible condition and the brass bindings have gained a green patina, the crate still holds, and you push aside the lid to reveal rows upon rows of dusty green bottles sitting in the weighty container, caked with stone grit but otherwise unharmed. They'd once been packed with sawdust, but that's rotted away into a disgusting mulch, leaving dust that seeps through the base of the cate when you pick it up. Ugh! Booze, thirty bottles of it — even if the labels weren't as faded as they are, you have no way of understanding what presumably is the boreal elf language. But you've seen these before, in the palace of ice... elven ice wine, also known to Ryn's kin as mirrorwine. Yeah... you can see how this would be terribly important to Nina, and how glad she would be to get her hands on a load of this. [party.has etheryn |"Oh dear," Ryn says, stepping up and looking over your shoulder at your find. "That's more mirrorwine in one place than you'd find in the palace cellars, especially near the end of Alissa's reign. Do you mind if I take a look?" Sure, she can knock herself out. You move aside, and Ryn pulls out one of the ancient, finely made bottles, brushing aside fine stone grit and squinting at the label in the gloom. Well? "This one's really old. Well, all mirrorwine dates from before the Godswar and the ensuing schism, but this goes a good while even before that. If we assume that this mine was abandoned during the Godswar, then it'd have been considered quite the vintage at that point, and by our standards. Look here at the bottom, they're still using the old dating system... the grapes were pressed roughly a hundred and ten years before the Godswar." You shake your head. Ordinary wine would've long since dried out, let alone soured into vinegar, but this is something else altogether. That being said, the presence of bottles of fine wine here... "...Imply corruption in my great-grandmother's reign, yes. Despite what Hethia and her people say, the era before the Godswar wasn't one of supreme enlightenment and harmony until my grandmother ruined it all." Ryn sighs. "But back to the point. I only know this from the histories, but mirrorwine wasn't supposed to fall into hands that weren't boer'alvar. The need for isolation wasn't always there, and these were clearly packed for long-distance shipping." Was there some kind of religious stricture against selling ice wine to other peoples, or something along those lines? "No, but it was simple politeness, I think. The druids didn't actually get most of their money from donations — they had very good apiaries and wineries that produced excellent honey, mead, mirrorwine and more. But the thing is that the latter was supposed to be a gift from the druids to the boer'alvar as a people, which is why it was sold at cost as opposed to the other fruits of their art. To sell away that which was given to you in good faith and abuse that kindness... well, it's not just the boer'alvar who look down upon such a practice." Which brings you back to the here and now — it looks like at least some of these convict mining camps were used as forwarding spots for smuggling. Ryn sighs. "It's all in the past, [pc.name]. Important to know... but also just as important to let go. They weren't all as good as dead... some did manage to survive their sentences. "Let's bring this back to Nina, then. She wasn't wrong — this is really valuable, although from the look on your face I'm sure it's not valuable in the way you were expecting." |[party.has cait |"Ooooh," Cait says, stepping up and looking over your shoulder at your find. "That looks like the fancy wine that Ryn sometimes sets out at the palace. Mind if I take a look?" Sure, she can knock herself out. You move aside, and Cait pulls out one of the ancient, finely made bottles, brushing aside fine stone grit and squinting at the label in the gloom. Well, anything? "Wait a moment, I'm trying to recall what Dad told Calla and I while we were on the ship, trying to prepare us for what we might find up here in the Marches. Right... "This stuff's really old. Look, it's dated in the pre-Godswar Belharan system, and if I'm not wrong the date should come to about a hundred and ten years before everything happened." She can read pale elf? Presumably that's what the labels are in... "No, but I can read numbers. Which brings up the question of why exactly the pale elves would be using the imperial dating system — I'm not completely sure, but I don't think they did. The empire's influence stopped at the River Ridell, even if there were agreements between them and the pale elves like the one Ryn tried to claim with Carmen." Well, that would imply that trade wasn't impossible... on the other hand, you get the impression that elven ice wine is kind of rare, even amongst the pale elves. Certainly the kind of thing you didn't just export on a whim. "I don't know about that. To hear Ryn speak of it, things were better in her great-grandmother's time; we can't just assume that things were the same back then as they are today. Who knows, the pale elves might have had a booming wine export business. It's certainly something I'd have to ask Ryn about when I next see her." Certainly lucrative enough for what's ostensibly a convict mining camp to engage in a bit of corruption on the side. If the workers were in on it, the officials almost certainly were, too. "The past was a lot more civilized, I'm told," Cait says with a sigh. "But Dad always used to point out that if we thought corruption in the sultanate was bad, one can only imagine what it would've been like in a sprawling empire like Belhar's. We can only keep it down, not get rid of it altogether. It's all in the past, [pc.name]. Important to know... but also just as important to let go. "Come on, let's bring this back to your bird and see what she has to say for herself." |[party.has quintillus |"Hmm," Quin says, stepping up and looking over your shoulder at your find. "Even if it's this old, I know contraband when I see it. Do you mind if I take a closer look?" Sure, he can knock himself out. You move aside, and Quin pulls out one of the ancient, finely made bottles, brushing aside fine stone grit and squinting at the label in the gloom. Anything notable? "The way these were packed, I'd think they were meant to be moved out with the ore shipments. It's a sturdy crate that's survived a couple hundred years, I'm sure it would've held up to a bit of weight. Who wants to go to the trouble of moving aside a huge pile of rocks to search its guts?" Quin chuckles, then dusts off some grit from the label with a fingertip. "The label's written in whatever language these elves use and I can't read that, but oddly enough there's more on the bottom that's clearly been added later, in antiquated Belharan to boot. Look...the vintage's dated roughly a hundred and ten years before the Godswar. This is good stuff, if it hasn't soured already, and while I don't know much about the pale elves they damn well make things to last." [pc.bg scholar acolyte |Hey, he's actually right. Now that Quin's pointing it out to you, you do recognize a word here and there from when you'd stumbled across a couple of the more ancient texts in your bookish past. |You'll just take to take his word for it, then. As far as you're concerned, it's all the same to you. ] "Even though I never actually made the cut, everyone knows that fresh talons cut their teeth on small-timers like smugglers. I'd been hoping to... never mind. "My guess is that this entire mining outpost was crooked — you don't get all the convicts joining in on the business and the contraband being left out in the open without the approval of whatever officials were stationed here. They'd receive the goods from their friends in the forest, then hide the booze in the ore shipments... whichever way you take to the Winter City from here, north or south, you'll be running into water, be it the fjord or the river. After evading the outriders on the roads, this would've been loaded onto a ship and punted to Belhar. A bit of a leap, I'll admit, but that's my guess given my knowledge of how things work — I don't expect anything to have been different just because these people were elves." Ice wine to Belhar, though... that's a long way to go. The addendum to the label in Belharan, though, would confirm that it was intended for somewhere that spoke the language, at the very least. "It's a long way, but they certainly felt it was worth it." Quin sighs and rubs his temples. "Ever hear that fucker Tollus go on about the pleasures of the old imperium and how it was his destiny to recapture them? He wasn't lying about the first part — even a commoner in the imperial capital lived better than a king today. They weren't lacking in the least for wealth, but they damn well were lacking for entertainment. I suppose elven ice wine counts as a passable distraction, doesn't it?" You suppose it would, yeah. If the palace's any indication, the boreal elves have been drinking it for a long time and still have yet to get bored of the stuff. "Aah, that's all in the past, [pc.name]. Important to know... but also just as important to let go, that bald fucker is made all the more dangerous because he knows to blend just enough truth into his lies to make them dangerous. "Let's bring this back to Nina, then. She wasn't wrong — this is really valuable, although from the look on your face I'm sure it's not valuable in the way you were expecting." |You shake your head. Ordinary wine would've long since dried out, let alone soured into vinegar, but this is something else altogether. That being said, the presence of bottles of fine wine here... in the scheme of things, you haven't been with Ryn's people for too long, but you're pretty sure that ice wine's supposed to be pretty rare even for them, perhaps even restricted?[pc.bg scholar acolyte | When you look at the label, you also note that the bottom half, date of the vintage included, is written in antiquated Belharan — you do recognize a word here and there from when you'd stumbled across a couple of the more ancient texts in your bookish past. That being said, a word or two's still not enough to make sense of it all... ] Oh well, no good thinking too much about it. Whatever went on here, it's all in the past, a distant memory even for the pale elves. You have more pressing business to handle. ] ] ]
rows.translation: 果然就是这里——一个巨大的木箱放在古老的火坑旁，周围环绕着同样陈旧、已经腐烂干枯的皮革防水布残片。按照妮娜自己的说法，这就是那件她梦寐以求、绝对不能让别人得到的重要物品，也是你历经千辛万苦、穿越这个危险而空洞的洞穴才终于获得的奖品。你再也无法忍受了，你的好奇心必须得到满足。虽然这些木箱的状况已经非常糟糕，黄铜制的封条上也覆上了一层绿色的铜锈，但箱子本身仍然完好无损。你推开盖子，看到里面摆着一排排积满灰尘的绿色瓶子，它们被石屑覆盖着，不过除此之外并没有受到任何损坏。 那些瓶子曾经装满了锯末，但锯末已经腐烂成了一堆恶心的淤泥，当你拿起这些瓶子时，淤泥会从瓶底渗出来，真是太恶心了！ 还有那些酒，整整三十瓶——即使瓶子上的标签没有现在这么褪色，你也根本无法理解上面写的是什么，毕竟那些应该是极北精灵的语言吧。 但你之前在冰之宫殿里见过这些——精灵冰酒，在瑞恩的族人中也被称作“镜之酒”。没错……你可以想象，这对妮娜来说该有多重要，她要是能得到很多这种酒，该有多高兴。 [party.has etheryn |哦，天哪，”莱恩走上前，从你身后看了看你找到的东西，说道，“这一处的镜之酒数量，比整个宫殿的酒窖里加起来还要多，尤其是在艾莉莎统治末期。我可以看看吗？当然，她完全可以把自己弄晕。你退到一边，然后Ryn取出了其中一个古老而制作精良的瓶子，拂去瓶身上的细小石屑，在昏暗的光线下仔细辨认着瓶子上的标签。 然后呢？ 这个确实非常古老了。嗯，所有的镜之酒都诞生于神战以及随之而来的分裂之前，但这个酒的酿制时间甚至更早。如果我们假设这个酒窖是在神战期间被废弃的，那么在当时，它就已经属于非常珍贵的老酒了；按照我们的标准来看，更是如此。 看看底部，他们仍在使用那种古老的日期纪年系统……那些“葡萄”其实是在大约一百一十年前被“压榨”出来的。 在……之前 神战之酒。” 你摇了摇头。普通的葡萄酒早就干掉了，更不用说会变成醋了，但这种酒却完全不同。不过，这里竟然有这么多上等的葡萄酒…………这意味着我的曾祖母在执政期间存在腐败行为，没错。尽管赫希娅和她的追随者们怎么说，但在‘神战’之前，那个时代其实并不是一个充满启蒙与和谐的时期，直到我的祖母破坏了一切。雷恩叹了口气，”不过还是回到正题上。我只是从历史记载中了解到这些：镜之酒本不该落入非布尔·阿尔瓦尔家族的人手中。其实，当初并没有必要将其隔离起来，而这些包装显然也是为长途运输而准备的。" 是不是有什么宗教禁忌，禁止向其他人出售冰酒，或者是类似的原因呢？ “并不是，我觉得只是出于礼貌而已。实际上，德鲁伊们并不是主要依靠捐赠来获取收入的——他们拥有非常出色的养蜂场和酿酒厂，这些地方生产的蜂蜜、蜜酒、镜酒等等产品都非常优质。 但事实上，后者本应是德鲁伊们送给布尔阿尔瓦尔这个民族的礼物，正因如此，它才以成本价出售，而并非像他们其他的作品那样被高价售卖。将别人出于善意送给你的东西卖掉，这种行为无疑是对这份善意的践踏。嗯，其实并不是只有那些布尔人会看不起这种做法。 这就把我们带回了现实——看来，这些囚犯劳改营中至少有一部分被用作走私活动的中转站。 瑞恩叹了口气：“这一切都已经成为过去了。 [pc.name]需要明白的一点是……但同样重要的是，也要学会放手部。那些事情，它们本就不属于你。 所有 简直跟死了没什么两样……不过还是有人成功熬过了那些惩罚。 “那我们就把这件事告诉尼娜吧。她没有错——这些东西确实很有价值，不过从你的表情来看，我敢肯定这些价值的含义并不是你预想的那样。 |[party.has cait |哦哦哦，”凯特走上前，从你肩膀后面看了看你找到的东西。“那看起来像是瑞恩有时在宫殿里准备的那种高档葡萄酒。我可以看看吗？” “当然，她想看就让她看吧。 你退到一边，凯特取出了其中一个古老而制作精良的瓶子，轻轻拂去瓶子表面的细小石屑，然后在昏暗的光线下仔细辨认着瓶子上的标签。 “嗯，有什么发现吗？” “等一下，我正在努力回忆爸爸在船上时跟卡拉和我说过的话，那些话应该是为了让我们做好在这里可能会遇到的各种情况的准备。 对了…… “这些东西真的非常古老。看，上面的日期是神战之前的贝尔哈兰纪元，如果我没记错的话，那个时间应该是在大约一百十年前。 在……之前 一切都发生了。” 她能看懂那些淡色精灵文字吗？大概那些标签上就是用这种文字写的吧…… “不，但我能看懂数字。这就引出了一个问题：为什么淡色精灵会使用帝国的纪年系统呢？我不太确定，但我觉得他们应该不会使用这种系统的。帝国的影响力在里德尔河为止，即使他们和淡色精灵之间有过一些协议，比如瑞恩试图和卡门达成的那种协议。 嗯，这意味着贸易并非完全不可能……不过，从另一方面来看，你会觉得精灵冰酒其实相当稀有，就连在浅色精灵中也是如此。这种东西肯定不是可以随随便便就出口的。 我不太确定。听Ryn说，她的高祖母那个时代，情况要好一些；但我们不能想当然地认为那时候的情况和现在一样。谁知道呢，那些苍白精灵说不定当时在葡萄酒出口业务上发展得非常成功呢。 下次见到瑞恩时，我肯定得问问她这件事。 对于一个名义上应该是囚犯劳改营的地方来说，这样的利润显然足以让相关人员搞一些腐败行为。如果工人都参与了其中，那么官员们几乎也肯定难逃其责。 “听说过去的情况要文明得多呢，”凯特叹着气说道。 但是爸爸总是说，如果我们觉得苏丹国的腐败现象已经很严重了，那么试想，在像贝尔哈尔这样庞大的帝国里，腐败会达到什么程度。我们所能做的，只是尽量控制它的蔓延，而无法彻底根除它。 这一切都已经成为过去了。 [pc.name]. 了解这些很重要……但同样重要的是，也要学会放手部。 “来吧，把这件事交给你的鸟儿，看看她自己有什么要说的。 |[party.has quintillus |嗯，”奎因说着走上前，从你肩膀后面看了看你找到的东西。“虽然它已经这么旧了，但我还是能认出违禁品来。你介意让我仔细看看吗？” “当然，随他便吧。 你让到一边，奎因取出了其中一个制作精良的古老瓶子，拂去瓶身上细小的石屑，然后在昏暗的光线下仔细辨认着瓶子上的标签。 “有什么特别的吗？” “从这些瓶子的包装方式来看，我猜它们应该是随矿石运输一起被运走的。 这是一个非常结实的箱子，已经存在了几百年，我相信它完全能够承受一定的重量。谁会愿意费劲地把一大堆石头搬开， just为了检查它的内部呢？奎因轻笑着，然后用指尖擦去标签上的一些灰尘。 标签上写着这些精灵使用的语言，我根本看不懂，但奇怪的是，在标签的底部还写着一些内容，这些显然是后来添加的，而且是用已经过时的贝尔哈兰语写的。看……这个物品的制造日期大概是一百十年前。 在……之前 《神战》。如果这东西还没有变质的话，那可真是相当不错的东西。虽然我对苍白精灵了解不多，但他们制作的物品确实经得起考验。 [pc.bg scholar acolyte |嘿，他其实说得对。现在既然Quin已经指出了这一点，你 做 偶尔会想起那些在年轻时阅读过的古老文献中出现的词语。 |那你也就只能相信他的话了。对你来说，反正结果都是一样的。 ] 虽然我最终并没有真正入选，但大家都知道，那些新晋的执法人员最初都是从处理像走私犯这样的小案子开始积累经验的。我原本还希望能……算了，罢了。 “我猜，这个采矿前哨站从一开始就是有问题存在的——如果没有这里驻扎的官员们的默许，根本不可能有那么多囚犯参与这种非法活动，也不可能有违禁品被公然摆在那里而不被处理。 他们会从森林里的朋友那里取得这些货物，然后把酒藏在这些矿石运输途中……无论你从这里往冬城方向走哪条路，无论是往北还是往南，都会遇到水域，无论是峡湾还是河流。 在躲过了路上的巡逻队之后，这些货物本来应该会被装上船只，然后被运送到贝尔哈尔。我承认，这个推测有点大胆，但根据我对当地情况的了解，我只能这么猜测——我并不认为仅仅因为这些人是精灵，事情就会有什么不同。" 将冰酒运到贝尔哈尔……虽然路途遥远。不过，贝尔哈尔语标签上的附加说明至少可以证明，这种酒是为那些使用这种语言的地区准备的。 “路途确实很长，但他们显然认为这是值得的。奎因叹了口气，揉了揉太阳穴。‘你有没有听过那个混蛋托卢斯总念叨着旧帝国的辉煌，还说重夺那些荣光是他的命运？第一点他确实没说谎——如今，就连帝都里的平民，生活也比那些国王还要好。 他们一点也不缺财富，但确实缺乏娱乐活动。我想，精灵冰酒也算是一种还算不错的消遣方式吧？ 你这么认为，是啊。从宫殿里的情况来看，极北精灵们已经喝了这种东西很长时间了，但他们似乎从未对此感到厌倦。 “啊，那些都已经成为过去了 [pc.name]需要了解的一点是……但同样重要的是要学会放手部。那个秃头混蛋之所以更加危险，正是因为他懂得在谎言中掺入适量的真相，从而使这些谎言变得极具威胁性。 “那么，让我们把话题回到妮娜身上吧。她没有说错——这些信息确实很有价值，不过从你的表情来看，我敢肯定这些价值的含义并不像你预想的那样。 |你摇了摇头。普通的酒早就干掉了，更不用说会变酸变成醋了，但这种酒却完全不同。话虽如此，这里竟然有这些高档葡萄酒……从整个情况来看，你似乎并没有和Ryn的人待在一起太久。 太 虽然过程有些漫长，但你很确定，即便是对他们来说，冰酒也应该属于非常稀有的饮品，甚至可能是受到限制的吧？[pc.bg scholar acolyte | 当你看到这个标签时，还会注意到标签的下半部分，也就是酒的酿造日期，是用古老的贝尔哈兰语写成的——你肯定也能看懂这种语言。 做 偶尔会遇到一些词，这些词是你在过去读书时偶然读到的一些较为古老的文献中出现的。不过，仅仅凭一两个词，还是远远不够理解整个内容的…… ] 唉，想得太多了也没用。无论这里发生了什么，都已经成为过去，就连那些苍白精灵也早已将其忘得一干二净。你还有更重要的事情需要处理。 ] ] ]
rows.raw: " This must be it, then — a large crate sitting by the side of an ancient firepit, surrounded by the rotted and dessicate remains of an equally aged leather tarpaulin. The so-called super important thing that Nina would be so glad to get your hands on, in her own words, the prize that you picked your way over this treacherous hollowed-out cavern to acquire... You can't take it any more, your curiosity has to be sated. While the wood is in terrible condition and the brass bindings have gained a green patina, the crate still holds, and you push aside the lid to reveal rows upon rows of dusty green bottles sitting in the weighty container, caked with stone grit but otherwise unharmed. They'd once been packed with sawdust, but that's rotted away into a disgusting mulch, leaving dust that seeps through the base of the cate when you pick it up. Ugh! Booze, thirty bottles of it — even if the labels weren't as faded as they are, you have no way of understanding what presumably is the boreal elf language. But you've seen these before, in the palace of ice... elven ice wine, also known to Ryn's kin as mirrorwine. Yeah... you can see how this would be terribly important to Nina, and how glad she would be to get her hands on a load of this. [party.has etheryn |"Oh dear," Ryn says, stepping up and looking over your shoulder at your find. "That's more mirrorwine in one place than you'd find in the palace cellars, especially near the end of Alissa's reign. Do you mind if I take a look?" Sure, she can knock herself out. You move aside, and Ryn pulls out one of the ancient, finely made bottles, brushing aside fine stone grit and squinting at the label in the gloom. Well? "This one's really old. Well, all mirrorwine dates from before the Godswar and the ensuing schism, but this goes a good while even before that. If we assume that this mine was abandoned during the Godswar, then it'd have been considered quite the vintage at that point, and by our standards. Look here at the bottom, they're still using the old dating system... the grapes were pressed roughly a hundred and ten years before the Godswar." You shake your head. Ordinary wine would've long since dried out, let alone soured into vinegar, but this is something else altogether. That being said, the presence of bottles of fine wine here... "...Imply corruption in my great-grandmother's reign, yes. Despite what Hethia and her people say, the era before the Godswar wasn't one of supreme enlightenment and harmony until my grandmother ruined it all." Ryn sighs. "But back to the point. I only know this from the histories, but mirrorwine wasn't supposed to fall into hands that weren't boer'alvar. The need for isolation wasn't always there, and these were clearly packed for long-distance shipping." Was there some kind of religious stricture against selling ice wine to other peoples, or something along those lines? "No, but it was simple politeness, I think. The druids didn't actually get most of their money from donations — they had very good apiaries and wineries that produced excellent honey, mead, mirrorwine and more. But the thing is that the latter was supposed to be a gift from the druids to the boer'alvar as a people, which is why it was sold at cost as opposed to the other fruits of their art. To sell away that which was given to you in good faith and abuse that kindness... well, it's not just the boer'alvar who look down upon such a practice." Which brings you back to the here and now — it looks like at least some of these convict mining camps were used as forwarding spots for smuggling. Ryn sighs. "It's all in the past, [pc.name]. Important to know... but also just as important to let go. They weren't all as good as dead... some did manage to survive their sentences. "Let's bring this back to Nina, then. She wasn't wrong — this is really valuable, although from the look on your face I'm sure it's not valuable in the way you were expecting." |[party.has cait |"Ooooh," Cait says, stepping up and looking over your shoulder at your find. "That looks like the fancy wine that Ryn sometimes sets out at the palace. Mind if I take a look?" Sure, she can knock herself out. You move aside, and Cait pulls out one of the ancient, finely made bottles, brushing aside fine stone grit and squinting at the label in the gloom. Well, anything? "Wait a moment, I'm trying to recall what Dad told Calla and I while we were on the ship, trying to prepare us for what we might find up here in the Marches. Right... "This stuff's really old. Look, it's dated in the pre-Godswar Belharan system, and if I'm not wrong the date should come to about a hundred and ten years before everything happened." She can read pale elf? Presumably that's what the labels are in... "No, but I can read numbers. Which brings up the question of why exactly the pale elves would be using the imperial dating system — I'm not completely sure, but I don't think they did. The empire's influence stopped at the River Ridell, even if there were agreements between them and the pale elves like the one Ryn tried to claim with Carmen." Well, that would imply that trade wasn't impossible... on the other hand, you get the impression that elven ice wine is kind of rare, even amongst the pale elves. Certainly the kind of thing you didn't just export on a whim. "I don't know about that. To hear Ryn speak of it, things were better in her great-grandmother's time; we can't just assume that things were the same back then as they are today. Who knows, the pale elves might have had a booming wine export business. It's certainly something I'd have to ask Ryn about when I next see her." Certainly lucrative enough for what's ostensibly a convict mining camp to engage in a bit of corruption on the side. If the workers were in on it, the officials almost certainly were, too. "The past was a lot more civilized, I'm told," Cait says with a sigh. "But Dad always used to point out that if we thought corruption in the sultanate was bad, one can only imagine what it would've been like in a sprawling empire like Belhar's. We can only keep it down, not get rid of it altogether. It's all in the past, [pc.name]. Important to know... but also just as important to let go. "Come on, let's bring this back to your bird and see what she has to say for herself." |[party.has quintillus |"Hmm," Quin says, stepping up and looking over your shoulder at your find. "Even if it's this old, I know contraband when I see it. Do you mind if I take a closer look?" Sure, he can knock himself out. You move aside, and Quin pulls out one of the ancient, finely made bottles, brushing aside fine stone grit and squinting at the label in the gloom. Anything notable? "The way these were packed, I'd think they were meant to be moved out with the ore shipments. It's a sturdy crate that's survived a couple hundred years, I'm sure it would've held up to a bit of weight. Who wants to go to the trouble of moving aside a huge pile of rocks to search its guts?" Quin chuckles, then dusts off some grit from the label with a fingertip. "The label's written in whatever language these elves use and I can't read that, but oddly enough there's more on the bottom that's clearly been added later, in antiquated Belharan to boot. Look...the vintage's dated roughly a hundred and ten years before the Godswar. This is good stuff, if it hasn't soured already, and while I don't know much about the pale elves they damn well make things to last." [pc.bg scholar acolyte |Hey, he's actually right. Now that Quin's pointing it out to you, you do recognize a word here and there from when you'd stumbled across a couple of the more ancient texts in your bookish past. |You'll just take to take his word for it, then. As far as you're concerned, it's all the same to you. ] "Even though I never actually made the cut, everyone knows that fresh talons cut their teeth on small-timers like smugglers. I'd been hoping to... never mind. "My guess is that this entire mining outpost was crooked — you don't get all the convicts joining in on the business and the contraband being left out in the open without the approval of whatever officials were stationed here. They'd receive the goods from their friends in the forest, then hide the booze in the ore shipments... whichever way you take to the Winter City from here, north or south, you'll be running into water, be it the fjord or the river. After evading the outriders on the roads, this would've been loaded onto a ship and punted to Belhar. A bit of a leap, I'll admit, but that's my guess given my knowledge of how things work — I don't expect anything to have been different just because these people were elves." Ice wine to Belhar, though... that's a long way to go. The addendum to the label in Belharan, though, would confirm that it was intended for somewhere that spoke the language, at the very least. "It's a long way, but they certainly felt it was worth it." Quin sighs and rubs his temples. "Ever hear that fucker Tollus go on about the pleasures of the old imperium and how it was his destiny to recapture them? He wasn't lying about the first part — even a commoner in the imperial capital lived better than a king today. They weren't lacking in the least for wealth, but they damn well were lacking for entertainment. I suppose elven ice wine counts as a passable distraction, doesn't it?" You suppose it would, yeah. If the palace's any indication, the boreal elves have been drinking it for a long time and still have yet to get bored of the stuff. "Aah, that's all in the past, [pc.name]. Important to know... but also just as important to let go, that bald fucker is made all the more dangerous because he knows to blend just enough truth into his lies to make them dangerous. "Let's bring this back to Nina, then. She wasn't wrong — this is really valuable, although from the look on your face I'm sure it's not valuable in the way you were expecting." |You shake your head. Ordinary wine would've long since dried out, let alone soured into vinegar, but this is something else altogether. That being said, the presence of bottles of fine wine here... in the scheme of things, you haven't been with Ryn's people for too long, but you're pretty sure that ice wine's supposed to be pretty rare even for them, perhaps even restricted?[pc.bg scholar acolyte | When you look at the label, you also note that the bottom half, date of the vintage included, is written in antiquated Belharan — you do recognize a word here and there from when you'd stumbled across a couple of the more ancient texts in your bookish past. That being said, a word or two's still not enough to make sense of it all... ] Oh well, no good thinking too much about it. Whatever went on here, it's all in the past, a distant memory even for the pale elves. You have more pressing business to handle. ] ] ] "

rows.original: The trip back out through the mine is uneventful — you return over the sinkholes by the same means that you crossed in the first place — and you're once more in the open. There's nothing more left for you in here now...
rows.translation: 再次穿过矿井返回外界的过程十分顺利——你还是通过当初进入时使用的那些通道，穿过那些天坑，最终重新回到了开阔地带。现在，这里已经没有什么可以留你再待下去了……
rows.raw: "\n        The trip back out through the mine is uneventful — you return over the sinkholes by the same means that you crossed in the first place — and you're once more in the open. There's nothing more left for you in here now..."

rows.original: You set off along the trail, seeing where it'll take you. The pines of the Frostwood are thicker than the vegetation of the Old Forest, although the underbrush is thinner. There's a shift in the air as you press forward, hopefully not getting lost in this arboreal labyrinth...
rows.translation: 你沿着小径前行，不知道这条路会将你引向何方。霜木地的松树比旧森林里的植被更加茂密，不过灌木丛却相对稀疏一些。随着你不断前进，空气中的氛围似乎也发生了变化……希望你不会在这片由树木构成的迷宫中迷路……
rows.raw: "You set off along the trail, seeing where it'll take you. The pines of the Frostwood are thicker than the vegetation of the Old Forest, although the underbrush is thinner. There's a shift in the air as you press forward, hopefully not getting lost in this arboreal labyrinth..."

rows.original: While moving along the trail, you spot a new path that you could've sworn was never there before. It was as if the trees had moved aside to reveal a way forward... but that's not quite right, isn't it? Still, it's a new direction in which you could take yourself, and that's exactly what you're looking for...
rows.translation: 在沿着小路前进的过程中，你发现了一条全新的路径——你发誓这条路之前根本不存在。就好像那些树木主动让开了道路，为你指出了前行的方向……但这样讲似乎有点不太对吧？不过，这毕竟是一个新的方向，你可以选择沿着它前进，而这正是你所需要的……
rows.raw: "While moving along the trail, you spot a new path that you could've sworn was never there before. It was as if the trees had moved aside to reveal a way forward... but that's not quite right, isn't it? Still, it's a new direction in which you could take yourself, and that's exactly what you're looking for..."

rows.original: Meandering amongst the pines and over the underbrush, you come across a series of several crumbled walls, the white, black-streaked marble long since worn away with time. Elven make, it looks like — while anything this ruined building might have once held has long since rotted away with time, the ground within holds several stands of plants, some of which you recognize as being potentially useful. It's a simple matter to gather some for your own use, especially when they're growing so thickly together. [party.has etheryn |"The Boer'Alvar have been trying to cultivate winterstem for centuries," Ryn remarks with a rare smile as you busy yourself with picking. "That, amongst other useful herbs you see now. The efforts have had... mixed results. As you can see, it's a plant that by far prefers to grow wild rather than in captivity. We don't exactly know why, but we think it's got something to do the pines in the Frostwood and how they fix the soil with their roots." ] You found [a] [var0]!
rows.translation: 在松树林中蜿蜒穿行，穿过灌木丛，你发现了一排摇摇欲坠的墙壁——那些白色大理石上布满黑色条纹的材质，早已被时间侵蚀得面目全非。这些墙壁看起来像是精灵建造的……虽然这座早已毁坏的建筑里曾经存放的物品恐怕早已腐烂殆尽，但地面上却生长着几株植物，其中一些你认出它们可能具有实用价值。把这些植物采下来供自己使用其实是一件很容易的事，尤其是当它们长得如此茂盛的时候。 [party.has etheryn |几个世纪以来，布尔人阿尔瓦尔族一直在努力种植冬茎作物。 当你忙于挑选的时候，瑞恩难得地露出了微笑。 这就是你们现在看到的这些有用的草药之一。我们的尝试取得了……不同的结果。正如你们所见，这种植物显然更喜欢在野外生长，而不是在人工培育的环境中。我们并不完全清楚原因，但我们认为这与霜木地区的松树有关——那些松树是如何用它们的根系来改善土壤的。 ] 你找到了。 [a] [var0]!

We don't exactly know why, but we think it's got something to do the pines in the Frostwood and how they fix the soil with their roots." ] You found [a] [var0]!"

rows.original: Wandering through the thick woods, you come across the ivy-covered remains of a ruined marble archway. Adjoining it is a small walled compound, long since overrun with weeds and more importantly, several stands of wild vegetables. There's enough here that you could take a few without overtaxing the local flora — if anything, with how overgrown some of these are thinning the herd probably couldn't hurt any. You spend a few minutes picking out the choicest specimens, then prepare to be on your way. [party.has etheryn |"It was before my time or even Grandmother's, but it was something of a fad for our nobility to play peasant, as they called it," Ryn remarks as she sits on a low wall and watches you work. "Those highborn who were simply too caught up in luxury and ennui — third and fourth sons and daughters who simply weren't involved in court at all — would dress down and play at farming, knowing full well that if things got too hard, they could quit any moment and return to their lives of comfort. That... well, people put a stop to that pretty quickly, in about three hundred years or so. It wasn't the best of times for anyone." ] You found [an] [var0]!
rows.translation: 在茂密的树林中漫步时，你偶然发现了一座被常春藤覆盖的、已经毁坏的大理石拱门遗迹。它的旁边是一个有围墙的小院，那里早已长满了杂草，更重要的是，还长了几株野生蔬菜。这里的蔬菜数量足够多，你可以摘一些带走，而不会对当地的植物资源造成破坏——事实上，由于有些蔬菜已经长得过于茂盛，采摘一些反而有助于控制它们的数量。你花了几分钟时间挑选了一些最新鲜的蔬菜，然后准备继续前进。 [party.has etheryn |那发生在我的时代之前，甚至也是我祖母的时代之前，但对我们贵族来说，扮演农民——他们就是这么称呼这种行为的——曾经算是一种流行风尚。 瑞恩坐在一堵矮墙上，看着你工作，说道。 那些沉溺于奢华与无聊的贵族子弟——那些根本不会参与宫廷事务的第三子、第四子们——会穿上便装去模拟农耕生活，但他们心里很清楚，只要情况变得太艰难，他们随时都可以停止这种游戏，重新回到舒适的生活之中。不过……嗯，大约在三百年后，人们很快就制止了这种行为。对任何人来说，那都不是一个美好的时代。 ] 你找到了。 [an] [var0]!

That... well, people put a stop to that pretty quickly, in about three hundred years or so. It wasn't the best of times for anyone." ] You found [an] [var0]!"

rows.original: The Frostwood feels even more claustrophobic than usual in the dead of night, barely the tiniest slivers of starlight managing to pierce the canopy in order to light your way forward. Off to one side of the trail, you hear a sudden laugh — and another, and yet another. From that direction, a procession of flickering blue flames emerge from the trees, crossing your path lengthwise in the distance — one, two, three, more — bobbing up and down in the air before vanishing again. [pc.ra kitsune |Of course, you know exactly what this is, and despite their strangely hypnotic movements, the wisps of foxfire are nothing to you other than pretty lights conjured up by children on the prowl. You vaguely wonder if they'll be successful on their hunt for benefactors out in the woods... |[party.has kiyoko |"Oh dear," your fox-wife remarks dryly with a small smile. "Children out at play again, looking for benefactors to lure in. Don't worry, they'll give you no trouble so long as I'm with you. That is, unless you're looking for it..." |The display was as mesmerising as it was unexpected, and you can't help but shake your head and gather your wits once more as you try to figure out what you've been doing for the last few seconds. Perhaps it's best not to wonder... ] ]
rows.translation: 在深夜，冰原森林显得比平时更加令人窒息。几乎没有任何星轻型能够穿透茂密的树冠，为你照亮前行的道路。在小路的某一侧，你突然听到了笑声——一个，又一个。从那个方向，一串串闪烁的蓝色火焰从树林中浮现出来，沿着小路的方向缓缓移动——一团，两团，三团……这些火焰在空气中上下跳动，然后又消失得无影无踪。 [pc.ra kitsune |你当然知道这到底是什么。尽管那些狐火呈现出一种奇异的、令人着迷的动态，但在你看来，它们只不过是孩子们在森林里制造出来的漂亮灯光罢了。你不禁暗自怀疑，那些在森林里寻找赞助者的孩子们，是否真的能够成功…… |[party.has kiyoko |哦，天哪。 你那位狐狸般的妻子带着一丝微笑，淡淡地说道。 孩子们又出去玩耍了，正在寻找愿意帮助他们的人。别担心，只要我在你身边，他们不会给你带来任何麻烦的……当然，除非你主动招惹他们…… |这种视觉效果既令人着迷，又完全出乎意料。你不禁会摇摇头，重新集中注意力，试图弄清楚自己在过去几秒钟里到底做了什么。或许，最好不要去想这些…… ] ]

Off to one side of the trail, you hear a sudden laugh — and another, and yet another. [pc.ra kitsune |Of course, you know exactly what this is, and despite their strangely hypnotic movements, the wisps of foxfire are nothing to you other than pretty lights conjured up by children on the prowl. You vaguely wonder if they'll be successful on their hunt for benefactors out in the woods... |[party.has kiyoko |"Oh dear," your fox-wife remarks dryly with a small smile. That is, unless you're looking for it..." |The display was as mesmerising as it was unexpected, and you can't help but shake your head and gather your wits once more as you try to figure out what you've been doing for the last few seconds. Perhaps it's best not to wonder... ] ]"

rows.original: Taking a sharp turn around a large pine as thick as a small hut, you run face-first into several strands of old webbing. Thankfully, they've long since dried out and are no longer sticky, but given the thickness of these strands and the web they must've once belonged to, the spider that spun these must have been person-sized — or more. That only raises the question as to what kind of prey the trapper in question was hoping to snare... it might be best to move on before too long.
rows.translation: 当你绕过一棵粗壮如小屋般的松树急转弯时，突然迎面碰上了几缕干枯的蛛网。幸运的是，这些蛛网早已干透，不再具有粘性，但考虑到这些蛛网的厚度以及它们所属的蜘蛛体型，想必那只蜘蛛的体型应该有人的大小——甚至更大。这就让人不禁好奇：制造这些蛛网的蜘蛛究竟想捕捉什么样的猎物……或许，最好尽快离开这里。
rows.raw: "\n    Taking a sharp turn around a large pine as thick as a small hut, you run face-first into several strands of old webbing. Thankfully, they've long since dried out and are no longer sticky, but given the thickness of these strands and the web they must've once belonged to, the spider that spun these must have been person-sized — or more. That only raises the question as to what kind of prey the trapper in question was hoping to snare... it might be best to move on before too long."

rows.original: Shuffling along the forest trail, you don't see it until it's too late — a mass of thorny, woody vines laid out across the forest trail in a sprawl, its mossy brown-green blending in with the fallen pine needles without a hitch. [ var0 |Thankfully, your reflexes are on point and you jump back at the first sharp prick, avoiding further trouble with the menacing-looking vegetation. Now that you know they're there, clearing them out with your [pc.weapon] is a simple matter, but you could've been in some trouble there if you'd just gone wading in. | By the time you feel the first prick of pain as the thorns catch onto your clothes and dig into your skin, you're already in deep enough that getting out without hurting yourself is a dim prospect. You beat back the tangled vines with your [pc.weapon] in a bid to extricate yourself from the situation, but don't manage to get out without several scrapes from the vicious vegetation. ] [party.has etheryn |"Where barriers and walls were needed in these parts, we'd use tanglevine to form natural walls to surround our homes with. The druids would shape them as we needed..." Ryn muses as she helps you clear the path forward. "Though now that they've fallen out of favor, the hedges have long since gone feral, to put it lightly. It's a pity." |Come to think of it, these thorny vines are quite similar to what Evergreen used to seal off the road leading into the Frostwood... ]
rows.translation: 当你沿着森林小径前行时，往往直到为时已晚才会注意到它——一大片布满尖刺的木质藤蔓横亘在小径上，它们那苔藓覆盖的棕绿色与掉落的松针完美地融为一体，让人难以察觉。 [ var0 |幸运的是，你的反应速度非常快，在感觉到第一阵刺痛时立刻跳了回去，从而避免了那些看起来十分危险的植物带来的进一步麻烦。现在既然你知道它们在那里了，就用你的工具把它们清除掉吧。 [pc.weapon] 这本来是一件很简单的事情，但如果你贸然插手的话，可能会惹上一些麻烦。 | 当那些荆棘钩住你的衣服、刺入你的皮肤，让你感到第一阵疼痛时，你已经陷得足够深了，要想不受伤地脱身出来，几乎是不可能的。你用尽全力拨开那些缠绕在一起的藤蔓 [pc.weapon] 为了摆脱这种困境，他试图脱身，但却在那些凶猛的植物中受了些伤，才终于得以脱身。 ] [party.has etheryn |在这些地方需要设置屏障和围墙时，我们会利用藤蔓来构筑天然的围墙，将我们的住所围起来。德鲁伊们会根据我们的需求来塑造这些藤蔓…… 当瑞恩帮助你清除前方的障碍时，她陷入了沉思。 虽然现在它们已经不再受欢迎了，但那些树篱早就变得杂乱无章了，说得轻一点就是如此。真是可惜。 |仔细想来，这些带刺的藤蔓与常青女士曾经用来封锁通往寒冰森林的道路的东西颇为相似…… ]

rows.original: You're standing outside the northern gates of the ruined wayfort, the unbreakable shield that once defended the realm of the boreal elves against the Belharan Empire. It's long since started to crumble, borne down by the weight of its neglect. A long, dirt road leads northwards from the fort into the dense depths of the Frostwood. You can still make out bits of cobble and brickwork, indicating that long ago, this road might have been paved and well-maintained, but it's difficult to imagine what that looked like.
rows.translation: 你站在这座废弃要塞的北门之外，那面曾经守护着极北精灵王国、抵御贝尔哈兰帝国的坚不可摧的盾牌，如今早已开始崩塌，沦为无人照料下的废墟。一条尘土飞扬的道路从要塞向北延伸，通向幽暗的寒冰森林深处。路上还能依稀看到一些鹅卵石和砖块的痕迹，这说明很久以前，这条道路或许曾经被铺设得整整齐齐、维护得很好，但如今已很难想象它当初的样子了。
rows.raw: "\n    You're standing outside the northern gates of the ruined wayfort, the unbreakable shield that once defended the realm of the boreal elves against the Belharan Empire. It's long since started to crumble, borne down by the weight of its neglect. A long, dirt road leads northwards from the fort into the dense depths of the Frostwood. You can still make out bits of cobble and brickwork, indicating that long ago, this road might have been paved and well-maintained, but it's difficult to imagine what that looked like."

rows.translation: 进入 [flags.WC_CLEAR|荒废驿堡|腐坏的花园]
进入 [flags.WC_CLEAR|荒废驿堡|腐坏的花园].

rows.original: [flags.EVERGREEN_MET |Lady Evergreen's manor sits in the heart of a small clearing at the end of a well-tended path. A large redwood arch covered in thick ropes and lanterns separates the Witch of the Woods' domain from the rest of the Frostwood. A lush garden flanks the path leading up to her door, in full bloom and ripe with produce despite the unnatural cold of the northernmost reaches. Branches overhang the arched roof, covered with the same thin gloss of frost and snow as the rest of the forest. The house has actual glass windows along its upper floors, and you can see lights glowing from inside through thick curtains. It seems the witch, or at least some of her daughters, are home. |You've passed beneath the strange redwood arch on the path, which has wound its way through the woods towards a small clearing. Somebody's built a rather large stone house here, what you'd probably call a manor if it sat on a proper plot of land — but aside from a rather large garden flanking the path up to the solid wood door, the forest seems to end mere feet from the house itself. Branches overhang the arched roof, covered with the same thin gloss of frost and snow as the rest of the forest. The house has actual glass windows along its upper floors, and you can see lights glowing from inside through thick curtains. Someone definitely lives here... There's a brass knocker shaped like the tail of a raccoon affixed to the door, practically daring you to come and call on whatever strange folk must live in this secluded estate. [party.has cait|"I... I think this is the place," Cait murmurs, glancing around in awe. "This must be where that witch lives. Please, [pc.name]... can we spare the time to speak with her? For my sake, if not for Calla's."] ]
rows.translation: [flags.EVERGREEN_MET |常青女士的庄园坐落在一片小空地的中央，那条被精心维护的小路尽头便是这里。一道由粗绳和灯笼装饰而成的巨大红木拱门将这位森林女巫的领地与弗罗斯特伍德的其余区域分隔开来。 一条小路通向她的家门，路的两旁是一片繁茂的花园。尽管地处最北端，气候异常寒冷，但这里的花朵依然盛开，各种果实也都已经成熟。树枝垂落在拱形的屋檐上，上面覆盖着与森林其他地方一样的薄薄一层霜雪。 这座房子的上层楼层确实装有玻璃窗，透过厚厚的窗帘，你可以看到里面的灯光正在闪烁。 看来那位女巫，或者至少是她的一些女儿们，现在在家。 |你沿着小路穿过了那道奇特的红木拱门，这条小路蜿蜒穿过树林，最终通向一片小空地。有人在这里建造了一座相当大的石屋——如果它建在一片合适的土地上，你可能会称它为庄园。不过，除了小路两侧有一片面积不小的花园，以及通往那扇实木大门的道路外，森林似乎在离房子仅几英尺的地方就结束了。 树枝垂挂在拱形的屋顶上，上面覆盖着与森林其他部分一样的薄薄一层霜雪。这座房子的上层楼层装有真正的玻璃窗，透过厚厚的窗帘，可以看到里面透出的灯光。 肯定有人住在这里。门上装着一个形状像浣熊尾巴的黄铜门环，仿佛在挑衅人们去探访这个与世隔绝的宅子里究竟住着些什么奇怪的人。 [party.has cait|我……我觉得就是这里了，”凯特轻声说道，敬畏地环顾四周，“这里肯定就是那个女巫居住的地方。求你了…… [pc.name]……我们能不能抽时间和她谈谈呢？就算不是为了卡拉，也请为了我考虑一下吧。] ]
rows.raw: " [flags.EVERGREEN_MET |Lady Evergreen's manor sits in the heart of a small clearing at the end of a well-tended path. A large redwood arch covered in thick ropes and lanterns separates the Witch of the Woods' domain from the rest of the Frostwood. A lush garden flanks the path leading up to her door, in full bloom and ripe with produce despite the unnatural cold of the northernmost reaches. Branches overhang the arched roof, covered with the same thin gloss of frost and snow as the rest of the forest. The house has actual glass windows along its upper floors, and you can see lights glowing from inside through thick curtains. It seems the witch, or at least some of her daughters, are home. |You've passed beneath the strange redwood arch on the path, which has wound its way through the woods towards a small clearing. Somebody's built a rather large stone house here, what you'd probably call a manor if it sat on a proper plot of land — but aside from a rather large garden flanking the path up to the solid wood door, the forest seems to end mere feet from the house itself. Branches overhang the arched roof, covered with the same thin gloss of frost and snow as the rest of the forest. The house has actual glass windows along its upper floors, and you can see lights glowing from inside through thick curtains. Someone definitely lives here... There's a brass knocker shaped like the tail of a raccoon affixed to the door, practically daring you to come and call on whatever strange folk must live in this secluded estate. [party.has cait|"I... I think this is the place," Cait murmurs, glancing around in awe. "This must be where that witch lives. Please, [pc.name]... can we spare the time to speak with her? For my sake, if not for Calla's."] ]"

rows.original:
This massive tree stands tall above the rest of the Frostwood, towering far above the canopy with its branches stretching outwards in every direction. With roots that are as thick as you are tall, the growth of this thing has been very clearly influenced or directed in some fashion — even the elven druids' wyld trees of old didn't get to these obscenely gargantuan proportions. To be quite honest, it feels more like a living artifact than a mere plant, if you could put such a sensation into words. A circle of empty space rings the tree itself, as if it's holding back the rest of the forest by sheer dint of its presence, a foreign entity in this land.

    No matter the time of year, the tree is eternally in bloom, pink petals coming loose in the northern wind and spralling away to the ground, sprinkling their beauty over the trim grasses. Ah, with ever aching heart, the blossoms are falling — a rather picturesque scene, if the entire thing had been of more normal proportions.
    
    [var0
        |As things stand, you spy an entrance nested in the fork of two roots, about as tall and wide as the chapel entryway back in Hawkethorne. At the moment, [
            var2
            |it's been closed. You should return to Evergreen with the bag Komari gave you.
            |it's been thrown wide open, as if someone knew you were coming and sought to invite you in. Waltzing right on up's an option, if a rather brazen one.
        ]
        |[var1
            |[pc.ra kitsune
                |The tree sings to something deep within you. Even with your eyes closed and ears bound, you know you could find the entrance to the den unerringly. All you'd need to do is concentrate for a bit... 
                |Since you know where the entrance to the kitsune den is located, you can just waltz on in. After all, you've received permission to visit, even if you are a foreigner to them.
            ]
            |As things stand, you spy an entrance nested in the fork of two roots, about as tall and wide as the chapel entryway back in Hawkethorne. However, it's been sealed tightly shut. With no obvious way to open it, you can only assume that mundane means aren't going to get you entry. At any rate, you're clearly not welcome here.
        ]
    ]
rows.translation:
这棵巨大的树木在霜木丛中高耸入云，它的树枝向四面八方伸展开来，远远超过了其他树木的高度。它的树根粗壮得与你的身高相当，由此可见，它的生长必定受到了某种外力的影响或引导——就连古代精灵德鲁伊所培育的那些野生巨树，也从未达到如此庞大的规模。 说实话，如果可以用语言来形容这种感觉的话，它更像是一件有生命的艺术品，而不仅仅是一株植物。围绕着这棵树，有一片空荡荡的空间，仿佛是它的存在本身就在阻挡着周围的其他树木，让它成为这片土地上一个与众不同的存在。

    无论是一年中的什么季节，这棵树总是鲜花盛开，粉红色的花瓣在北风的吹拂下纷纷飘落，散落在修剪整齐的草地上，为这片景色增添了一抹美丽。啊，每当看到这些花瓣飘落，心中总会感到一阵酸涩——倘若这一切的比例能够更加协调一些，那该是多么一幅如画的美景啊。
    
    [var0
        |目前来看，你看到一个入口隐藏在两根树根的分叉处，它的高度和宽度与鹰棘镇镇上那座小教堂的入口差不多。此刻， [
            var2
            |它已经关闭了。你应该带着小毬给你的那个包回到常青女士。
            |门已经大敞着，仿佛有人早就知道你会来，特意邀请你进去。直接走过去也是一个选择，只不过这个做法有点太冒失了。
        ]
        |[var1
            |[pc.ra kitsune
                |那棵树仿佛在向你内心深处诉说着什么。即使你闭着眼睛、捂着耳朵，你也知道自己一定能找到那个入口。你所需要的，只是稍微集中一下注意力而已…… 
                |既然你知道狐狸洞的入口在哪里，那就直接进去吧。毕竟，即使你对它们来说是个外人，你也已经得到了进入的许可。
            ]
            |目前的情况是，你看到一个入口隐藏在两根树枝的交汇处，它的高度和宽度与鹰棘镇小镇上那座小教堂的入口差不多。然而，这个入口被紧紧地封住了。由于没有明显的开启方法，你只能认为，普通的手段是无法打开它的。无论如何，很明显，这里并不欢迎你的到来。
        ]
    ]

rows.original: The entrance is closed. You need to return to Evergreen.
rows.translation: 入口已经关闭。您需要返回常青女士之地。
rows.raw: "The entrance is closed. You need to return to Evergreen."

rows.original: There's a branch in the old road here. In the distance to the south you can make out the shadowy shapes of the Wayfort's towers, and in the north, your view is dominated by frost-crusted evergreen trees and thick grass... but there's another way to the east, a narrow footpath through the bramble that's been much better maintained than anything around it all the way back to the gates themselves. [var0 |The canopy of thorns has wilted here, creating just enough of a gap for you to pass through unharmed. |There is a great canopy of thorny vines stretching across the northern pass, seeming to stretch beyond line of sight into the cold forest. There's no way to progress beyond here. [party.has etheryn|"That... wasn't here when I came down," Etheryn mumbles, walking up and examining the vines. "I wonder..."] ] You can see a pair of lit lanterns a short ways to the east, hanging from a large wooden arch covered with thick cords of rope that hang over the trail...
rows.translation: 这条老路上有一条小岔路。向南望去，你可以隐约看到荒废驿堡家族的塔楼轮廓；而向北望去，视野中尽是被霜冻覆盖的常绿树木和茂密的草地……不过，在东边还有另一条路——一条穿过灌木丛的狭窄小径，这条小径维护得非常好，一直延伸到大门所在的地方。 [var0 |这里的荆棘丛已经枯萎了，因此留出了足够的空间让你可以安全地穿过。 |一片茂密的带刺藤蔓覆盖了北面的山口，那些藤蔓似乎一直延伸到视线之外的寒冷森林中。从这里往北，根本无法继续前进。 [party.has etheryn|我下来的时候，这里并没有这个……”伊瑟琳喃喃道，走过去仔细检查那些藤蔓。“我在想……] ] 在东边不远处，你可以看到一对亮着的灯笼，它们悬挂在一座巨大的木制拱门上，那些粗厚的绳索从拱门上垂下来，横跨在小路上……
rows.raw: " There's a branch in the old road here. In the distance to the south you can make out the shadowy shapes of the Wayfort's towers, and in the north, your view is dominated by frost-crusted evergreen trees and thick grass... but there's another way to the east, a narrow footpath through the bramble that's been much better maintained than anything around it all the way back to the gates themselves. [var0 |The canopy of thorns has wilted here, creating just enough of a gap for you to pass through unharmed. |There is a great canopy of thorny vines stretching across the northern pass, seeming to stretch beyond line of sight into the cold forest. There's no way to progress beyond here. [party.has etheryn|"That... wasn't here when I came down," Etheryn mumbles, walking up and examining the vines. "I wonder..."] ] You can see a pair of lit lanterns a short ways to the east, hanging from a large wooden arch covered with thick cords of rope that hang over the trail..."

rows.original:
Before you is a towering hill, covered in craggy stone and thick moss. The snow that's otherwise ever-present in the Frostwood succeeds from the hill as if by magic, forming an almost perfectly circular line fifty feet from the start of the rise. A number of particularly large and ancient-seeming trees grow roots in the soil on the hillside, though their trunks seem blackened in places as if ravaged by fire. 
    
    There is a cave entrance not far from where you stand, clearly man-made. Large oblong stones stand in two rows leading away from the entrance, like primitive arches. They're all covered with strange red symbols, and while you cannot decipher the language, you can clearly see pictograms that can only possibly represent fire repeated several times on each.
    
    [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE_EN
        |
        |[party.has etheryn
            |"T-this is... the Temple of Terrestrial Fire," Etheryn breathes. "Even before the bridge fell, most boreal elves had forgotten about this place. Our — my — ancestors thought the earthfire would keep the frost from consuming our hearts. It didn't."
        ]
        
        [party.has cait
            |"Strange markings on those pillars," Cait murmurs to herself. She fishes through her bag until she finds a scrap of parchment and charcoal, and sets about taking rubbings of one. "Dad would love to see this. He thinks the druidic faiths of the elves are so fascinating..."
            
            [party.has etheryn
                |"H-hey, you could just... just ask me..." Ryn whines, ears drooping as the catgirl trots past her towards more interesting scholarship.
            ]
            
            [party.has atugia
                |"I can help! That one over there is about... Burning to death to sate the eternal flame!" Her excitement fades to a frown as she furrows her brow. "B-but the one you're inscribing now is about tamin' the fire inside to make it work for you. A bit less fatal."
            ]
        ]
    ]
rows.translation:
你面前有一座高耸的小山，山上布满了崎岖的岩石和茂密的苔藓。在霜木之地，雪本来是随处可见的，但在这座小山上，雪却仿佛被施了魔法一般，从山足部开始，形成了一条几乎完美的圆形雪线，这条雪线距离山足部有五十英尺远。 在山坡上的土壤中，生长着一些特别高大、看起来极为古老的树木，不过它们的树干在某些地方似乎被烧焦了，仿佛遭受过火灾的侵袭。

在你站立的地方不远处，有一个洞穴入口，很明显这是人工开凿的。 两排巨大的长方形石块排列在入口两侧，仿佛是原始时期的拱门。这些石块上全都刻着奇怪的红色符号，虽然我们无法解读这些符号所代表的语言，但可以清楚地看到其中反复出现的图案——显然，这些图案象征着火。
    
    [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE_EN
        |
        |[party.has etheryn
            |这……这是地火神殿，”伊瑟琳轻声说道，“即使在桥梁坍塌之前，大多数北方精灵也已经忘记了这个地方。我们的祖先认为，地火能够阻止寒霜侵蚀我们的心灵，但事实并非如此。
        ]
        
        [party.has cait
            |那些柱子上有奇怪的痕迹，”凯特自言自语道。她翻找着包，终于找到了一张羊皮纸和木炭，便开始仔细地描摹其中的一个痕迹。“爸爸一定会喜欢这个的。他一直觉得精灵们的德鲁伊信仰非常有趣
            
            [party.has etheryn
                |喂，你完全可以……直接问我啊……”莱恩哀怨地说道，那只猫娘大步流星地从她身边走过，朝着那些更吸引人的奖学金走去，她的耳朵都耷拉了下来。
            ]
            
            [party.has atugia
                |我可以帮忙！那边的那个故事是关于……为了熄灭永恒之火而付出生命的代价！”她的兴奋瞬间消失了，取而代之的是一脸困惑。“但是你现在正在讲述的这个故事，却是关于如何控制内心的火焰，让它为你所用……这样就不会那么致命了。
            ]
        ]
    ]

rows.original: Enter the [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE|Temple of Terrestrial Fire|weird fire temple].
rows.translation: 输入 [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE|地火神殿|奇怪的火神庙].
rows.raw: "Enter the [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE|Temple of Terrestrial Fire|weird fire temple]."

rows.original: Start looking around the scene of the king's fatal injury so many decades ago. You're probably not going to find anything, but that's not why you're truly out here, right?
rows.translation: 开始仔细观察那些发生在几十年前、导致国王致命受伤的场景吧。你很可能什么也找不到，但你也并不是为了这个目的才来到这里的，对吧？
rows.raw: "Start looking around the scene of the king's fatal injury so many decades ago. You're probably not going to find anything, but that's not why you're truly out here, right?"

rows.original:
The wind blows cold here. 

    You're at the bottom of a rocky, snow covered cliff face. Ice and compacted snow occasionally falls from the cliff and surrounding trees, thumping onto the ground below. There's a cave nearby, it's large entrance casting a visible fire-light glow outward. If your memory serves, it's the cave that belongs to that giantess half-lupine you met before... maybe she's home.
rows.translation:
这里的风很冷。

你此刻正处于一片布满岩石、被积雪覆盖的悬崖下装。偶尔会有冰块和压实的雪从悬崖上以及周围的树木上掉落，重重砸在下面的地面上。附近有一处洞穴，它那宽敞的入口处散发着明显的火轻型。如果你没有记错的话，这应该就是你之前遇到的那个半狼族巨女居住的洞穴……也许她现在就在家里。
rows.raw:
"
    The wind blows cold here. 

    You're at the bottom of a rocky, snow covered cliff face. Ice and compacted snow occasionally falls from the cliff and surrounding trees, thumping onto the ground below. There's a cave nearby, it's large entrance casting a visible fire-light glow outward. If your memory serves, it's the cave that belongs to that giantess half-lupine you met before... maybe she's home."

rows.original: See if the big puppy is around.
rows.translation: 看看那只大小狗在不在附近。
rows.raw: "See if the big puppy is around."

rows.original: Go through the Gates of Winter and enter the Winter City.
rows.translation: 穿过冬之大门，进入冬城吧。
rows.raw: "Go through the Gates of Winter and enter the Winter City."

rows.original: See if there's anything to Nina's vision, or if she's just crazy. Or maybe both.
rows.translation: 看看尼娜的预感是否有根据，还是她只是疯了。又或者两者都是真的。
rows.raw: "See if there's anything to Nina's vision, or if she's just crazy. Or maybe both."

rows.original: You still aren't done with retrieving whatever it is that Nina wanted from this mine. Head back in.
rows.translation: 你还没有完成从这座矿井中取出妮娜想要的东西吧？快回去继续找吧。
rows.raw: "You still aren't done with retrieving whatever it is that Nina wanted from this mine. Head back in."

rows.original: You pick through the dense nettles and thornbriars, shuffling along the forest trail at a snail's pace. With how isolated this place is, you wonder when the last time anyone's ever been out this way. Overlooking the fjords in the east is about all it has going for it, and even then, the view's marred by thick copses of evergreen trees. And then you trip over something while you're distracted by the view. Plap! You pick yourself up out of the snow and check yourself over, picking nettles out of your [pc.armor]. No harm done, looks like. But what the hell is catching your foot? [party.compPara cait etheryn viv |"Buried treasure!" Cait gasps. |"W-what is... is that metal?" Ryn gasps. |"I sense magic," Viv says. "Not potent, but magic all the same." ] You pull something out of the snow, a thin wooden box latched with brass and sealed with wax. It's only a couple of inches across and deep, but long enough to fit a forearm in there... a scroll case? Buried out here in the middle of nowhere? "Maybe the storm unearthed it," you mutter. You acquired a Druidic Scrollcase.

rows.raw: ' You pick through the dense nettles and thornbriars, shuffling along the forest trail at a snail's pace. With how isolated this place is, you wonder when the last time anyone's ever been out this way. Overlooking the fjords in the east is about all it has going for it, and even then, the view's marred by thick copses of evergreen trees. And then you trip over something while you're distracted by the view. Plap! You pick yourself up out of the snow and check yourself over, picking nettles out of your [pc.armor]. No harm done, looks like. But what the hell is catching your foot? [party.compPara cait etheryn viv |"Buried treasure!" Cait gasps. |"W-what is... is that metal?" Ryn gasps. |"I sense magic," Viv says. "Not potent, but magic all the same." ] You pull something out of the snow, a thin wooden box latched with brass and sealed with wax. It's only a couple of inches across and deep, but long enough to fit a forearm in there... a scroll case? Buried out here in the middle of nowhere? "Maybe the storm unearthed it," you mutter. You acquired a Druidic Scrollcase. '

"Another ice rose. Always nice to see a bit of home out here. It's a good thing that the ones in the gardens are pretty easy to keep alive; despite the thorns, they don't handle the wild as well as winterstem does." Maybe their soil requirements aren't as strict. They're probably more susceptible to other problems, though. Sunlight, possibly, or climate? "I think that that's right, but don't forget blights. You wouldn't think of them being a problem for an icy thing like this, but from what the gardeners tell me, a blight will ruin rosebushes faster than anything else." It's a shame that something so pretty can be ruined so easily. "Yeah."[etheryn.highConfidence | Your elven companion sighs, but perks up again pretty quickly. rows.original: Cautiously avoiding the icy thorns, you carefully take hold of the flower and pick it off the stem. Hopefully it survives the journey in your pack — you'd hate to see the pretty thing squashed before you can make use of it!

rows.original: "Oh, hi! It's you again!" The all-too familiar tittering voice of the tanuki witch rings amongst the trees as she steps out onto the trail and into view. "I just met a bunch of big, manly leothrans and had some fun with them! You should watch out, they're all over this neck of the woods! Could do something awful to you if you're not prepared!" Right. Does that mean that she's not going to do something awful to you, too? Any chance she might actually leave you alone this time around?

rows.original: "Hmm... I guess I can give it a rest if you're not feeling very frisky." The witch doesn't look too pleased by the prospect, her little round ears curling downwards atop her head, but she's able to resign herself to the situation. "You haven't got any family jewels I can coax out of you right now, so I guess I can turn a blind eye and hope that another bunch of leothran studs pass through real soon." She really is willing to let you just walk on by without a fight? "I don't like it — what's the point of having all this junk if you're not willing to use it? Still, you've got nothing that my sisters or I want, so I guess I can just look the other way if you're not going to be enthusiastic about it. It's not as much fun if you're just going to try and beat me off all the while." Looks like you're really getting a free pass here, and you'd better make up your mind before the tanuki-girl witch changes hers. Do you want to just head off and leave her be, or are you going to entertain her?

rows.original: You shrug and tell the tanuki temptress that you're not particularly interested in fighting her right now. The Frostwood is dangerous, a fact well-known to her mother and sisters, and you'd rather save your strength for more pressing encounters rather than waste it fucking around. "Weeeell, I guess." The witch folds her arms under her pert chest. "Wouldn't have made the offer if I didn't mean to follow through, I suppose. But if I ever happen to bump into you while you're packing any kind of meat, don't expect me to just turn a blind eye!" With a petulant sniff and swish of her skirts, she's gone, disappearing back into the shadow of the woods from which she emerged. You linger for a bit, wondering if she's going to double-back on you, but after half a minute or so it looks like she's really gone. Best to keep moving, then.

rows.original: Oh, fine. Even if you don't have anything she might want, you'll entertain her for a bit. Maybe Evergreen will appreciate you keeping one of her daughters out of trouble... by introducing her to a small measure of controlled trouble. Guess that's how these things work. The witch's face brightens, her little round ears perking up on her head as she starts to move in rhythm, lusty energies pouring into the air surrounding her person. "Hee, thanks! rows.raw: ' To witness someone stepping out so gracefully from around a tree pounds a spike of adrenaline and fear from your neck to your gut. [party.Yall] leap back, but it's only Kura, the black-haired kitsune tasked with watching over the woods. "[pc.name]," she murmurs, eyes roving across your body, focusing on your [pc.tails], your [pc.ears]... and your eyes. In an uncharacteristic hurry she bounds forward and kneels down, pressing her head to the soil. What's the big idea...? "[pc.name]... you've become a kitsune," she answers, sitting up. "My position on the social strata is not so low that I do not comprehend the blessing you've received. One cannot become like us on a whim, which says to me that you have received Keros' divine favor. Of the few stories of home I have ever paid attention to, it is his life and how he created us that is fresh in my mind." You tell her to stand, and she obeys without question. Her expression towards you speaks of greater reverence, lacking all of that mischief she showed to your previous form. "You simply honor me with your presence, [pc.name]. And... going forward... if you deign to return to these woods, I place myself at your disposal. Whether you wish for it or not, the understanding we had between us has transformed into a hierarchy. You are a chosen champion, and I am merely a handservant in your shadow." That's a rather ignominious change in behavior... "But it is our way," she replies. "There will be those who will look..." She pauses thoughtfully, tilting her head. "...Unfavorably on you as a foreigner whom has received this great honor, but not I. I am more than happy to serve your immediate needs, as long as you understand that my true mistress remains [silly|Ishida-dono|Mistress Azami]. Of course, given your station as our divine lord's handpicked champion, you outrank her, too... but nevertheless, she is my direct superior." Even if you wanted to take her somewhere, you're not about to force her to leave her life behind. For now, you accept this change. It's not like you intend to treat her much differently. "Consent to my whims, and I'll not hinder you... for a time. But if I require sustenance and I see you again, well... then I'll have to make this ultimatum again.
